News.title: Meet Navi Pillay: The former UN human rights chief awarded the Nobel Peace Prize
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay, a South African-born jurist, has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

The former UN human rights chief currently serves as an ad hoc judge at the International Court of Justice, the highest court of the United Nations, in the ongoing genocide case against Myanmar.

Making the announcement in Oslo, Norway, Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee, said Pillay’s work “is a source of hope and inspiration to all those who seek to bring about a more peaceful world”.

Her win is expected to be seen as a high-profile rebuke to US president Donald Trump and Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, both of whom have rejected the findings of a UN commission she led that Israel committed genocide in Gaza. Both leaders also have been highly critical of the institutions where Pillay has worked.

While her work has been global in scope, criticism often has been fiercely local, notably in places like Israel and in apartheid-era South Africa, as she and peers took on some of the world’s most painful and sensitive legal issues and most vulnerable populations.

open image in gallery Chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee Jorgen Watne Frydnes shows a photo of Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay ( Reuters )

Pillay, 85, received the news while attending the Nuremberg Forum, a gathering to discuss international law in Nuremberg, Germany, the location of the trials of Nazi war criminals that helped lay the foundations of international law.

“Firstly, at this venue, your applause means a great deal to me,” she said to a standing ovation.

“You know, you don’t want to receive an award, prize or anything unless the public agrees that you deserve this.”

And joking, she added: "But being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this information.”

Born in Durban, in South Africa's Natal province, Pillay served as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014.

In 1967, she became the first woman to start a law practice in Natal and the first non-white woman to serve on South Africa's High Court.

She is the fifth South African national to win the Nobel Peace Prize, after Nelson Mandela and FW de Klerk, Archbishop Desmond Tutu and Albert Luthuli.

She chaired an investigation that determined Israel committed genocide in Gaza

Pillay chaired the Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory and Israel, which was created by the UN-backed Human Rights Council.

The commission a year ago concluded Israel was responsible for genocide in Gaza with a specific intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza.

The commission also found that the Israeli president, prime minister and former defence minister "have incited the commission of genocide.” Israel, which has refused to cooperate with the commission since it was established in 2021, has strenuously denied the charges.

open image in gallery Former UN Human Rights Commissioner Navi Pillay ( Reuters )

Pillay has repeatedly rejected accusations from critics who accused her of antisemitism or allegedly turning a blind eye to the Hamas attacks in Israel.

In an interview last year, she recalled how she worked closely with some Jewish lawyers in the fight against apartheid in her native South Africa and was invited to Israel as the UN rights chief from 2008 to 2014.

Pillay’s win brings renewed attention to US President Donald Trump’s ongoing feud with the International Criminal Court. The Trump administration has already sanctioned 13 of the ICC’s staff members, among them key prosecutors and nine judges, including the court’s Japanese President Tomoko Akane.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has launched what he called a “sweeping campaign to dismantle the threat posed by the International Criminal Court.”

News.title: Gulf Coast braces for Isaias as hurricane expected to strengthen
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Isaias was expected to strengthen into a major hurricane on Friday as it surged towards the Gulf Coast, where final preparations were being made for potentially life-threatening storm surges and high winds.

The National Hurricane Center said the hurricane is set to make landfall late on Friday somewhere along the Alabama-Florida line.

Meanwhile, the weather event is expected to create dangerous conditions in the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi.

The Category 2 storm was packing 110 mph (177 kph) winds early on Friday – just shy of a Category 3 status – and was set to continue strengthening. Category 3 storms can cause devastating damage, the center warned.

Isaias was expected to weaken quickly as it hits shore and be downgraded to a tropical storm by Saturday afternoon as it moves north and inland along the Alabama-Mississippi line, the center said.

open image in gallery Brian Brunick (C) and other residents fill sandbags that were provided by the city of Orange Beach as they prepare for the possible arrival of Hurricane Isaias on October 08, 2026 ( Getty )

“Preparations should be rushed to completion as the weather will go downhill quickly today,” the hurricane center said in an early morning forecast. “While the storm is not expected to make landfall at peak intensity, it is likely that Isaias will still be a significant hurricane when it reaches the coast.”

Isaias, the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, was centered about 200 miles (322 kilometers) south-southeast of the mouth of the Mississippi River and moving to the north at about 15 mph (24 kph), the center said.

It was expected to make landfall between Mobile Bay on the Alabama coast and Choctawhatchee Bay in the Florida Panhandle in the evening.

Besides wind and storm surges, the hurricane will likely bring flash flooding and spawn tornadoes, the hurricane center said.

A hurricane warning was in place from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to the western Florida Panhandle. Tropical storm warnings were issued from southeastern Louisiana to Aucilla River along Florida's Big Bend.

Preparations have been going on for days. On Thursday, residents boarded up windows and stacked sandbags while thousands of National Guard soldiers were deployed.

open image in gallery David Schisler and Courtney Head place plywood over the windows of the Islander Ice Cream restaurant as they prepare for the possible arrival of Hurricane Isaias ( Getty )

Isaias is expected to bring a storm surge as high as 5 to 7 feet (1.5 to 2 meters), with the deepest water hitting immediate coastal areas, along with large and dangerous waves, the hurricane center said.

Coastal communities moved quickly to prepare on Thursday, as Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey ordered non-residents to immediately evacuate Gulf Shores, Orange Beach and Dauphin Island. Videos on social media showed traffic at a standstill on a highway leading out of Gulf Shores, where double-red beach flags signaled water access was closed.

Several counties announced mandatory evacuations for some coastal areas. The governors of Florida and Alabama declared states of emergency for dozens of counties, with Florida’s Ron DeSantis saying about 5,000 National Guard troops were expected to mobilize by Friday.

On Dauphin Island, a 15-mile (24-kilometer) barrier island off the Alabama coast, officials encouraged voluntary evacuations, particularly on its popular western section, which is vulnerable to storm surge.

Mayor Jeff Collier said he did not anticipate substantial damage, “but at the same time, these things are very fickle and a little jog here or there, or some last-minute increase in strength — we just have to be prepared for the worst.”

Meanwhile in the Pacific Ocean, Hurricane Simon, which formed as a tropical storm on Wednesday off of Mexico and became a hurricane late Thursday, was forecast to strengthen into a Category 4 hurricane.

News.title: The funniest workplace sitcom just turned 20 — and it’s not The Office
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

It was a Wednesday night, October 11, 2006, when Tina Fey’s Liz Lemon first bought an entire hot dog cart’s worth of hot dogs just to spite some jerk who cut in line, and the world was introduced to 30 Rock.

Looking back now, it’s clear we were in the midst of a golden age for workplace sitcoms. Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant’s superlative, groundbreaking The Office had run from 2001 to 2003, paving the way for the Steve Carell-starring American adaptation that arrived in 2005 and quickly became a television juggernaut.

Britain’s The IT Crowd also debuted around the same time, while a couple of years later Fey’s longtime collaborator Amy Poehler brought Parks and Recreation, her big-hearted take on small-town government, to screens.

Amidst all that competition, however, 30 Rock always stood out as something special. By the time it came to an end after seven seasons in 2013, it had proved itself weirder, smarter and sharper than anything else on television. More to the point, it was simply funnier than its rivals.

In a fastidious 2014 survey, The Atlantic writer Talib Visram found that 30 Rock has an astounding joke-per-minute rate of 7.44, more than any other sitcom he examined. In terms of laugh density, the show is the closest thing we’ve ever had to a live-action version of The Simpsons (before it went downhill).

open image in gallery Tina Fey, Jack McBrayer, Jane Krakowski, Alec Baldwin and Tracy Morgan in ‘30 Rock’ ( NBCUniversal Television Distribution )

Fey, of course, had a wealth of experience to draw on as the first female head writer of Saturday Night Live. She first joined the long-running sketch show in 1997 as a behind-the-scenes writer, before eventually working her way into the cast (and behind the Weekend Update desk) in 2000. While still working as the show’s head writer, she’d gone off to Hollywood and enjoyed great success with her first-ever movie script: 2004’s Mean Girls.

Surprisingly, it wasn’t originally her idea to take viewers behind the scenes at an NBC sketch show based out of 30 Rockefeller Plaza. She originally pitched the network a sitcom where she would have played the producer to Alec Baldwin’s on-air Bill O’Reilly-style blowhard news commentator.

Much like Aaron Sorkin and HBO later did with The Newsroom, she envisioned a show that would wrap real-life current affairs into the narrative. “It was good we didn’t try to do that, because I would have drowned trying to keep up with the subject matter,” Fey told Rolling Stone in 2013.

It was actually an NBC exec who suggested she mine her experience in the SNL writing room. “It seemed so lazy to just write about writing,” Fey recalled thinking, but she reconsidered when she hit upon the idea of casting her former SNL castmate Tracy Morgan as one of the show’s stars. “I thought, ‘Oh, this could be a thing.’”

open image in gallery Alec Baldwin was never better than as network executive Jack Donaghy, argues Kevin EG Perry ( NBC )

The chaotic Morgan, who played a character named Tracy Jordan, did indeed become one of the most hilarious and unpredictable weapons in the show’s arsenal (in one memorably meta sequence, he can be heard off-screen yelling: “We’re on a show within a show! My real name is Tracy Morgan!”) but, as with all great workplace comedies, 30 Rock thrived because of its ensemble.

There was Fey herself as the schlubby Liz Lemon, essentially a version of her own personality as a writer at SNL before she started appearing on screen. “I wouldn’t want her to do anything that I wouldn’t do,” she once said of the character. In the pilot episode, Liz’s female-focused sketch comedy series, The Girlie Show, starring Jane Krakowski’s wildly narcissistic Jenna Maroney, is forced by a meddling NBC executive to take on Jordan as its new male star.

That executive was a never-better Alec Baldwin as Jack Donaghy, whose ambition to rise through the ranks of NBC’s real-life parent company General Electric was matched only by the sharpness of his suits (“It’s after six,” he once remarked after being asked by Lemon why he was wearing a tuxedo. “What am I, a farmer?”). The character, partly inspired by SNL creator Lorne Michaels, was officially known as the Vice President of East Coast Television and Microwave Oven Programming, a ridiculous job title that only seems more prescient in our current age of mergers and endless media giant consolidation.

open image in gallery ‘30 Rock’ creator Tina Fey, Alex Baldwin and Lorne Michaels after winning big at the 2007 Emmys ( Getty Images )

While 30 Rock could be silly, it didn’t shy away from sharp-witted satire. When GE sold NBCUniversal to Comcast in 2011, the takeover was spoofed as the network being sold to family-owned TV company Kabletown within the world of the show. “It’s a fine and generous company,” said Lemon nervously, breaking the fourth wall to look directly down the camera.

The show was never a major ratings hit during its initial run on air, pulling in an audience of 5 to 7 million at its peak. For context, that’s about half the audience who were watching The Big Bang Theory at the time. Nevertheless, Fey’s show became a critical darling, winning a total of 16 Emmys, including a three-year run as Outstanding Comedy between 2007 and 2009.

Today, 30 Rock lives on via streaming (on Peacock in the U.S. and Netflix in the U.K.) and through the wide variety of deathless memes it spawned, from Steve Buscemi playing a terrible undercover cop uttering: “How do you do, fellow kids?” to Liz’s weary “What a week, huh?” being volleyed back by Jack’s: “Lemon, it’s Wednesday.”

open image in gallery Steve Buscemi’s ‘How Do You Do Fellow Kids?’ meme originated in a 2012 episode of ‘30 Rock’. The actor later referenced the scene for a Halloween costume ( Twitter/@WUTangKids & @DebraWexler_ )

The show also gained a reputation for an almost Simpsons-esque prescience after many of its spoof shows and movies were ushered into reality. Most famously, the show’s reality show satire MILF Island (“Twenty-five super hot moms. Fifty eighth-grade boys. No rules.”) preceded the all-too-real 2023 TLC series MILF Manor, and it also predicted celebrities being inserted into shows by AI avatar and 10-second microshows. “Most of the fake shows were just heightened versions of what was already happening,” Fey recently told The Ringer. “So yeah, not surprised that we actually ended up with MILF Island. We’re a fallen society.”

As for Fey, in the years since 30 Rock ended, she’s gone from a Liz to a Jack. She now heads her own sprawling media empire estimated to be worth up to $150 million, with a production company behind a string of hit shows as well as a Mean Girls Broadway musical. She’s also long been rumored as the most likely successor to Lorne Michaels if and when he ever releases his steely grip on SNL.

Whether or not Fey takes that tricky job, and whatever else she creates, it seems unlikely she’ll ever top the wild brilliance of 30 Rock. As thick and fast as the jokes came, it was also a show with real heart. In the finale, as Jack struggled to find the words, Liz told him simply: “I love you too, Jack.” Their platonic, teasing, ultimately supportive relationship helped create the sort of workplace where you’d be more than happy to stay late. Time for a rewatch.

News.title: Amazon's delivery box is changing and so is online shopping
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

As afternoon draws to a close, stacks of brown cardboard packages of various sizes gather in lobbies. Marked by the distinctive curved smile stretching from "A" to "Z", each parcel signals a commercial empire built on promises of endless choice and instant satisfaction.

The Amazon delivery box, a familiar presence on suburban doorsteps and urban corridors alike, represents more than simple cardboard. It symbolises a modern consumer culture where orders are expected within hours or, in a growing number of cities, in under 30 minutes. Behind every delivery lies a vast logistical network of warehouse workers and automated sorting robots, alongside fleets of trucks, vans, bicycles and drones bringing items directly to doorsteps.

This level of speed marks a stark departure from a few decades ago, when immediate purchases required travelling to a local shop. Mail-order catalogue options existed, but deliveries routinely took at least a week to arrive.

Amazon swiftly reshaped those consumer expectations. Launched from founder Jeff Bezos’s garage as an online bookshop in July 1995, the company expanded into CDs, DVDs, toys and clothing, evolving into "the everything store".

In 2005, Amazon transformed online retail by introducing two-day shipping for Prime members. Since then, delivery times have steadily contracted. This year, the company is rolling out 30-minute delivery, with Amazon noting that over 300 million items across more than 35 categories now qualify for free Prime shipping in the US.

open image in gallery An Amazon Flex driver delivers a large cardboard box to a residential doorstep. ( Getty/iStock )

E-commerce should account for 17.4% of U.S. retail sales this year, or $1.4 trillion, according to research firm eMarketer. Amazon commands 40% of the U.S. online market, ahead of No. 2 Walmart at 11.4%, according to the firm. This comes as Amazon evolves into not only an e-commerce juggernaut but a major force in cloud computing and artificial intelligence.

As Amazon rapidly expands, it's rolling out a series of innovations to make its packaging lighter, tighter and easier to recycle, according to Pat Lindner, the company's vice president of mechatronics and sustainable packaging. Amazon is also moving away from single-use plastic packaging. Amazon reduced the share of its North American shipments that use single-use plastic packaging from 65% in 2023 to 27% in 2025.

open image in gallery Packages in Amazon boxes move along a conveyor belt at the UPS Worldport hub in Louisville, Ky., Nov. 20, 2015. (AP Photo/Patrick Semansky, File) ( Copyright 2018 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

Moreover, Amazon is reducing the number of its trademark boxes it uses.

Now, about 11% of the company's global orders are shipped in their original manufacturer packaging without adding extra boxes or envelopes, Amazon says. And last year, more than half weren't sent in a box — they were either delivered in their original packaging or flexible packaging.

Still, the box won't go away, Lindner says. “The box will always be important," he says, “and we’ll continue to innovate to meet the customer’s needs.”

News.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor compensated £300,000 after Royal Lodge lease ends
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has been granted £302,000 in compensation after his lease on his former Royal Lodge home in Windsor was officially surrendered, a Crown Estate spokesperson said.

The former Duke of York left the Royal Lodge and moved onto the Sandringham Estate in Norfolk in February this year.

As he handed back the keys, Mr Mountbatten-Windsor paid £1.8m for dilapidations, the sum of which was informed and reviewed by independent advisers. This term was included in the lease to reflect the significant £7.5m refurbishments made by the tenant at the start of the lease.

The outbuilding needs significant repairs and the main house and garden are understood to need restoration, as reported by The Times.

open image in gallery Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor now lives on the Sandringham Estate ( Getty )

A Crown Estate spokesperson said Mr Mountbatten-Windsor was entitled to compensation because, as per the terms of his lease, he surrendered it within the first 25 years.

The Crown Estate received a net amount of £1.5m, taking into account the £302,000 compensation to the former Duke of York.

A spokesperson for The Crown Estate said: “The lease for Royal Lodge has ended and our focus now is firmly on its future use and the opportunities to generate additional financial value for the nation from its early return.”

The Crown Estate is understood to be determining the future use of the property as part of the Windsor Estate. When the review is complete, the property will be marketed for its proposed future use by two nationally recognised agents.

open image in gallery The entrance gates near Royal Lodge, the former home of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, in Windsor ( PA )

Mr Mountbatten-Windsor’s tenancy at the Royal Lodge ended after it was reported he had lived there on a peppercorn rent since 2003, although he paid £1m for the lease and a further £7.5m for refurbishments.

In June, a National Audit Office investigation revealed that the late Queen’s second son received an undisclosed private income from subletting three cottages on the Royal Lodge estate while paying a peppercorn rent for more than two decades.

The former Duke of York’s £302,000 payout – and £1.8m dilapidation fee – is the latest issue, as he has been locked in a legal battle with Thames Valley Police.

A High Court judge agreed to quash search warrants issued by the Central Criminal Court which allowed officers to raid the Royal Lodge and his home on the Sandringham Estate.

Now, both sides must engage in another court battle as to whether the force can use the material seized from Mr Mountbatten Windsor’s premises, with a hearing in the case to be held in private in 2027.

Thames Valley Police’s investigation into misconduct in public office remains ongoing. Mr Mountbatten-Windsor has strenuously denied any wrongdoing.

News.title: Apple is about to launch a whole new kind of Mac, report claims
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Apple is about to launch its first touchscreen Mac, according to reports.

The company is planning to launch a new version of the MacBook that will come with a touch-sensitive OLED display, according to a new report from Bloomberg. It is expected to arrive this month, alongside updates to its existing Mac line-up with new chips and an improved iPad Mini, the same report claimed.

Apple has long been rumoured to be working on touchscreen MacBooks. But its executives have also been dismissive of the idea since at least 2010, arguing that it is uncomfortable to reach out and press the display of a laptop.

The latest rumours come amid a busy launch period for Apple. Last month, it launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, the latter of which will be released on 23 October, and the company is planning a smart home-focused event on 13 October that will also bring entirely new kinds of products.

The increased released schedule comes amid the arrival of new Apple chief executive John Ternus, its former hardware chief, who took over from Tim Cook at the beginning of September. He has been reported to be looking to push Apple into introducing new kinds of devices at an increased speed compared to his predecessor.

The second October event is due to come towards the end of the month, the report said, with Bloomberg claiming it will happen “on or around” Tuesday, 27 October. It is unclear what format Apple will choose for either of the October events, and whether they will feature a public, live-streamed video of the kind it uses to launch its iPhones.

The latter event will focus primarily on the Mac, the report claimed, though a new iPad Mini is also expected. The launch will focus on “creative professionals who work in video production, photo editing and music production”, Bloomberg reported.

The headline products will be the new 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen devices, which will also have new OLED displays, bring the Dynamic Island from the iPhone to the Mac for the first time, as well as coming in a new “significantly lighter” design. Those computers will be powered by Apple’s M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which were first announced in March, when they were added to Apple’s existing MacBook Pro models.

But there will also be a new iPad mini with an OLED screen, a different placement for the FaceTime camera, and a better speaker system. There will also be new versions of the iMac and entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro that will be unchanged on the outside but get the M6 that was announced with an updated Mac mini in August.

Apple’s executives have been negative about the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. In a Wired interview in 2018, for instance, its software chief Craig Federighi said that “the ergonomics of using a Mac are that your hands are rested on a surface, and that lifting your arm up to poke a screen is a pretty fatiguing thing to do”.

That echoed statements from Steve Jobs at a 2010 launch event, in which he rejected the idea of a touchscreen Mac for similar reasons. He said that the company had tested the idea but found it “ergonomically terrible” and that “touch surfaces don’t want to be vertical”.

“It gives great demo but after a short period of time, you start to fatigue and after an extended period of time, your arm wants to fall off,” he said. “It doesn't work, it's ergonomically terrible.”

In 2021, when he was Apple’s hardware engineering boss, new chief executive John Ternus seemed to echo those concerns. He said instead that Apple already made a touchscreen computer in its tablet, and positioned that as distinct from the Mac.

“We make the world’s best touch computer on an iPad. It’s totally optimised for that,” he told the Wall Street Journal then.

“And the Mac is totally optimised for indirect input. We haven’t really felt a reason to change that.”

But there have been signs that Apple has been softening its stance. During a 2022 interview, Mr Federighi was again by the Wall Street Journal about the possibility of a touchscreen Mac, and gave a cryptic response: ““Who’s to say?”.

It remains unclear how and whether Apple has addressed those concerns about the ergonomics and comfort of reaching out to touch a laptop screen. While many other companies have launched touchscreen laptops of their own, that problem has continued to limit their adoption, and some have taken other steps such as allowing the laptop screen to open all the way around so that it can be held like a tablet.

News.title: What is the XFG Covid strain? Symptoms and what to know as the variant hits the UK
News.content:
Cases of Covid-19 have risen sharply across the UK this month, driven largely by a variant of the virus known as ‘XFG’.

Sometimes referred to as ‘Stratus’ and the ‘American strain’, owing to the fact that it is now the most common strain in North America, it was first identified in January 2025 and has since spread worldwide.

Between August and September, Covid cases in Britain jumped 230 per cent, from 1,374 to 4,589 new infections, half of which were caused by the XFG strain.

Hospitalisation rates have also increased by 15 per cent in the same period, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

The true number of cases is likely to be much higher, as most people who contract Covid-19 experience a milder illness and will not visit hospital or receive an official diagnosis via their GP.

What are the symptoms, and how is it different from other variants?

Symptoms of XFG are similar to other variants of Covid-19 like Delta and Omicron, and typically begin with a sore throat, before developing into a cough and fever.

However, experts have noted that patients diagnosed with XFG tend to present with a characteristic hoarse, croaky voice, which is distinctive from older strains.

More than 30 other symptoms have been known to be associated with XFG and other Covid strains, including diarrhoea, vomiting, loss of taste and smell, shortness of breath, headache, and muscle aches.

Why are cases rising?

Current data does not suggest that XFG leads to more severe illness than any other variant in circulation, according to the UKHSA.

As the UK moves into winter, colder and wetter weather naturally influences the rise in respiratory illnesses like Covid-19 and the flu, given people spend more time indoors and in closer proximity to each other, where viruses can more easily transmit between them.

It has also been roughly a year since the last significant wave of Covid-19 cases, meaning that the population-wide immunity has somewhat waned, making people more susceptible to the disease, the UKHSA said.

Can you be vaccinated against XFG?

The current Covid-19 vaccine is designed to protect against XFG and related strains specifically, after modelling suggested it would become the dominant variant this season.

Those eligible for a Covid-19 autumn booster include adults over the age of 75, residents in care homes, and anyone over six months old with a weakened immune system, due to a health condition or treatment.

Covid vaccines are also available to buy privately for those who are not eligible for a free jab, and typically cost around £98 per dose.

What should you do if you suspect you have XFG?

The NHS no longer advises that people with symptoms of Covid-19 take a test, unless they want to do so.

If you feel unwell or have a high temperature, health authorities advise you to try and stay home and avoid contact with people until you feel better.

They also recommend avoiding contact with vulnerable people, like those undergoing chemotherapy or the elderly, for at least 10 days.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Harry’s Invictus Games challenge in Kenya is helping veterans battle physical and mental scars
News.content:
Wounded veterans from 10 countries have gathered in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley for a week of endurance challenges, organised by the charity behind Prince Harry’s Invictus Games.

Twenty-five serving and former personnel, among them a Ukrainian who survived a direct bomb hit in Donetsk and a Danish combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Afghanistan, will run, hike or cycle up to 120km across the area on Saturday October 10, World Mental Health Day.

The Invictus Games Foundation, the charity the Duke of Sussex founded in 2014 for wounded, injured and sick service personnel, has organised the event.

For Vasyl, a Ukrainian soldier, it will be his first time in Africa and his first long-distance challenge.

After three weeks of military training in the UK, the 34-year-old joined a brigade in Donetsk as a reconnaissance squad commander, spending more than 19 months on the front line. He was wounded when a drone dropped a grenade three metres from him, and the shrapnel still causes frequent pain in his leg which can sometimes make walking difficult.

But he said the physical injury was easier to bear than the loss of the friends he made in the trenches.

“There is a level of kindness between comrades in a trench that you will never find in civilian life,” he said. “If someone made a mistake or said something wrong, we immediately forgave them and thought nothing more of it.

“For me, the pain of loss is the hardest thing the war has left behind.”

News.title: From Yale to the Congo: The mathematician who became one of Africa’s most intrepid reporters
News.content:
Sundaram has a lot of experience with the Rwandan methods of control. After spending 17 months in DRC, he moved to Kigali and he is eloquent about the convoluted effects of dictatorship. “Living in Rwanda taught me so much about how dictatorships function internally and how counter-intuitive they can be. A friend of mine who was working in public health told me ‘When we ask people in India to wash their hands we get a 30 per cent success rate from a campaign, but when we need people in Rwanda to wash their hands, we just need to slip a line in one of Kagame’s speeches and we get a 90 per cent success rate. That’s fantastic isn’t it?’

“And I said, ‘well is it? It’s great for short term health outcomes but what does that say about society? Isn’t democracy about people choosing freely? What if the government tells them to do something bad – like what happened in the genocide when people were told to kill all the Tutsis?’

“Kagame and his army stopped the genocide, and he has restored peace, but he governs using the same system that was used to perpetrate the genocide.”

In Bad News: Last Journalists in a Dictatorship, the book Sundaram went on to write about his time in Rwanda teaching journalists, he describes a more extreme version of this phenomenon, recalling how Kagame once commented that thatched roofs on huts were primitive. “And the local authorities took that as a sign that he didn’t like thatched roofs, and that they should get rid of them. And without replacements being built, people climbed up and dismantled their own thatched roofs. And I saw these villages with houses which just had mud walls without roofs, and the families were sitting outside with their children and their goats, the thatch strewn on the ground. In the rain, quite often. The children would get sick, and it was like a war zone.

“At the end of my time in Congo, I was at a UN base and they were digging latrines, when they found some human bones. They stopped digging and alerted the press, and I happened to be in Goma nearby.” He subsequently found out that it was one of a series of mass graves containing the bodies of Congolese killed by forces controlled by Kagame. “And so when I arrived I had a sense of what Rwanda had done in Congo, but I didn’t fully appreciate the extent to which it was totalitarian. I’d heard that the country was a shining example of progress – aid programs were successful, and poverty reduction programs. The streets were clean, public services functioned. I was living in a nice house with a big garden provided by the journalism programme I was working in.”

Many European governments, including Britain, are enamoured with Rwanda, because, says Sundaram, “dictatorships can be very efficient”. But it is a “mirage of a country”, he says.

The teaching programme he was running was briefed not to challenge the government on any level, and an embassy official told him that if any of the journalists mentioned repression they would be expelled.

“Layer by layer, as I began to talk to the journalists I was training, the true story unravelled. The first instance was when one of them left the programme, and I heard him on the radio one day praising the president, but with a degree of flattery that was completely exaggerated, and I didn’t understand why. The rest of the class were reluctant to talk about it but eventually I learned that another student had been beaten to a coma on the day he criticised the president.

“I started to realise that my class contained some of the most courageous journalists in the country.” As a foreigner, if he transgressed, Sundaram could have his visa cancelled or get kicked out, or even locked up for a couple of days, but for the Rwandan journalists, everything was at stake. They could be killed or their families threatened.

“But still they persisted, and they took me around the country and showed me all the things the government didn’t want anyone to see – things they couldn’t report on because it was too dangerous, so they wanted to show me because they wanted somebody to speak up. It’s really a book about them – they’ve been my greatest teachers in journalism.”

News.title: I tried Amazon’s new iPad rival – and there’s one standout feature
News.content:
Amazon says that this tablet has three times the computing power and nine times the graphics power of any previous Amazon tablet, so this is a significant boost in performance to previous models.

That will make light tasks, such as crunching through emails, browser-based activity like online shopping and document work. With a keyboard factored in, it could work as a laptop alternative for some. The same could be said of the iPad Air, although with recent price increases from Apple and the matte screen, for my money, this is a better proposition.

The premium makeover that comes with the Alexa Tablet Pro includes a slim aluminium design, with flattened edges, so it looks like an iPad or Samsung tablet, only 6.5mm thick. The Pro version only comes in the Graphite colour seen here. All models in the new line-up feel more grown-up and less like kid’s tablets than the Fire range. Plus the switch to proper Android over Fire OS is welcome and will result in better app compatibility (although I noticed that these tablets were running Android 16, which is now an old version).

It has a battery that’s good for 16 hours of video playback and supports 27W charging. There are cameras front and rear although like any tablet, these won’t be as good as your phone, while there’s support for Dolby Atmos from the speakers, so your movies will sound decent.

The AI capabilities are a step up

As the name suggests, Amazon is keen to promote the AI element here. It has customised the interface slightly with access to Alexa+ meaning you can utilise Amazon’s AI at any time to ask about what’s on the screen, to control smart home devices or search for content. If you are a keen Alexa user, then that will be a plus, but for me it’s not the headline news.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football tips: Game Week 6
News.content:
As the Telegraph Fantasy Football season heads further into 2026-27, the award-winning experts at Fantasy Football Hub ccontinue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

Join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips.



Telegraph Fantasy Football: last week's insights



Brighton humble the champs

For the second week in a row, the Seagulls are highlighted for a ‘near-perfect’ performance, this time scoring an impressive three goals without reply against the Gunners. Thirty-five-year-old Pascal Gross (£3.7m) once again stole the headlines with a goal and an assist, but defensive assets Maxim De Cuyper (£2.8m) and Luka Vuskovic (£2.9m) similarly warrant TFF manager interest.



Brentford thrash Chelsea

The Bees also ran out 3-0 victors last time out, with Igor Thiago (£4.6m) netting his first league goal of the campaign. One point of note was the surprise omission of Mamadou Sangare (£3.1m) from the starting XI; his 7 per cent ownership will be hoping that was just a tactical decision based on the opposition.



Etihad thriller

Brian Brobbey (£3.3m) joined a short list of players to score a hat-trick in a losing effort in the Premier League, as Sunderland conceded five in Manchester. Antoine Semenyo (£4.9m) was City’s star player, with an appearance, two goals, an assist and tackle bonus combining for a 16-point return.

Visit the Telegraph Fantasy Football Stats Centre for all player points >



Telegraph Fantasy Football Tips: Game Week 6



The Telegraph Fantasy Football player list has been analysed ahead of the upcoming games, and these look like the best players to transfer in:



1. Bukayo Saka (£6.0m)

Only Haaland (£8.3m) has bettered the England winger’s nine shots on target this season, and with a share of set-pieces, potentially including penalties, Arsenal’s No.7 has the means to return a haul against Leeds at the Emirates in Saturday’s early kick-off.



2. Gonzalo García (£3.7m)

Fulham now play all three promoted teams back-to-back, starting with Ipswich in GW6. The forward has looked lively at the start of the season and will be looking to add to his two goals this weekend.



3. Harvey Barnes (£4.4m)

A Monday night fixture is always a great entry point to make fixture gains, and with no international football over the break, the winger will be looking to return against Coventry.

News.title: Kenyan authorities scramble to find passengers on Ebola flight
News.content:
Authorities are racing to track down passengers who boarded a flight from Uganda to Kenya on Saturday alongside a man infected with Ebola.

The man travelled by bus from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of an Ebola outbreak that has killed 4,000 people, to Kampala, Uganda. He then boarded a flight to Nairobi on Saturday, October 3, which was operated by the African airline Jambojet.

The patient went to a hospital in Nairobi and died just 48 hours later, meaning the journey took place in the final days of infection, the stage at which patients who die of the disease are most contagious. By October 6 authorities had tracked down 28 contacts, including family members of the deceased, but said they urgently needed to track down 23 passengers and crew who had travelled on the same flight.

The man is Kenya’s first ever case of the disease. Ebola does not typically spread through the air like Covid-19 or measles, requiring close contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person to spread. However, an aeroplane cabin significantly intensifies these risks because passengers share cramped spaces for prolonged periods and touch the same surfaces, such as a cabin toilet.

“We are working closely with the Ministry of Health, Port Health Services and other relevant authorities to support the ongoing public health response, including the identification and management of the other guests and crew who may have been in contact with the individual,” a spokesperson for Jambojet said on Tuesday.

After landing in Kenya, airport staff screened the patient, standard protocol for people travelling from at-risk countries during the current Ebola outbreak, but allowed him to continue his journey into Nairobi.

Kenya’s health ministry director-general, Patrick Amoth, said the patient may have passed through airport screening because medication had masked his symptoms.

News.title: Africa embraces ‘Go to Work on an Egg’ to boost maternal health and nutrition
News.content:
The sun is barely up when villagers start queuing for eggs at the metal gate of Shamim Haried’s home.

By noon, all that day’s supply is usually sold out, but people keep coming and asking if there are any left.

Demand is so high that arguments can break out in the queue, says the mother-of-two who lives outside Malawi’s capital, Lilongwe.

Her eggs are cheaper and fresher than those sold in the market.

“The people almost fight for eggs: it’s hard to watch,” she explains.

“Eggs are the cheapest healthy protein that they can get and it’s better for them to buy here than anywhere else.”

Her flock of 1,400 chickens lay around 1,000 eggs each day, but she reckons she could sell three times that.

Sports.title: Defining results that got Man Utd managers the sack, from Moyes’ European nightmare to Amorim’s Grimsby embarrassment
Sports.content:
Next

EVERY Manchester United manager in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era has endured a defining result that led to their axing.

With Michael Carrick, the suspicion is it will be the opening weekend loss at Hull. Carrick remains in charge but United have not recovered from their going-over at the newly-promoted Tigers a month ago.



Carrick has been in the dugout with two former United managers and shared their pain. There were tears during the interval at Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s last match at Watford.

Solskjaer did his post-match media rounds in front of the Sir Elton John Stand. He was still standing but knew it was time to say Goodbye Yellow Brick Road.



Here are the results that saw the tide turn against recent United managers…

DAVID MOYES: Olympiakos 2-0 United, February 2014



Gary Neville’s hyperbolic suggestion that the first 15 minutes of the second half at Fulham was the worst he had seen United play in 46 years was total claptrap.

Among the dozens of worse 15-minute spells, Olympiakos is one of them. Only times it by six.

Handed a kind Champions League knockout draw, United lost 2-0, Robin van Persie complained about team-mates in his “zone”, Roy Keane unloaded on live television and Carrick’s wife, Lisa, dubbed Keane a “****”.

United executive vice-chairman Ed Woodward took a picture of the scoreboard to remind him it could not get any worse (it would) but there was a shift at boardroom level.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Man Utd ratings v Fulham MANCHESTER UNITED salvaged a 1-1 draw as Fulham narrowly missed out on their first Premier League win of the season. Matheus Cunha’s late deflected strike saved United from a first defeat at Craven Cottage since 2009. Lisandro Martinez’s embarrassing own goal after Senne Lammens parried out Calvin Bassey‘s shot in the 63rd minute summed up a dreadful afternoon for the Red Devils. Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the outrun United players at a sunny Craven Cottage.

With Champions League qualification through the Premier League improbable, Woodward touched base with Louis van Gaal in March.

As soon as it was mathematically impossible for United to finish in the top four with a 2-0 loss at Everton on Easter Sunday, the club made up their mind.

Dedicated correspondents revealed on Easter Monday that Moyes would be sacked. On Tuesday morning, it was confirmed.

LOUIS VAN GAAL: Midtjylland 2-1 United, February 2016

There was a February fright for Van Gaal as well. At Danish minnows Midtjylland, United were so bad their supporters sang along to the old Frankie Valli and Four Seasons tune.



“Freezing cold on a Thursday night, and we’re playing f*****g s***e, what a feeling, what a night.”

Days later, this correspondent broke the news that Jose Mourinho had a gentleman’s agreement to take over at United.

That United trounced Midtjylland 5-1 in the second leg was largely inconsequential. They were only in the Europa League after Champions League group stage elimination and would be outfought by Liverpool in the next round.

Mourinho had to sit tight for three more months and United’s failure to secure Champions League football saw Van Gaal’s contract shredded a year before its expiry date.



JOSE MOURINHO: United 1-2 Sevilla, March 2018

The watershed moment of Mourinho’s two-and-a-half years at United is trickier to pinpoint.

United’s elimination by Sevilla in the Champions League last 16 was scandalous. Sevilla were one of the weakest teams in the knockout phase and had already dismissed one coach.

After the Old Trafford triumph, Sevilla did not win in nine games and Vincenzo Montella was given the boot.



Woodward privately found United’s 3-1 loss at West Ham in late September 2018 to be difficult to stomach.

Rumours sparked by a loose-lipped United great that Mourinho would go, whatever the result against Newcastle a week later, were false but he had entered the endgame.

When United hosted Juventus on October 23, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was in town. He reached a verbal agreement with Woodward to take over as caretaker if or when Mourinho fell on his sword.

Eight weeks later, Solskjaer was parachuted in.

OLE GUNNAR SOLSKJAER: United 0-5 Liverpool, October 2021



There were various windows when United could or should have dispensed with Solskjaer while Mauricio Pochettino was available. Eventually, his downfall came about more hastily.

United presented Solskjaer with a new contract in the summer of 2021 when his previous deal still had a year left to run. Come October, they had decided he had to go.

The 5-0 capitulation to Liverpool signalled the end for Solskjaer, with the thrashing soundtracked to Scousers crowing, “Ole’s at the wheel”. Yet United had no succession plan, so stood by him until they formulated a strategy.



United beat Tottenham 3-0 two days before Nuno Espirito Santo was sacked and earned a last-gasp draw at Atalanta. But they were outclassed by Manchester City in a 2-0 defeat in which United had more attempts on target at their own goal than City’s.

It was the November international break yet the manner of the loss was not deemed a sackable result. So Solskjaer took charge at Vicarage Road, where United were hammered 4-1 by eventually relegated Watford.

Solskjaer filmed his exit interview the following morning.

ERIK TEN HAG: United 0-3 Tottenham, September 2024

United had planned to sack Ten Hag in May until they lost their nerve following the uplifting FA Cup final win against City. Ten Hag’s contract was extended by a year, which was hardly a ringing endorsement, but United signed a handful more Dutch players.



Nothing changed. September was bookended by two 3-0 home reverses to Liverpool and Tottenham.

On the day of the former, chief executive Omar Berrada insisted Ten Hag retained “full backing”. Come the end of the month, United started planning his sacking.

The October international break came and went but Ten Hag was a dead man walking.

United did not act until a pretty luckless defeat at West Ham, decided by an appalling VAR intervention, in late October so that they were assured of hiring Ruben Amorim.



RUBEN AMORIM: Grimsby 2-2 United, August 2025

Amorim is the one United manager whose sacking was not results-related.

The Portuguese engineered his departure by undermining director of football Jason Wilcox and daring the club to sack him after his final match in charge at Leeds.

Amorim was dismayed by Wilcox’s conduct in a meeting to review the lifeless 1-1 draw with basement club Wolves on December 30.



He also got wind of Wilcox referring to himself as “the manager” in exchanges with staff at United’s Carrington training complex.

But, ultimately, elimination by League Two Grimsby on a biblically rainy night in Cleethorpes was Amorim’s ‘Midtjylland moment’.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

United were 2-0 down at half-time, Amorim got out a tactics board and defeat in a penalty shootout pushed Amorim past the point of no return.

Whatever strides United made over Amorim’s final four-and-a-bit months, he could not be a success after such a debacle.

Sports.title: West Ham defender Dinos Mavropanos taking Championship by storm after learning from Erling Haaland
Sports.content:
Next

DINOS MAVROPANOS has gone toe-to-toe with Erling Haaland and Robert Lewandowski — so he knows a thing or two about lethal goalscorers.

But right now the West Ham defender is giving Championship strikers a fright after embarking on the hottest scoring streak of his career.



Towering defender Mavropanos has already netted four times this term, leaving a host of frontmen in his wake as the Irons fight for an immediate Premier League return.

His dominant performances saw him crowned SkyBet Championship Player of the Month for September, completing a double sweep for the East London club alongside boss Nuno Espirito Santo.



And both will be desperate to keep that momentum rolling when West Ham host London rivals QPR tonight where victory will take them back to the top of the table.

Greek powerhouse Mavropanos, 28, told SunSport: “Right now, everything goes right with set-pieces. It’s an aspect of the game we work hard on.



“I try to get the best out of it because I know how good the deliveries are from the guys who take them.

“The timing is important. I know how I can get an advantage from those balls into the box.”

Though currently battling in the second tier, Mavropanos built his reputation in elite company across the Premier League, Bundesliga and international stage.

And when asked to pick the most lethal marksmen he has stood up against in his career, Mavropanos said: “Haaland and Lewandowski — and I don’t have to explain why.



“As a defender, I don’t want my opponent to score. But with those two, you have to be focused for every single minute because they can always find a way to score.”

Yet despite keeping pace with the division’s leading scorers and taming world-class forwards, Mavropanos laughs off any suggestion he will be holding scoring clinics for West Ham’s attackers.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He smiled: “No, the strikers know already! They are going to score more goals than me because they are attackers, they have the qualities and get more chances.

“I don’t want to make people think I’m going to score 10 or 15 goals — although a 1-0 win with me scoring the winner is always nice.



“But I want to do my job and if I can get some goals along the way, then I’m happy.”

Despite winning last season’s Hammer of the Year, Mavropanos suffered the heartbreak of relegation, being edged out on the last day by an agonising two points by bitter London rivals Tottenham.

While others looked for an exit, the defender felt a duty to stay and help guide West Ham through their Championship rebuild.

He said: “It was a difficult moment for the club getting relegated. There were too many ups and downs and at the end we didn’t make it.

“But for me, it was important to be in a place where I feel really good. The environment here is great, the people help us, and the fans are always supporting us. I want to give back to them.



“For me, it was never an option to just look for a way out.

“When you win Hammer of the Year and you feel the love from the fans and the people at the club every day, you have a responsibility.

“We went down together, so it was always my goal to stay here, fight for this shirt, and help lead us straight back to where this club belongs.



“It’s nice to be up there fighting for promotion. The Championship is competitive and played at a high level. We know what we have to do.”

Mavropanos has also taken on a key leadership role in guiding West Ham’s emerging stars, such as 18-year-old academy defender Airidas Golambeckis, who made his debut this season.

He added: “Airidas is really good. He’s been training with the first team for the last couple of months and that gives him great experience.

“I always try to tell the youngsters to work hard and be patient. Nowadays, a lot of kids expect things straight away, but it’s not that easy. Him and the other young guys have huge potential.”

Juggling a brutal club schedule with international duty, Mavropanos arrived back at Rush Green having played a gruelling four games in just 10 days for Greece — capped by a man-of-the-match performance in a stunning 1-0 win in Germany.



Yet the Hammers ace keeps his recovery simple, shunning modern gadgets to keep track of everything.

Mavropanos said: “I’m not that crazy with technology or how deep I sleep. I just listen to my body.

“Sleep and food are the most important things. Then after that, you have ice baths, saunas, and treatments. As long as I’m healthy, I want to be out there giving everything for the team.”

Mavropanos credits his career turnaround to a crucial spell in Germany with Stuttgart and Nürnberg after leaving Arsenal.

And after testing himself in the Bundesliga and Premier League, he insists the Championship is as brutal as it gets.



He said: “My time in Germany was really important for me. After having some injury problems early in my career, going to the Bundesliga gave me the rhythm and confidence I needed.



“The Championship is relentless. In the Premier League you have quality, but here every single game is a physical battle from the first minute to the last. You can’t drop your level for even one week.”

Nuno, meanwhile, says although the managerial gong is nice, his team are nowhere near the finished article in the Championship.

He said: “It’s nice to listen to all the plaudits — but we have to improve. There’s a lot in our game we must do better.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We didn’t start the league as we wanted but we’ve reacted — but now the challenge is to sustain it and not believe it’s done.

“This award is a reflection of how we’ve all completed a small spell where we did things well.”

Sports.title: Inside story of Man City stars’ first 24 hours back as Ferran Soriano addresses squad and firm belief they’ll be cleared
Sports.content:
Next



MANCHESTER CITY stars have been assured the club will fight to clear its name through every available legal avenue following its financial scandal.

SunSport understands chief executive Ferran Soriano has moved to reassure players that City remain confident of overturning the guilty verdict following their return to training on Thursday.



Despite the uncertainty surrounding the club’s future, the atmosphere at the Etihad has remained remarkably calm, with players urged to maintain their focus on matters on the pitch.

Soriano is understood to have addressed the squad before boss Enzo Maresca delivered his own message ahead of preparations for their clash with Liverpool.



City chiefs are determined to ensure the ongoing legal battle does not derail the team’s momentum following the international break.

The club has also pointed to its previous successful appeal against Uefa sanctions in 2020, when a two-year European ban was overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.



And sources inside the Etihad, speaking anonymously to protect their relationships with the club, insist there is a strong belief that City can emerge victorious from their latest legal challenge.

One source told SunSport that the mood around the training ground on Thursday was calm, with every effort being made to maintain the positive atmosphere that existed before the international break.

Maresca reinforced that message during his press conference ahead of the Liverpool showdown, insisting he has complete faith in the club’s handling of the situation.

The City boss said: “First of all good morning, I understand the reason why most of you are here, but the only thing I can say is something that I already said, there is a process ongoing and in this moment I completely trust the club. This is what I can say about that.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Pressed on whether he believed City could win their appeal, the Italian added: “I spoke with the club for sure, we all trust and probably the right moment to speak about that is when we are going to win this appeal.”

Former manager Pep Guardiola is another influential figure determined to offer his support as City attempt to navigate one of the most turbulent periods in their history.

SunSport has already revealed that the Spaniard is expected to attend City’s upcoming clash with Paris Saint-Germain, in a further show of solidarity with his former employers.

Guardiola, who spent a decade at the Etihad, repeatedly defended the club during previous investigations and has remained a staunch supporter despite his departure.



The legendary boss has also been in contact with Maresca, with the pair speaking following City’s recent encounter with Manchester United.

Maresca confirmed the conversation and welcomed the prospect of Guardiola returning to the Etihad, insisting the former manager will always have a place at the club.

He said: “I spoke with Pep the last time after the Man United game, but I know that he is coming.”

The City boss added: “It’s always a pleasure, after 10 years here he can come any time he wants, not just a game, for a training session, for any moment.”

Buckley posted pics from the wedding on Instagram.



Jordeen captioned the wedding post: “Mr and Mrs Semenyo.”

Semenyo’s wedding came at the same time that his club Man City, who he only joined in January, made major headlines.



City were hit by 130 charges increased from 115, with an independent commission finding the club guilty of over 100 of them.

In shock findings from an independent commission, it was revealed City had inflated their revenues by more than £900million through ‘sham’ commercial deals.

City have always denied wrongdoing and the club recently released a statement vowing to prove their innocence.

But Semenyo and Jordeen would have been sure not to let City’s situation be a distraction on their special day.

The pair got engaged last November.



Jordeen and Antoine made the engagement Instagram official with the caption: “Forever has a nice ring to it.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And while that got fans talking in the comments section, Jordeen’s latest post attracted thousands of comments.

City team-mates Rayan Cherki, Jeremy Doku, Ruben Dias and a host of Premier League stars gave the new couple their congratulations.

REAL MADRID icon Cicinho has made the stunning transition from winning the LaLiga title with Real Madrid to becoming an evangelical pastor.

Sports.title: Wolff: People who think Mercedes favour Antonelli should watch Teletubbies
Sports.content:
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff says people who believe the team have favoured Kimi Antonelli over George Russell this season are "brainless" and should watch Teletubbies and Mickey Mouse instead of Formula 1.

Antonelli has defied pre-season expectations to build an 84-point lead over Russell at the top of the Drivers' Championship with just seven races remaining, including this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.

Wolff offered a scathing response to the suggestion Mercedes do not treat their drivers equally, which included a reference to criticism the team previously faced from Lewis Hamilton fans before the seven-time world champion left to join Ferrari.

"They're brainless, whoever thinks that," Wolff said on Friday in Singapore.

"It's completely nonsensical. We've had it in the past with Lewis fans."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell is OUT with a Power Unit failure in the closing stages of the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

Russell will start from the back of the grid in Singapore after an engine failure last weekend in Malaysia forced him into taking a penalty.

The Brit also confirmed on Thursday that he is likely to have to incur a further grid penalty before the end of the season given the position he has been left in by multiple technical failures.

Antonelli has also suffered from poor reliability this season, with technical issues costing the 20-year-old significant points hauls in Barcelona and at Silverstone.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell reacts to the penalty caused by his Bahrain GP engine failure, which will see him start at the back of the grid at the Singapore Grand Prix.

Despite the problems, Mercedes are closing in on a first constructors' title since 2021, as they hold a 151-point lead over Ferrari at the top of the standings.

Wolff continued: "I don't know what's going on. Do they think I have a button that says, 'George, engine failure now?'

"Or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we're fighting for the Constructors' Championship, when we've always had the mindset of providing everybody with equal material."

The Austrian suggested the situation is potentially a product of the way social media is used, but insisted that he is ultimately amused by it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff fumes after George Russell Power Unit failure at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

"I guess this is maybe where social media goes today," he added. "People hide behind their screens and then they lash out. There's a lot of polarisation going on.

"Sometimes I read what people write, I find it hilarious. These people really contribute to my own entertainment when they're abusing the team or myself. I'm Satan, I've heard. Overall, funny.

"Zero understanding and respect for people who come up with these things. Rather than watching Formula 1, they should do Teletubbies, or some Mickey Mouses."

'I feel a lot of emotions and compassion for George'

Wolff offered a further response to the idea that he favours Antonelli by revealing elements of the close relationship he and his wife Susie Wolff share with Russell and the Brit's partner Carmen Montero Mundt.

He said: "We have had Kimi since he was 11. He's integral part of the team. It's very nice to see him grow, be in a position now that he's fighting for a championship at such a young age, the talent he has.

"On the other side, George, who's been with us since he was 17. Someone that I feel a lot of, how can I say, emotions for and compassion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the F1 Show podcast, Naomi Schiff discusses what George Russell can do now after his 'gut-wrenching' DNF.

"We are very close. We spend time with Carmen and Susie off the track with each other. If people would see that we're traveling together, we're having coffee in the same coffee shop, we're going in a gym.

"That's why it's pretty annoying to have some lunatics that have no understanding really about how relationships work coming up with these kind of accusations. I don't pay any attention to this.

"Most important is that George knows how the team is, and Kimi knows, and we will always try to give them equal opportunity."

Sports.title: Weekend Winners: Kate, Sam and Declan have their say on Silver Trophy
Sports.content:
Kate Tracey, Sam Boswell and Declan Rix reconvene to discuss the best betting angles for the feature Handicap Hurdle at Chepstow on Saturday, the Silver Trophy.

Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies will be hoping that Masked Man can win at this fixture for the second year in a row as he heads the market for another ultra-competitive renewal of the Silver Trophy at Chepstow.

Attheraces.com's Declan Rix

"I'm siding with the Double Green-owned machine that is Masked Man for Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies. He won at this meeting last year making his first run under rules, he was competitive in all of them starts last season and they even chanced him in the Grade One at Aintree.

"His trainer combination are flying at the minute, with a 50 per cent strike rate and I know he is favourite, but he is still a good price and will be ready to go for this."

Host Kate Tracey

"I went to Olly Murphy's last week for a stable tour and the first horse and the one he kept mentioning was Daylatedollarshort with Sean Bowen on. He showed progression in handicaps after being a little bit disappointing in his career.

"He ran an almighty race at the Punchestown Festival when finishing second. He looked fit and ready to go last week, and he could land the race for the same connections that won this race last year."

BetVictor's Sam Boswell

"Washington is a huge price here. He may be a 10-year-old, but this is his time of year. He loves racing in Wales in October and his record in this month is where he is at his peak.

"He could go well at a massive price for a trainer in Harry Derham, who hasn't been in the winner's enclosure for a while but has provided plenty of placed efforts from his runners so far. He's a good each-way bet at a huge price."

Sports.content:
8m ago 07.49 EDT Women’s World Cup playoff The Republic of Ireland are now 5-0 up away to Kazakhstan, who are down to 10 players after their captain Yulia Myasnikova was sent off. It’s not even half-time. Share Updated at 07.50 EDT

The Oklahoma City Thunder guard has become the latest North American sports star to take an interest in football, following the likes of LeBron James and Tom Brady . “This is a club with a long-standing presence at the top of European football, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. Atletico said the partnership was “grounded in shared values: ambition, excellence and the belief that every result must be earned”. Atletico did not reveal how big a stake 2025 NBA champion and back-to-back NBA MVP Gilgeous-Alexander had taken. “His investment reflects an interest in the club’s long-term vision and international growth,” it said. Kyra Carusa scored twice, with Chloe Mustaki getting the other goal. The winners of this two-legged tie will face either Belgium or Poland for a place in Brazil next summer.
