The review also recommended that measures would be implemented for testing of the software, recognising that opportunities for testing are limited, to make it robust as possible. The FIA , together with the teams and Power Unit Manufacturers (PUMs), will continue to strengthen Power Unit software testing and verification capabilities, enhancing the overall validation process through independent assessment and collaborative feedback, including input from the supplier of the standardised Electronics Control Unit (ECU). The FIA would like to address comments suggesting that the software had not been tested prior to its deployment. Before implementation, teams and Power Unit manufacturers conducted simulation exercises to validate the software package, which was subsequently tested in full-scale running during Free Practice 1 sessions at both the Belgian Grand Prix and the Dutch Grand Prix. On Sunday, the sequence of software installation and integration was as follows: 15:45: The race start procedure was suspended following two formation laps after a number of cars experienced power loss issues. 15:50: Within five minutes of the suspension the FIA technical team had identified the cause of the issue and released an updated Power Unit software configurations designed to address the problem. 16:03: Eighteen minutes after the suspension the FIA provided teams with further technical guidance and clarifications in response to implementation, installation and operation of the revised software configurations.

16:20: Teams and Power Unit manufacturers then completed the integration process, with all competitors ready to start the race approximately 20 minutes later. 16:22: The 10-minutes signal to start the race was issued. 16:33: Cars left the pit lane for the race start procedure. The FIA would like to recognise and thank all stakeholders amongst the teams, Power Unit manufacturers and the FIA technical team for their diligence and responsiveness during the interruption. Their collective efforts enabled the issue to be identified, addressed and resolved, allowing the race to proceed safely.

Sports.title: Bektemir Melikuziev Calls for WBA to Strip Munguia Over Mandatory Snub
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev accused Jaime Munguia of refusing their ordered WBA super middleweight title fight, writing on Instagram Thursday morning that he had accepted concessions on preparation, drug testing, and pay to secure his mandatory shot.

His complaint came before news of Munguia’s proposed October 31 fight against Nikita Zon on the Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli card in Riyadh. Melikuziev’s account raises a question for the champion’s team: what is preventing the mandatory defense if the challenger has accepted everything asked of him?

“I agreed to fight Jaime Munguia on short notice, without a proper training camp. I agreed to fight without VADA testing, even though we have always insisted on it. I even agreed to accept the lowest possible purse or no purse at all,” Melikuziev wrote on Instagram. “We made every concession possible to make this fight happen. And yet, my team has now informed me that Munguia is still refusing to fight me.”

Those are Melikuziev’s claims about the negotiations. His willingness to accept those terms does not establish that an agreement was completed, but it puts pressure on Munguia’s team to explain why another opponent is being pursued.

“So I have one simple question: Why hasn’t a purse bid been ordered? And if the champion refuses to fulfill his mandatory obligation, why hasn’t he been stripped of his title?” Melikuziev wrote.

The WBA gave the teams until October 21 to negotiate, so that deadline has not yet expired. However, Melikuziev is asking the organization to act if Munguia is refusing the ordered defense while pursuing another opponent.

“Stop acting as if there is no mandatory and no rules,” Melikuziev wrote.

Later Thursday, the WBA announced that it had not approved Munguia–Zon and reaffirmed Melikuziev’s status as the official challenger.

Melikuziev further alleged that Munguia wanted more money to face him and offered to stage the fight in Uzbekistan with additional funding. That financial account remains his version of events.

For Munguia, scheduling Zon does not resolve the mandatory. Melikuziev says he has removed every obstacle on his side. Munguia’s team now faces the question of what remains on theirs.

Sports.title: WBA Has Not Approved Jaime Munguia–Nikita Zon Fight
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia’s proposed October 31 fight against Nikita Zon has not received WBA approval, the sanctioning body announced Thursday night, reminding his team that Bektemir Melikuziev remains the mandatory challenger for his super middleweight title.

The statement puts an obstacle in front of the planned Riyadh appearance. Munguia has been named to face Zon, but the WBA has already ordered him to negotiate a defense against Melikuziev.

“The WBA has not approved the Jaime Munguia vs. Nikita Zon bout. Bektemir Melikuziev is the official contender in the super middleweight division,” the organization posted on its official X account on October 8. “The WBA will review the situation.”

That leaves Munguia’s team needing a ruling before it can present the Zon matchup as an approved WBA title defense. The announcement of an opponent has not settled the championship obligation.

The WBA ordered Munguia–Melikuziev on September 21, giving the teams until October 21 to reach an agreement. Its published order stated that Munguia’s 120-day mandatory defense period expired on August 30. If negotiations fail, or either side refuses to negotiate, the championship committee may call a purse bid.

That deadline falls just ten days before the proposed Zon fight. Unless the WBA grants an exception or approves another arrangement, the mandatory order remains an obstacle to Munguia defending his belt against someone else.

Munguia could risk losing his WBA title if he goes ahead with Zon without approval. The organization has already ordered him to negotiate with Melikuziev, and announcing another opponent does not suspend that obligation or stop the October 21 deadline.

Melikuziev should not have to wait indefinitely while Munguia pursues a different fight. He is the mandatory challenger, negotiations have been ordered, and the WBA has publicly confirmed that the proposed Zon defense has not been approved.

The WBA has not announced a stripping decision. However, if Munguia proceeds without an exception, he risks entering the Zon fight with his championship on the line outside the ring.

Sports.title: Iglesias Drops Oliver Zaren Twice, Scores 7th round stoppage
Sports.content:
IBF and IBO super middleweight champion Osleys “El Tornado” Iglesias broke down Oliver “The Great Dane” Zaren, scoring two sixth-round knockdowns before stopping the Danish challenger in the seventh on Thursday at Capitole de Quebec in Quebec City, Canada.

The Cuban southpaw’s first IBF title defense headlined Camille Estephan’s Eye of the Tiger card, streamed on DAZN. Iglesias gradually wore down his larger opponent before turning a one-sided contest into a decisive finish.

Zaren’s size and toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not land enough punches to slow the champion’s attack. Iglesias continued finding him with clean shots, increasing the punishment as the rounds passed.

The sixth was particularly damaging for Zaren. Iglesias put him down twice and left him with a cut over his left eyebrow. The challenger continued into the seventh, but his trainer, former super middleweight champion Mikkel Kessler, threw in the towel to prevent further punishment. The stoppage came at 1:31, with Eddie Claudio refereeing the scheduled 12-round contest.

Iglesias, who is based in Berlin, followed his title-winning victory over Pavel Silyagin with another stoppage. Zaren, from Roskilde, Denmark, showed determination in his first world title challenge, but the fight exposed how much more he needed offensively to compete with the champion.

Wilkens Mathieu Takes Split Decision Over Vladimir Shishkin

In the co-feature, Montreal’s Wilkens Mathieu retained his NABF super middleweight title with a split-decision victory over Vladimir Shishkin in a 10-round contest.

Two judges scored the fight 98-92 for Mathieu, while the third favored Shishkin 97-93. The divided scoring reflected a fight in which Shishkin’s boxing skills gave Mathieu considerably more to deal with than Iglesias faced in the main event.

Mathieu looked for heavy punches but did not always follow them with enough regular work, allowing Shishkin to compete through his more measured boxing. Steve St-Germain was the referee.

Dzmitry Asanau Outpoints Luis Santana

Dzmitry “The Wasp” Asanau defeated Montreal’s Luis Santana by unanimous decision over 10 rounds at lightweight, adding Santana’s NABF title to his IBF Intercontinental and WBC Continental Americas belts.

Asanau dropped Santana with a left jab to the chin in the third round. The judges scored the bout 98-91 twice and 97-92. Junior Padulo Jr. refereed.

Imam Khataev Knocks Out Padraig McCrory

NABF light heavyweight champion Imam Khataev needed just 69 seconds to knock out Belfast’s Padraig “The Hammer” McCrory in their scheduled 10-round bout.

Khataev landed a left hook to the head that dropped McCrory, who could not beat the count. Junior Padulo Jr. was the referee.

Leila Beaudoin Wins Every Round On The Cards

Leila Beaudoin, of Lévis, Quebec, defeated Argentina’s Brisa “La China” Alfonzo by unanimous decision in their 10-round super featherweight contest.

Beaudoin dropped Alfonzo with a body shot in the sixth round, with the challenger taking an eight-count before continuing. All three judges scored the fight 100-89. Alain Villeneuve refereed.

Daylen Pepin Stops Matias Pinilla

Quebec’s Daylen Pepin stopped Chile’s Matias Pinilla at 2:59 of the fourth round in their lightweight contest.

A flurry from Pepin brought the finish in the round’s final seconds. Jeff Topping was the referee.

Jacob Blais Defeats Yoan Trottier

Montreal welterweight Jacob Blais earned a unanimous decision over Quebec City’s Yoan Trottier in a four-round bout.

Trottier suffered a cut over his right eyebrow in the second round. All three judges scored the contest 40-36 for Blais, with Jeff Topping refereeing.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Batters Oliver Zaren Into Seventh-Round Stoppage
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias slowly battered his larger challenger Oliver Zaren into a seventh-round stoppage on Thursday night, retaining his IBF and IBO super middleweight titles at Théâtre Capitole in Quebec City.

Zaren’s trainer, former champion Mikkel Kessler, threw in the towel in the seventh after watching his fighter absorb sustained punishment. The Dane’s toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not produce enough offense to change its direction.

Iglesias (16-0, 15 KOs) had to work longer than he has against some of his previous opponents, steadily breaking Zaren down rather than ending the contest with an early knockout. The challenger took the shots and continued trying, giving the Cuban time to demonstrate how effectively he can wear down an opponent who doesn’t go away immediately.

“I hope the winner [Canelo-Mbilli] faces me. I’d like my next fight to be a Unification,” said Iglesias about wanting to fight the winner of the October 31st fight between WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli and Canelo Alvarez.

Zaren looked bigger, but that size did little to slow Iglesias. The champion controlled the contest and landed cleanly, increasing his output as the rounds passed. Zaren was spending too much of the fight absorbing punches without delivering enough back to make Iglesias hesitate.

That was the difference between surviving and competing. Zaren remained on his feet, but there was little reason to expect the fight to turn in his favor. Kessler eventually made the decision his fighter’s durability had delayed, preventing further punishment in a contest that had become one-sided.

The 26-year-old Zaren (19-1-1, 8 KOs) entered his first world title challenge ranked fifth by the IBF. His unbeaten record had been built without a victory over a leading super middleweight, and Iglesias exposed how much more was required at championship level.

For Iglesias, 28, this was his first IBF defense after winning the vacant belt against Pavel Silyagin in April. He has now stopped Vladimir Shishkin, Silyagin and Zaren in consecutive fights.

Bigger names remain the next test. Zaren gave Iglesias rounds and showed considerable toughness, but he never forced the champion to fight on his terms. Iglesias leaves Quebec with another challenger worn down and another stoppage on his record.

Sports.title: Wilkens Mathieu Takes Split Verdict Over Vladimir Shishkin
Sports.content:
Wilkens Mathieu retained his NABF super middleweight title with a disputed split-decision win over Vladimir Shishkin on Thursday night, with many viewers believing the veteran’s boxing skills deserved the verdict at the Capitole de Québec.

Two judges scored the ten-round fight 98-92 for Mathieu, while the third favored Shishkin 97-93. The bout was the co-feature on the Eye of the Tiger card headlined by Osleys Iglesias against Oliver Zaren, streamed on DAZN.

Mathieu, 21, spent too much of the fight loading up on punches rather than letting his hands go with quicker shots. He looked for power when a steadier flow of punches and combinations could have helped him build his offense.

That approach gave Shishkin time to read his attacks and use his experience. The 35-year-old former world-title challenger applied pressure and made Mathieu work, producing stretches where his power punches quieted the hometown crowd.

Shishkin’s skills were a major part of the difficulty. Mathieu had the younger legs, but the veteran showed that youth and punching power do not automatically overcome an opponent who knows how to interrupt an attack and make his own work count.

Mathieu had his successes and finished strongly in the tenth. However, many fans felt Shishkin had already done enough to win. The disagreement was about who deserved the decision, rather than simply whether Mathieu had faced a tougher fight than expected.

The two 98-92 totals were especially striking. Both judges gave Mathieu eight rounds, a wide margin for a fight in which Shishkin repeatedly troubled him. The third judge’s 97-93 score for Shishkin reflected a very different reading of the action.

Mathieu entered following an eighth-round stoppage of Olympic silver medalist Esquiva Falcao in June at the same venue. Shishkin brought experience from his IBF title defeat against William Scull and his stoppage loss to Iglesias.

The result keeps Mathieu moving toward bigger fights at 168 pounds, but his performance leaves questions about that pace. Against better opposition, loading up without enough punches between the power shots could cost him rounds that he cannot recover with a strong finish.

Sports.title: Imam Khataev Demolishes Padraig McCrory In One Round
Sports.content:
Imam Khataev demolished Padraig McCrory in the first round Thursday night, retaining his NABF light heavyweight title with a knockout at 1:09 at the Théâtre Capitole in Quebec City.

The Olympic bronze medalist needed little more than a minute to end the scheduled 10-round contest on the DAZN-streamed Eye of the Tiger card headlined by Osleys Iglesias against Oliver Zaren. Khataev improves to 13-1 with 12 knockouts, while McCrory drops to 20-3 with 10 KOs.

A left hand to the side of McCrory’s head put the Belfast fighter down, leaving him unable to beat the count. The broadcast commentary described the punch as affecting his equilibrium. Although McCrory’s reaction briefly suggested a body shot, the damage was attributed to the head punch.

There was no opportunity for McCrory to work his way back into the fight. Khataev’s power settled it before the challenger could establish anything, turning what was supposed to be a full night’s work into another short appearance.

The result gives Khataev his third consecutive victory since losing a split decision to David Morrell in July 2025. He had already stopped Adam Deines and Mickael Diallo during that rebuilding run.

McCrory was a substantial underdog, and the speed of the finish showed how little room he had for error against a puncher like Khataev. Coming out of a brief retirement after a June farewell victory, he found himself facing an opponent whose power was far beyond what that comeback win had prepared him for.

Khataev handled the opponent in front of him, but this was too brief to reveal much about his development since the Morrell defeat. His punching power was already established. The next useful test would be someone who can survive those early exchanges and force him to make adjustments over several rounds.

That is the challenge for his handlers now. Another quick knockout keeps Khataev moving, but tougher opposition would give a clearer picture of how close he is to another fight against a leading light heavyweight.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Targets Opetaia, Beterbiev, Usyk and Fury
Sports.content:
David Benavidez laid out a wish list featuring Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, Oleksandr Usyk and Tyson Fury, but his willingness to skip ahead to Usyk shows how quickly his cruiserweight plans could change.

“We got two great fights at cruiserweight before we get up there first,” Benavidez said to Inside Ring Show. “We got Jai Opetaia, then I think Beterbiev is going to come up to cruiserweight.” “If we can get a fight in with Usyk and Tyson Fury, then that’s something I’m willing to do.”

Benavidez appears to smell the money available at heavyweight. He describes his ambitions as a search for greatness, but Usyk and Fury also offer the possibility of enormous paydays. His interest extends beyond spending years building a cruiserweight reign.

The proposed sequence assumes plenty. Benavidez would need to secure those fights and win them to keep building toward the next one. Opetaia could derail that route through his southpaw combinations, movement, and experience at 200 pounds.

Beterbiev brings another threat, although Benavidez says there is interest from the other side.

“Beterbiev has definitely reached out to our team, and he’s been actively trying to make that fight,” he said.

That is more concrete than simply naming an opponent, but it still leaves the weight, timing, and agreement unresolved.

More revealing was Benavidez’s response to the possibility of Opetaia fighting Deontay Wilder. Rather than waiting, he suggested taking his business straight to heavyweight.

“If we can’t get that fight for Cinco de Mayo with Jai Opetaia, then we’ll do it with Usyk.”

That would be a substantial leap. Usyk’s movement and accuracy would test whether Benavidez could apply his pressure against an elite heavyweight. Fury’s size and reach would create a different set of difficulties.

Benavidez’s ambition is clear. What remains uncertain is how much of this list he can turn into reality. Naming four major opponents is easy compared with negotiating the fights and beating the men across from him.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol’s Vanishing Hunger Exposed
Sports.content:
Dmitry Bivol knows who he wants in the ring, but he is in no rush to lock down a contract. During an appearance on Inside the Ring, the champion singled out Artur Beterbiev, Canelo Alvarez, plus David Benavidez as his top targets. Still, he refused to pick one or name a date.

“This is Beterbiev, this is Canelo, and this is Benavidez,” Bivol said to Inside Ring Show. “This is three most big fights, I think, for me now.”

Bivol has the names ready. What is missing is any real urgency to get these bouts signed.

When asked about completing the Beterbiev trilogy by May, Bivol mentioned he would accept that timeline if all sides agreed. He pointed out that past talks hit roadblocks. That leaves fans with another vague target instead of a firm date. Waiting longer simply means Beterbiev gets older.

They split their previous two bouts. Unfinished business remains. Delaying the rubber match alters the physical test. While that does not prove Bivol wants to age his rival out, the advantage definitely leans his way.

Targeting Canelo makes pure financial sense. Bivol dominated their first clash, neutralizing the smaller boxer with ease. A return bout promises massive money against someone whose style he already mastered. Extra ring wear on Canelo only tilts the odds further in Bivol’s favor.

Benavidez offers a totally unique puzzle. Yet Bivol gave zero clues about when he wants that clash. He never clarified if he would jump to cruiserweight either.

Looking at other belts produced similar noncommittal answers. Bivol talked about how tough it feels jumping from 175 to 200 pounds, but skipped any mention of challenging Jai Opetaia.

His back surgery definitely plays a role in camp routines. He admits he must train smarter these days, which makes total sense. Even so, the core mystery lingers. Which major challenge does he actually want next?

Right now, Bivol is focusing entirely on Callum Smith. Past that date, his big plans stay strictly hypothetical. Something has changed with Bivol since his rematch with Beterbiev in February 2025. That twelfth round against Beterbiev took something out of him that a doctor cannot fix.

Bivol can talk all he wants about back rehabilitation and careful training camps, but the hesitation in his matchmaking tells the real story. When a fighter gets dragged into deep water, absorbs damage, and feels the fight slipping away beneath him with seconds left on the clock, it changes his wiring. Bivol survived that final barrage to collect the decision, but he walked away knowing exactly how violent that rivalry is. The appetite to jump straight back in with Beterbiev or any tough opponent has vanished.

Putting Canelo and Benavidez on a public wishlist is standard diversion. Canelo is a safe, massive payday against an opponent Bivol already solved without breaking a sweat. Benavidez is locked into cruiserweight campaigns, giving Bivol the perfect out to claim weight disparities prevent the bout. Meanwhile, Beterbiev is on the other side of forty, yet Bivol will not commit to a date to finish business.

Taking the Callum Smith fight while slow-walking the rubber match proves the point. Bivol went from an active technician hunting undisputed status to a cautious champion protecting his brand. When an elite boxer starts looking for reasons not to fight the very guys who tested his chin, the hunger is gone.

Ghana News.title: Ato Forson has performed wonders with common fund releases – Northern Regional Minister
Ghana News.content:
Northern Regional Minister, Ali Adolf John, has praised Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson for what he describes as a remarkable improvement in the release of the District Assemblies Common Fund to Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies.

Speaking at a meeting with Regional Ministers, Metropolitan Municipal District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) and Coordinating Directors in Tamale, the Northern Regional Minister said assemblies were now receiving significant releases under President John Dramani Mahama’s government, a development he said had brought relief and excitement to local authorities.

“The Common Fund that comes to the various assemblies, tell me in the history of Ghana when have you ever experienced such quantum of monies coming to the assembly?” he asked.

According to him, many MMDCEs are happy about the level of support reaching their assemblies, especially those who have taken time to understand the difficulties previous district chief executives faced in accessing funds for development.

“Our MMDCEs who are here are very happy about what is happening in their assemblies, especially those of them who have taken the pain to know from those of us who have been DCEs before what we went through,” he said.

He noted that in the past, assemblies struggled to receive even the limited amounts promised to them, particularly over the last eight years.

“The monies that used to come, and especially in the past eight years, the money that was even promised them, that peanut that was promised them, was not even coming,” he stated.

The Northern Regional Minister said the situation had changed under President Mahama and Dr. Forson’s stewardship at the Ministry of Finance.

“But under John Dramani Mahama’s government, under the ministership of Dr. Ato Forson, we have seen wonders being performed. We are very, very happy about what we are experiencing so far,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Zelensky accuses US of inaction as Russian strikes kill over 70 in two days
Ghana News.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the US of ​being unwilling to help Ukraine after a Russian bomb attack on Thursday killed at least 35 people in the east, sending the two-day death toll ‌from Russian strikes to over 70.

Hours after the strike on the embattled city of Kramatorsk tore through two buses, Zelensky criticised Washington's effort to pursue economic ties with Russia while also seeking to mediate the more than four-year war.

City authorities reported a new drone attack in the evening that killed two people. That brought to 35 the total death toll in the city.

Local authorities reported that a Russian guided aerial bomb ​killed two people in a village in southeastern Dnipropetrovsk and one person died in the western city of Ivano-Frankivsk.

The attacks were launched a day after a mass ​Russian drone and missile assault killed dozens across Ukraine — 22 of them in a residential building in the central town of Pryluky, around ⁠130 km (80 miles) east of Kyiv.

Speaking in the early evening, Zelensky said 78 people were killed and 215 wounded by strikes in the last two days across Ukraine.

Speaking to reporters ​in Pryluky, the Ukrainian leader urged the US to accede to his requests to expand Ukraine's access to the Starlink satellite service to help it target Russian ballistic-missile launchers.

'THAT'S CALLED UNWILLINGNESS'

"Open ​Starlink for Ukraine. You did open it when you were responding to Iran ... I’ve said quite openly — give it to us, help us defend our skies and dominate there. And then Putin will sit down at the negotiating table," he said in an emotional statement.

Ukraine has in recent months aimed to wrest the battlefield initiative from Russia, whose gains have slowed this year, but is still suffering from Moscow's increasingly ​brutal air war.

"So where's the truth here, where's the honesty? Where's the stalemate? ... That's called unwillingness," he said, referring to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's assertion earlier on Thursday ​that the war is at a stalemate and that the United States would keep working toward a settlement.

"One cannot, on the one hand, negotiate with the Russians about future economic projects, whilst on the other ‌hand say that ⁠we find ourselves in some sort of ... diplomatic stalemate," Zelensky added.

Top Russian and US officials, including US Special Envoy Jared Kushner, have held talks about bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that delivered Russian gas to Germany before Moscow invaded Ukraine, Reuters reported on Thursday. Ukrainian negotiators will travel to the US on Friday and Saturday for talks, Zelenskiy added, urging US President Donald Trump to increase sanction pressure on Russia.

Zelenskiy told reporters in Kyiv that he expected Kyiv's European partners to join the talks with the US. He also said Ukrainian negotiators would ​raise the issue of air defences in ​light of near-constant Russian attacks.

INTENSIFYING STRIKES

Twenty people ⁠were wounded in the Kramatorsk strike — one of the biggest single attacks of the year by Russia. Moscow has denied targeting civilians, but regularly pounds cities with missiles and drones.

"The Russians are deliberately targeting civilians. For them, a bus full of passengers is an attractive target precisely ​because a single strike can kill as many people as possible," regional governor Vadym Filashkin said on the Telegram app.

Images posted by ​officials showed bodies strewn across ⁠a street littered with debris and a charred shell of a bus. Some bodies had not been identified yet, Zelenskiy said, adding that the attack would not go unanswered.

Separately, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said four people were killed and 19 wounded in morning attacks on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv. Water and electricity supplies were subject to interruptions which officials said would take time to put ⁠right.

Russia has ​unleashed relentless drone strikes against Kyiv in recent weeks, targeting warehouses, data centres and renewing its campaign against ​Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter.

Russian technology and AI company Yandex said it could not yet determine whether equipment at a data centre hit by a Ukrainian drone attack could be restored. Zelensky did not refer specifically to the ​strike on Yandex, but said Ukraine was "mirroring" Russian attacks on data centres.

Ghana News.title: Bipartisan majority of Americans blame Trump policies for rising costs, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
Ghana News.content:
Some 78% of Americans blame President Donald Trump's policies for rising prices that are outpacing their earnings, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that found majorities of Republicans and Democrats citing the cost of living as their top concern ​ahead of next month's midterm elections.

Fifty-seven percent of Trump's Republicans said that costs have been growing faster than their paychecks, a stark example of how his pursuit of import tariffs, war with Iran ‌and other policies have clashed with a central 2024 campaign promise to kill inflation and lower prices "on day one."

Inflation instead has increased, to the point where the US Federal Reserve has pivoted to rate hikes to quell price increases policymakers have attributed to a variety of factors, including rising global energy costs following the start of the Iran war, and the administration's imposition of aggressive import taxes.

Concerns about the economy and the war have driven Trump's public approval to record lows and have been weighing onsupport for his party ahead of the November 3 election that will ​determine control of Congress for the next two years.

About one in four Republicans disapproved of Trump's handling of the economy, a view shared by 63% of independents and 92% of Democrats. Disapproval was even sharper when ​it came to inflation, with 68% of all respondents and 40% of Republicans dissatisfied.

Jeffrey Talley, 65, a retired bank examiner from Mission Hills, Kansas, is a registered Republican, who ⁠said he voted for Trump in 2016 but not in 2020 or 2024 and now plans to vote for Democrat Adam Hamilton in what has become an unexpectedly competitive Senate race in the state.

"I'm pretty much against all the nonsense that's ​going on in the Middle East with the Iran war, and pushing up the price of gasoline ... that's been very disheartening," said Talley. He views the election as a chance to elect "somebody to put a check and balance on the craziness ​that's going on in the White House."

The six-day Reuters/Ipsos poll, conducted online and nationwide and completed on Monday, gathered responses from 4,506 US adults. It had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for Americans in general and 3 points for Republicans, Democrats and independents.

'EVERYTHING HAS GONE UP'

The national average price of a gallon of gasoline was $4.36 on Thursday compared with $3.11 a year ago, while diesel fuel prices stood at $6.28 after a record run-up perhaps felt deepest in farm states including Kansas.

Another Kansan, 41-year-old Athena Barrett of Kansas City, said Trump's performance had motivated ​her to register to vote because "I don't really like what the president is doing."

"Gas prices ... food prices, the cost of living -- everything has gone up; what's going on with Iran, and all the stuff with immigration," said Barrett, who ​is Hispanic.

Hispanic voters supported Trump in large numbers in 2024, but polls have shown support eroding.

White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said Trump had ended the "inflation crisis" of his predecessor in office, Democrat Joe Biden, by boosting the economy with tax cuts and lowering the ‌costs of prescription ⁠drugs. "The president has delivered tangible wins for American families," Rogers said by email.

Inflation spiked to a 40-year high during Biden's term and played an important role in Trump's 2024 election victory.

Its persistence, albeit off the highs of the COVID pandemic, has meant higher daily prices for things like gas, ground beef and airline tickets as well as higher interest rates. The 30-year home mortgage is now at 7.5%, double what homebuyers were used to just six years ago.

Poll respondents cited the cost of living as a top issue in their decisions on how to vote, with 54% of respondents, including 40% of Republicans, saying they felt it had increased a lot in the last year, compared with 30% who said it was up only a little and 10% ​who said it was unchanged.

Some 78% of the respondents - including ​64% of Republicans and 76% of independents - said some ⁠blame lies with the White House, with most Americans viewing tariffs as an important cause of higher prices.

LITTLE HIT TO SPENDING

The poll provided only limited indications of people cutting back on spending. Some 63% of respondents said they were eating out at restaurants less often, and 56% said they were spending less on entertainment or streaming services.

Smaller shares said they ​were driving less or falling behind on bills.

Economic data does show Americans in general still making modest gains in their income, even after accounting for taxes and rising ​prices. Overall hourly wage gains are ⁠growing roughly in line with the consumer price index, meaning much of any growth in pay is eaten up in higher prices, the type of treading water that can sour attitudes about the state of the economy.

Surveys of consumer confidence by both the Conference Board and the New York Federal Reserve have reflected a dim outlook.

Some of Trump's policies still resonate: 45% of respondents said unauthorized immigration was a root cause of higher prices, echoing the argument made by the administration that people in the country illegally ⁠create extra demand ​for things like housing, pushing up costs.

Herman Sims, 67, of Dallas, has voted Republican since 2012, and plans to continue doing so in a ​close Senate race between Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico even though he works for a trucking company hit hard by high diesel prices.

While he said he disagreed with Trump's decision to go to war with Iran, he would not vote for a Democrat: "What I've seen ​with the Democratic Party is they care more about themselves and will tell you anything, but they're more about spending."

Ghana News.title: New Trump rules will make it harder for farmers to access US funds for energy projects
Ghana News.content:
President Donald Trump's looming changes to ​a rural energy program that has distributed billions of dollars in recent years will make it harder for many farmers to access funds ‌for such things as solar arrays and energy efficiency projects, farmers, energy companies and analysts said.

It is Trump's latest move to slash government support for renewable energy. While working on the changes, the administration had halted applications this year for the Department of Agriculture's Rural Energy for America Program, or REAP.

In the last decade, REAP has helped fund more than 19,000 energy projects by ​American farmers and small business owners, according to the National Sustainable Agriculture Coalition. The projects include solar and wind installations, manure biodigesters and energy efficiency ​upgrades.

Between 2014 and 2025, REAP invested more than $4.8 billion across grants and loan guarantees in renewable energy and energy efficiency ⁠projects, NSAC's analysis of USDA data said.

Since the US Congress authorized REAP in 2008, the program has allowed farmers who had not yet broken ground on ​a project to apply for grants covering as much as half the cost. But under changes released last week and effective October 16, farmers cannot apply for ​funding until they complete a project and demonstrate one year of energy savings.

Farmers have been hit hard this year by Trump's tariff policies and higher costs of fuel and fertilizer, and most will find it difficult to access the program, said Richa Patel, policy specialist at NSAC, noting REAP projects can cost several thousand to hundreds of thousands of dollars.

"For a lot of farmers, that ​just simply won’t be possible, especially with these times already being so financially uncertain," Patel said.

A USDA spokesperson said the changes to REAP "are intended to help ​the program pay for actual production and results of projects, not just projections."

PROGRAM HAD BEEN PAUSED

The Trump administration halted REAP applications this year as it worked to rewrite program regulations, and ‌last year ⁠it restricted eligibility for solar projects. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said solar was taking up prime farmland needed for crops.

Nearly 64% of REAP projects since 2017 were solar arrays, according to USDA data, enabling farms and other rural businesses to generate their own power and save on utility bills.

REAP has historically been a bipartisan, widely supported program, said Ann Mesnikoff, federal legislative director at the Environmental Law & Policy Center, which sued the Trump administration in September for its changes to REAP's solar eligibility.

More ​than two thirds of REAP grants have ​gone to recipients in Congressional districts ⁠held by Republicans, according to a Brookings Institution analysis of federal data published last year.

The program was so popular that Veronica McFadden in 2023 left her job with a solar company to start an Iowa-based business dedicated to helping farmers apply ​for REAP grants. Business has dried up since the program stalled and in August she was forced to lay off ​all five of ⁠her employees.

McFadden is uncertain whether many of her clients will be able to take advantage of the program under the new rules.

"Now it's much riskier," McFadden said of the rules unveiled last week. "And for small farmers, particularly young farmers ...they may not be able to do this, pay it all upfront."

McFadden recently helped Michigan dairy farmer Ron Rusk apply ⁠for a ​REAP grant to help fund an $85,000 ground-mounted solar project to provide about 80% of his farm's electricity, ​which he hoped would help him pass the farm on to his son.

"It would be a nice asset for him to have going forward to make this operation economically viable, which is not ​always the case," said Rusk, whose grant was never awarded.

Ghana News.title: John Jinapor warns energy sector board chairs, CEOs against toxic working relationships
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor

The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has warned board chairpersons and chief executives of state-owned energy institutions that strained working relationships and internal conflicts could cost them their positions, even when they deliver results.

He said effective teamwork, mutual respect and accountability were essential to improving institutional performance, urging appointees to put aside personal differences and work together to achieve the government’s energy sector objectives.

Dr Jinapor gave the warning at the 2026 Energy Sector Performance Review Retreat, organised by the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition at Volta Seren Hotel in Ho from October 7 to 10. He reminded the officials that their appointments were temporary and that no one was above accountability.

“Anybody who thinks he’s untouchable, please, you are making a big mistake,” he cautioned, stressing that executive authority rested with President John Dramani Mahama, who appoints ministers and, through the appropriate processes, board members and chief executives to implement government policies.

The Minister warned that disagreements between board chairs and chief executives, as well as tensions between executives and their deputies, could undermine institutional performance. He urged chief executives to respect their boards and obtain the necessary approvals before making major financial commitments, while board members must provide effective oversight. Deputies, he added, should support their superiors rather than undermine their authority.

Dr Jinapor said he hoped the government would not have to dissolve any more boards during his tenure, calling on appointees to improve their working relationships and remain focused on delivering results. He said collaboration and accountability were necessary to ensure that state-owned energy institutions fulfilled their mandates.

Government plans 3,000 transformers to address power distribution challenges

The Minister also outlined measures to address electricity distribution challenges, including the procurement of approximately 3,000 transformers following a shortage of about 600 at the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG).

He said some of the transformers had already been deployed to improve power distribution, while the government was working with the Ministry of Finance to mobilise US$500 million for investment in the transmission network.

Dr Jinapor commended GRIDCo and the Volta River Authority (VRA) for restoring power in record time following the August 1 incident, which resulted in the loss of approximately 1,000 megawatts of electricity. He said the incident exposed weaknesses in the transmission system and underscored the need for modern infrastructure, including an interim containerised substation and a planned ultra-modern transmission infrastructure and control centre.

On electricity generation, he cautioned against investments that could create unnecessary financial pressure, saying decisions must be guided by actual demand, available capacity and affordability. He added that the government was working with the VRA to restore idle power plants to service.

Jinapor urges ECG to improve revenue collection as IPP payments rise

Dr Jinapor has urged ECG to improve its billing and revenue collection efficiency as the government works to strengthen the financial position of the electricity distribution company.

He said most Independent Power Producers (IPPs) were now receiving nearly 100 per cent of their bills, compared with about 40 per cent when the current administration assumed office. He also welcomed plans to engage private sector operators in meter reading and billing, with payments made electronically.

The Minister argued that greater investment in locally owned power generation companies could help retain more revenue within Ghana and reduce pressure on the cedi. He said improving revenue mobilisation was important to sustaining the power sector and meeting its financial obligations.

Jinapor cites TOR turnaround as example of effective leadership

Dr Jinapor has commended the management of the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) for reviving the facility without seeking financial support from the government, describing its progress as an example of what effective leadership and teamwork could achieve.

He said the refinery’s turnaround demonstrated that state-owned enterprises could overcome significant challenges through commitment, innovation and cooperation.

The Minister also expressed optimism about Ghana’s petroleum sector, saying the decline in production recorded in previous years had been halted. He attributed the improved outlook to renewed investor interest and agreements with companies expected to undertake further exploration and drilling activities.

He urged leaders across the energy sector to sustain the progress and work collectively towards building a reliable, affordable, sustainable and resilient energy sector capable of supporting Ghana’s economic transformation.

Ghana News.title: Recover, protect and properly account for every cedi of public money – Finance Minister
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Finance, Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson, has called for a renewed of national commitment to recover, protect and properly account for every cedi of public money.

Speaking in Tamale at an engagement on the 2025 Auditor-General’s Report with Regional Ministers, Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives, Dr. Forson said Ghana could no longer afford waste in the management of public resources.

The engagement, held under the theme “Recovering Every Cedi”, brought together key regional and local government leaders to strengthen financial accountability, improve compliance and ensure that public funds are used strictly for their intended purposes.

“Ladies and gentlemen, Ghana does not have the luxury of wasting public resources. Every cedi already has a job waiting for it,” Dr. Forson said.

“It can buy medicine, repair a classroom, desilt a drain, improve a market or maintain a feeder road. So, when a cedi is wasted, left uncollected or poorly spent, somebody, somewhere, loses a service.”

The Finance Minister said the theme must go beyond a conference slogan and become a practical discipline across all levels of government.

“That is why ‘Recovering Every Cedi’ cannot remain just a slogan on today’s banner. It must become a way of working: collect what is due; protect what is collected; spend what is approved; account for what is spent; recover what is owed; and prevent it from happening again,” he stated.

Dr. Forson stressed that financial accountability is not only about compliance with audit rules, but about protecting services that directly affect the lives of citizens. He said public funds must translate into visible improvements in communities, including better schools, roads, health facilities, markets, drainage systems and local infrastructure.

He urged Regional Ministers, MMDCEs and Coordinating Directors to take audit findings seriously, recover funds where necessary, close loopholes and strengthen internal controls to prevent future losses.

The meeting was attended by several Regional Ministers, including the Northern Regional Minister, Ali Adolf John; Savannah Regional Minister, Salisu Be-Awuribe Issifu; North East Regional Minister, Ibrahim Tia; Upper West Regional Minister, Puozuing Charles Lwanga; Oti Regional Minister, John Kwadwo Gyapong; and Upper East Regional Minister, Akamugri Donatus Atanga.

Ghana News.title: GTA denies collecting money for US, Canada visas ahead of 2026 World Cup
Ghana News.content:
CEO of GTA, Maame Efua Houadjeto

The Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) has denied collecting money from applicants in exchange for visas or visa opportunities linked to Ghana’s tourism promotion activities during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

In a press statement issued on October 9, 2026, the Authority said its involvement was limited to identifying participants, facilitating institutional introductions and providing guidance on visa application procedures.

It explained that the initiative, which was approved by its Board, sought to showcase Ghana’s tourism, culture, music, fashion, crafts and creative industries to international audiences.

The GTA said it engaged the United States Embassy and the Canadian High Commission to seek guidance on visa requirements for participants but had no authority to issue visas or influence application outcomes.

“At no point did GTA possess the authority to issue visas, guarantee visa approvals or determine the outcomes of individual applications,” the statement said, adding that such decisions rested exclusively with the respective diplomatic and immigration authorities.

The Authority further explained that proposed private-sector sponsorship proved impracticable due to the substantial financial requirements, prompting participants to bear their own visa application fees, travel and accommodation expenses.

It also denied collecting money for visa opportunities, stating: “The Ghana Tourism Authority unequivocally denies collecting money from any applicant in return for visas or visa opportunities.”

It urged the public to distinguish payments made to independent travel service providers from payments to the Authority or its officials.

Ghana News.title: GTA CEO Maame Efua Houadjeto denies involvement in World Cup visa scandal
Ghana News.content:
CEO of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), Maame Efua Houadjeto

The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), Maame Efua Houadjeto, has denied personal involvement in the sale of visas or the collection of money from applicants in exchange for visa opportunities linked to Ghana’s tourism promotion activities for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

In a press statement issued on Friday, October 9, 2026, she said her involvement in the initiative was part of her official responsibilities and the Authority’s mandate to promote Ghana as a tourism destination.

The programme was intended to showcase the country’s tourism, culture, music, fashion, crafts and creative industries to international audiences during the tournament.

“As the CEO of the GTA, I firmly deny any personal involvement in the sale of visas or the collection of money from applicants in exchange for visa opportunities,” she stated.

She explained that the Authority engaged the United States Embassy and the Canadian High Commission to seek guidance on visa application requirements but had no power to guarantee approvals or determine the outcome of applications.

The statement also defended the inclusion of bloggers, social media influencers, digital content creators, photographers and videographers in the programme, arguing that tourism promotion extends beyond conventional journalism.

“The professional relevance of participants should be assessed against their intended functions and promotional responsibilities rather than exclusively against conventional journalism classifications,” it said.

The CEO added that the circumstances surrounding the programme should be assessed using verified facts, institutional records and the distinct responsibilities of the parties involved.

The scandal, which is currently a subject of investigation, has led to the suspension of the Director-General of the National Sports Authority, Yaw Ampofo Ankrah.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
