World.title: Saudi Arabia reopens Riyadh airport after Houthi attack kills three
World.content:
Saudi Arabia has seen several attacks by the Houthis in recent days, with the airports appearing to be the primary target.

Saudi Arabia has reopened Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport following attacks by the Houthis that killed three people and injured several.

In a statement on social media on Friday, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said attacks the previous day had hit airport facilities and an aircraft belonging to state carrier Saudia.

The Houthis have hit Saudi airports in several attacks this week as the armed group continues to face an offensive by the Riyadh-backed internationally recognised Yemen government.

The strikes on Thursday caused injuries ranging from minor to severe, as well as material damage, GACA said. Airport operations have now resumed and air traffic has returned to normal.

Saudia Airlines said one of its pilots was killed and an aircraft was damaged.

“It is with profound sadness that Saudia announces the passing of Captain Hamoud Ali Alkalthami,” the flag-carrier said in a statement, citing an “incident” at the Riyadh airport.

Saudi Arabia has seen several attacks by the Houthis in recent days, with the airports appearing to be the primary target.

GACA said Wednesday that attacks earlier in the week had killed three civilians and injured 36 at Abha and King Khalid airports. At least three people were also wounded in other attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border.

A Houthi military spokesperson said on Thursday that the armed group had launched a ballistic missile towards King Khalid airport, claiming that the missile had successfully hit its intended target, causing damage and disrupting air traffic.



The campaign appears to be a revival of a tactic seen last month.

On September 18, Saudi-led coalition forces said they intercepted and destroyed a suspected Houthi ballistic missile fired towards King Khalid airport.

A day later, at least one explosion was heard near the airport in Riyadh, and a large plume of black smoke was seen rising from a fuel storage area.

The Houthis have warned aviation companies to avoid using Saudi airspace, saying any aircraft operating in there, except over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, is a target.

‘Substantial forces’

The return to the attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports comes as Yemeni forces continue a counteroffensive against the Houthis.

The push was launched after the Iran-aligned rebel group last month seized a broad swath of territory along the strategic Bab al-Mandeb strait, which connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, in a sudden push.

The Yemeni government forces this week claimed key gains around the Bab al-Mandeb coastline, but intense fighting continues.

The conflict, which was frozen for some years until it was brought back to life by the United States’ war on Iran, has stoked further upheaval in a region already destabilised by Israel’s wars on Gaza and Lebanon.

It now threatens to draw other states into the conflict, with Pakistan and Turkiye having agreed to deploy troops under a mutual defence pact signed with Saudi Arabia earlier this year.

A spokesman for Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Friday that the country now has a “substantial number of forces as well as resources … in Riyadh”.

Pakistani military personnel “would not be crossing the borders of the other side for an attack on the Houthis, but of course (are acting) in the defence of the territory”, he noted.

Rocket launch platforms

The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government said on Friday that it had destroyed three rocket launch platforms that were used by the Houthis “to threaten regional security”.

Spokesman Colonel Turki al-Maliki declared that all Houthi attacks on civilians and civilian facilities “will be met with resolve” by the Saudi-led coalition.

On Thursday, the coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles heading in the direction of Riyadh, and one missile in the direction of the city of Khamis Mushait, close to the Yemeni border.

Earlier in the week, its armed forces carried out 97 “precise targeting operations” against Houthi reinforcements on the Tor al-Baha front and the Taiz axis, using warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles and snipers, it added.

World.title: Real Madrid’s Mourinho lashes out at ‘ridiculous’ criticism of Mbappe
World.content:
Striker takes fire for where and how he has chosen to recover from a knee injury as his return to play could come as early as Saturday.

Share Real Madrid’s Mourinho lashes out at ‘ridiculous’ criticism of Mbappe on social media

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho has slammed criticism of star striker Kylian Mbappe, calling the attacks “ridiculous”.

The French captain has come under fire for spending his time recovering from a left knee injury in France and Switzerland rather than Madrid. He suffered a hyperextension of the joint while playing in a Nations League match against Turkiye on September 25.

The 27-year-old was also pictured at the entrance of a Parisian nightclub and photographed on a bicycle when he was in Switzerland.

Some fans claimed it was a deliberate snubbing of Mourinho, who only days before had said players should avoid skiing or riding bicycles to avoid injury.

“Are these criticisms over the top? They are ridiculous,” Mourinho said at a news conference on Friday on the eve of Real’s La Liga home match with Villarreal.

“All the players who were obliged to be present every day for their recovery were here.

“Mbappe came, like the others, to undergo scans in order to be diagnosed.

“He then went to see a specialist in France because he has history with his knee, which we cannot ignore.”

Mourinho, whose side lost to Atletico Madrid in their last match and already lag six points behind bitter rivals Barcelona, is never one to shy away from a confrontation and tackled each of the criticisms against Mbappe.

“Problems involving football are not sufficient for you,” the 63-year-old Portuguese coach told reporters.

“Therefore, you have raised the issue of the discotheque, which in fact was not one because it was used for a private event for Fashion Week.



“As for the bicycle in Switzerland, it was in a hotel made up of small houses which makes them available so guests can ride to the communal areas, and you would have us believe he was competing in the Tour of Switzerland.”

Mbappe, who returned to training on Wednesday, could feature on the pitch as early as Saturday. Mourinho shrugged off the potential of a hostile reception for Mbappe against Villarreal, reiterating that he was “certain” the all-time World Cup record goal scorer has fulfilled “his obligations to Real Madrid”.

It is not the first time this season that Mbappe has been subjected to attacks by fans.

The Ultras Sur, a Real Madrid supporters group linked to the far right and banned from the Santiago Bernabeu, took issue with him last month.

They were furious that before a Real Madrid match, Mbappe, alongside Vinicius Jr and fellow Frenchman Ibrahima Konate, partially rolled up T-shirts bearing the words “We are all Ceutans“, which was intended to be a message of support for people in the Spanish territory bordering Morocco.

Ceuta, a Spanish North African exclave, has been grappling with a migration crisis.

Mbappe was also criticised earlier this season over his choice of a location for recovery from a previous injury, which led to an online “Mbappe Out” campaign by some Real fans.

World.title: Manchester City charges: Maresca says Premier League club will win appeal
World.content:
Coach Enzo Maresca says he has absolute faith in Man City despite guilty finding over breaches of Premier League financial rules.

Share Man City will win appeal against financial charges, Maresca says on social media

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says he has absolute faith the club will win its appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

In his first news conference since the bombshell announcement last week, the Italian on Friday also rejected any suggestion that City’s haul of silverware over the past 15 years was now tainted.

“I completely trust the club,” said Maresca, who was appointed manager in June but also previously worked at City as part of Pep Guardiola’s coaching staff.

“I trust the club because I trust the people, and this is also the reason why I joined the club. … There is not another club in the world where I would like to be.”

An independent commission found that City had arranged “sham” contracts with a number of their commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.2bn) over nine seasons from 2009 to 2018.

The 10-time English champions, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, are appealing against the judgement.

They likely face a severe points penalty that could lead to relegation or even expulsion from the Premier League if they fail to overturn the verdict.

“The reason why I joined this club is because I completely trust 100 percent the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, all the organisation. So I don’t have any doubt about that,” Maresca said.

“I spoke with the club for sure, and we all [have] trust, and the right moment to speak about that is when we win this appeal.”



Since an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008, City have become the dominant force in English football.

They have won eight Premier League titles, the Champions League and multiple other trophies over the past 15 years.

Maresca, whose side have won all five of their Premier League games this season, rejected the suggestion that those previous successes were now tainted.

“Absolutely not,” the former Chelsea boss said. “I know the effort from the players, from the club, from the manager in that time that was Pep.

“So I know exactly the effort that the club put to achieve that kind of target.”

Maresca to welcome Guardiola’s first return to Man City

Guardiola stepped down at the end of last season after a trophy-laden decade at the Etihad Stadium.

City travel to Liverpool on Sunday for their first outing since the guilty finding, and Guardiola is set to attend their next home game against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.

“After 10 years here, he can come at any time he wants,” Maresca said. “I think it would be nice for him. It would be nice for the fans, for everyone.”

Maresca had spoken to City’s in-house media on Thursday and said the current players “don’t care too much about the noise” currently surrounding the club.

The new head coach and his players, however, are set for a hostile reception when they travel to Anfield, the home of their fierce rivals, but Maresca said his players would stay focused on the match.

“Probably [it] will be even more warm in terms of environment. But the reason why I decided to be manager is for this kind of game,” he said.

“I’m not worried at all. Again, the environment is from the players. It’s nice.

“In this moment, we are top of the league, so the players have all the reasons to be happy and excited.”

World.title: ‘Indentured servants’: US green card move will hit thousands of IT workers
World.content:
The US is suspending top tech firms, including Microsoft, from a key programme to sponsor foreign workers’ green cards.

Share ‘Indentured servants’: US green card move will hit thousands of IT workers on social media

The United States government has moved to exclude some of the world’s top tech companies from a programme that allows them to sponsor skilled foreign workers for permanent residency.

Vice President JD Vance said the action was a response to companies abusing the system to hire lower-paid foreign workers at the expense of US workers.

It comes as US President Donald Trump’s administration continues efforts to clamp down on immigration – both legal and undocumented – and make it harder for immigrants to get residency or citizenship.

But the latest move also potentially impacts thousands of foreign workers, many of whom have spent years waiting for a backlog in applications to clear.

Here’s what to know about the latest policy:

How does the current system work?

The suspension concerns the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme, which enables a US-based employer to sponsor a foreign worker’s green card — as the permanent residency is commonly known. To qualify, the employer is supposed to demonstrate that there are insufficient US workers for a needed job role and that bringing a foreign worker will not impact the pay or conditions of US workers in the industry.

PERM is a key step in the green card process for many skilled foreign workers. Major tech companies often hire workers on temporary visas, such as the H-1B, before they transition to permanent residency through the PERM process.

What have Vance and others said?

Vance on Thursday accused major companies of fraudulently using the current visa regime to displace US employees and bring in lower-paid foreign workers who amount to “indentured servants”.



“The programme has become rife with fraud,” said Vance at a White House news conference. He claimed that many workers who start off on temporary H-1B visas and later apply for permanent residency under the PERM programme are “being mistreated by their employers” and “used to undercut the wages of American workers”.

“You’ve got to hire great American workers,” the US vice president said. “You cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants.”

Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling used similar language, saying the US would “shut down the pipeline of systemic fraud that has flooded our country”.

“The fraud doesn’t end with getting the job,” said Sonderling. “That job becomes a pathway for foreign workers and their families to stay in America permanently and eventually (become) US citizens.”

“And who pays for it all? The American worker,” he said.

Which companies are impacted?

Vance singled out Microsoft as a major offender and said it would be suspended from the PERM programme.

Other companies whose PERM applications will no longer be processed include US software firm Adobe and some of the world’s top IT firms, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. Of these, Capgemini is French, Microsoft and Adobe are American, and the rest — Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCL — are all Indian.

“We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labour certification applications involving these companies,” said Sonderling.

Vance said the suspensions would continue “as long as it needs to”.

Other companies that rely heavily on H-1B visas such as Meta, Amazon or Alphabet’s Google will not be affected.

Have tech firms been abusing US immigration rules?

Critics of the H-1B visa and PERM green card process argue that some employers use the system not to fill legitimate skills shortages, but to reduce labour costs, gain leverage over workers and make it harder for US employees to compete for jobs. They say companies do this by hiring foreign workers at lower wages and manipulating recruitment conditions to keep out qualified US workers.

Vance said Microsoft last year let go 6,000 US workers, while also securing 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards.

“If you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one and a half foreign indentured servants,” said Vance.



Sonderling said companies being suspended from PERM had received more than 230,000 H-1B visas and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications since 2009.

“That’s hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers,” Sonderling said.

The H1-B visa system has also emerged as a lightning rod for many of the most vocal backers of Trump’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement, some of whom have married criticism of the programme with anti-immigrant stereotypes — particularly against Indians — to demand that the scheme be scrapped.

Microsoft disputed the implication that its visa filings represented new hires replacing US workers. In a statement, the company said that 80 percent of the roughly 6,000 H1-B visa applications it issued last year were “to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees”, not for new employees, and that the other filings were for “individuals already legally in the United States”.

The company also said that it only files applications for people who “meet the rigorous standards of this visa category” and that such employees are paid equally to any others who do similar work.

What does this mean for foreign workers?

The suspension could make it harder for foreign workers in the tech industry to obtain permanent residency in the US. Many of those affected are likely to be Indian nationals, who account for a large share of the country’s skilled foreign workforce in the technology sector.

Each year, there are only 85,000 slots for new H-1B visas (not including filings for renewals), but hundreds of thousands of applications. Many H-1B visa holders work in technology-related jobs: 62 percent of the beneficiaries in the 2025 fiscal year worked in computer-related occupations.

Indian nationals account for roughly 70 percent of existing H-1B visa holders.

The Trump administration has already tried to crack down on the H1-B scheme, and in August proposed a new $103,000 fee for H1-B applications, after an earlier pitch for a similar fee was struck down by a federal court. The fee, the government argues, would help provide revenue that could be used to service the vast US immigration system, while reducing the incentive for companies to attempt to misuse H1-B visas.

But the new move to restrict the pathway to a green card for foreign workers already in the US, legally, could impact not just those who might have dreamed of working or living in the US — but thousands already in the country.

The US typically issues around 140,000 employment-based green cards every year. But it also has a strict country-based cap — applicants from any one country cannot receive more than seven percent of green cards issued in a year.

Yet, because the employment-based green card application system is largely used to convert many H1-B visa holders into permanent residents, applicants for permanent residency are disproportionately Indian.

The result: Nearly one million Indians legally in the US on work visas are currently stuck in the employment-based green card backlog. They represent 79 percent of the total green card backlog of around 1.25 million people.



Even before the latest move, Indian green card applicants in certain employment categories would have needed to wait for decades, according to a 2025 analysis for the Congressional Research Service.

Sonderling’s statement that the US will no longer process “any pending permanent labour certification applications” from the blacklisted companies has raised fears that tens of thousands of foreign workers in the country legally — most of them Indian — who have waited for years might suddenly no longer be eligible. For others, the wait could get even longer.

Has India responded?

Yes. India’s Ministry of External Affairs issued a statement saying the US’s suspension does not “advance the shared ambitions of both countries”.

The ministry said that “talent mobility adds value” to both the Indian and US economies, including providing US companies “with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation”.

The ministry also criticised comments by Vance comparing foreign workers to indentured servants as “unwarranted” and “deeply offensive”, saying his words recalled “painful historical and colonial legacy connotations”.

Colonial powers — the British, Dutch and French — took more than 1.6 million Indian workers as indentured labourers to work on plantations and build railways in their other colonies: in Malaysia, Mauritius, South Africa, Kenya, Uganda, Fiji, Suriname, Guyana and other Caribbean countries.

India’s foreign ministry said Vance’s descriptions also “ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem”.

World.title: Labour fends off the Green party in closely watched UK by-election
World.content:
Sagal Abdi-Wali, who arrived in the UK as child refugee from Somalia, won 3,300 more votes than Zack Polanski, leader of the Greens.

Share Labour fends off the Green party in closely watched UK by-election on social media

The Labour Party has won an election for a parliamentary seat vacated by former leader Keir Starmer, fending off a challenge from the left-wing Green Party in a boost for the British prime minister.

Labour candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali, the leader of the local council, won the seat in the central London constituency of Holborn and St Pancras with 12,292 votes, compared with 8,928 for Zack Polanski, the Green Party leader who came second.

The victory, which had been expected, will buoy Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who was recently installed by lawmakers fearful that Starmer’s unpopularity was opening the way for a challenge by the populist Reform UK party at the next national election.

After losing left-wing support to the Greens earlier this year, Labour looks to have won many voters back, a result that triggered more questions about Polanski’s leadership, who had promised to make his party “an eco-populist” movement.

There are now five Green MPs, compared with one in 2023.

But Polanski, 43, came under fire after party members passed a motion declaring that Zionism is racism at their annual conference.

The move, which called for “the establishment of a single democratic Palestinian State in all of historic Palestine” was criticised by Jewish groups, other parties and most Green Party lawmakers. Polanski did not vote on the motion.

Labour has held Holborn since the seat was created in 1983.

Labour’s Abdi-Wali, who arrived in the United Kingdom as a child refugee from Somalia, said her victory was a defeat for “those who seek to divide us”.



“We have a responsibility to defend what we’ve built and pass it on,” she said.

After conceding defeat, Polanski, who is not an MP, answered his critics, saying he would stay on as leader, and described the result as part of “Andy Burnham’s honeymoon”.

Polanski congratulated Abdi-Wali, but said, “One in three voters backed us here, and we know that many more considered it.”

Al Jazeera’s Sonia Gallego, reporting from London, said, “The constituency has been going through what some people have been calling ‘the Burnham bounce‘ … so far there is a deep sigh of relief (among Labour) that they’ve managed to hold on.”

Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has changed voter habits during the past three years. The Greens, far more critical of Israel’s conduct than any other party, got a boost in the 2024 general election.

Back then, Starmer won the seat with 49 percent. Andrew Feinstein, a pro-Palestine independent candidate, came second, with 19 percent.

Polanski has raised the “progressive vote” while “reducing the Labour vote”, Feinstein said.

World.title: Is Trump signalling a return to war with Iran after the midterms?
World.content:
US media reports suggest he may be weighing strikes before the vote but the president has ruled that out.

Share Is Trump signalling a return to war with Iran after the midterms? on social media

United States President Donald Trump has said that he does not intend to bomb Iran again until the November midterm elections, even though several US media outlets have reported that the Pentagon has drawn up plans to relaunch attacks before that vote.

Trump has been accused of misdirection on the issue in the past. The US launched its initial attacks on Iran on February 28, as talks with Iran were ongoing and despite Trump saying just the day before that he had not made any decision. One year previously, the US struck Iran towards the end of Israel’s June 2025 12-day war, despite Trump saying he would announce a decision about attacks “in two weeks”.

Still, striking Iran ahead of the midterm elections would be risky for the administration as the war remains deeply unpopular with Americans.

Resuming the war afterwards may have less of a negative impact on Trump, who is not eligible to run for another term as US president anyway.

Here’s what we know about Trump’s plans.

What has been reported by US media?

In the past two days, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and other publications have reported claims by unnamed officials that the Pentagon has drawn up plans to attack Iran before the midterms, if authorised to do so.

On Wednesday, US publication Axios cited US and Israeli officials saying the Pentagon has instructed US Central Command (CENTCOM) to prepare for imminent major combat operations. The Atlantic also reported along similar lines.

What has Trump said?

On Thursday, Trump posted on his Truth Social media platform that he will not order a resumption of strikes on Iran before November 3, when the US midterm elections will be held.



“I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition…we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd,” he said.

The president added that the US is presently “having productive discussions” with the Iranian side. However, that was also the case on February 28, the day the US and Israel first struck Iran, triggering the war.

Trump did not make any reference to preparing for potential military operations, nor did he provide more details on the state of talks.

Why might Trump be hesitant about resuming bombing before the midterms?

Trump and Republicans are worried about a voter backlash against the war at the polls. The US war on Iran is intensely unpopular domestically as Americans have had to grapple with surging prices of gas, food and other basic commodities because of the crisis in the Middle East.

Since the start of the war, surveys have shown that large numbers of Americans did not approve of striking Iran.

Now, about 65 percent of Americans say they “disapprove” of the way in which Trump has handled the Iran war overall, according to a Pew Research Center poll released on Thursday. Trump stated at the start of the war that it would go on for just a few weeks, however, it is now into its eighth month.

According to Pew, most Americans now believe the war will continue for at least another year. Even Republican or more conservative-leaning voters are growing more negative about the war, its poll found.

The conflict has also severely affected Trump’s personal ratings and eroded support for Republicans. A Reuters/Ipsos poll on Thursday found that only 30 percent of his supporters were enthusiastic about voting in the midterms, compared with 48 percent of Democratic voters.

About 13 percent of those who voted for Trump in 2024 say they are not sure who to vote for in the congressional elections.

Delaying attacks until after the elections could potentially shield Republican candidates from voter backlash, analysts say.

While analysts say Trump will see a good performance at the polls as approval for renewed strikes, a Republican defeat at the polls could equally further incentivise him to hit Iran again as he will calculate that he has little to lose at that point.

While that could further affect Trump’s ratings, the president is not eligible to run in the next presidential election in any case.

Will the US restart the war after the midterms?

In recent weeks, the US president has threatened to “end” the war with force after the elections as talks with Iran have dragged on.



At a Republican convention in September, he accused Iran of trying to affect the outcome of the midterms and said that conflict “is going to end immediately after the elections”.

In an interview with Time magazine two weeks ago, he also said it would be “possible” to ramp up bombing in Iran after the elections, but declined to elaborate. Analysts say his comments were designed to calm voters, while at the same time warning Iran of potential aggression after the vote.

Last week, the US military dispatched about 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines aboard several ships now sailing to the Middle East amid threats of new attacks from Trump. The vessel formation included the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group.

The deployment increases the number of US troops in the region to 20,000, alongside hundreds of aircraft and at least three carrier strike groups.

In the past, US troop build-up in the Middle East and the Caribbean has subsequently resulted in military action.

In June, Washington and Iran signed a ceasefire agreement that quickly broke down over control of the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump has repeatedly said that the US has the upper hand in the strait, citing more oil exports and Iran’s weakened economy. He has also voiced aversion to a deal with Tehran over management of Hormuz, but said he might consider it because “they’re willing to offer us anything to stop”.

Washington rejected a recent proposal from Iran to reopen the strait based on certain conditions it wants the US to meet, including the lifting of sanctions, unfreezing Iranian assets and guaranteeing an end to attacks. Last week, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran was considering a counterproposal from the US.

World.title: Ex-OpenAI staff say they were fired for raising safety concerns
World.content:
Three former researchers pen open letter warning of ‘chilling’ effect on company culture.

Share Ex-OpenAI staff say they were fired for raising safety concerns on social media

Three former OpenAI employees say they have been fired due to their efforts to ensure the safety of artificial intelligence.

Safety researchers Mikita Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang levelled the accusations on Thursday after their dismissals last week. The trio warned of a “chilling” effect on other staff concerned about the frontier technology’s risks.

OpenAI said they were let go due to misconduct involving the mishandling of company information.

“I believe we were fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation,” Balesni said in a post on X.

Korbak expressed a similar sentiment, expressing his belief that he had been terminated for raising concerns that OpenAI was “losing the ability to monitor what AI agents think, one of our best tools for catching when they misbehave”.

In an open letter published in tandem with their social media posts, Balesni, Korbak and Wang expressed concerns that their dismissal would make their former colleagues “afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI”.

“We could raise safety concerns and disagree openly, and were encouraged to draw on the expertise of independent safety organizations,” they said in the letter. “This is part of what made OpenAI special, and why we are immensely proud to have been part of the team.”

The three added that “if the people closest to the risks can no longer work in high-trust, high-bandwidth ways with each other and with third parties”, then AI could not be developed safely.



“It is that culture we are writing to defend,” they stated.

The trio denied violating company policy, saying any engagement with external safety experts had been in line with the mandate of their roles.

“Given the significant safety concerns surrounding the development of AI, employees must not be left working in an environment where fear and unclear rules stymie AI safety work and weaken third-party accountability,” they said.

“Terminations such as ours, executed and communicated so abruptly, are chilling the open culture OpenAI has prized in the past.”

In a statement, OpenAI said it had uncovered “a significant breach of trust” by the former researchers that went beyond what was described in their letter and said it stood behind the decision to fire them.

“We want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out,” the San Francisco-based company said.

“Safety and research debates happen every day at OpenAI, often spirited and highly critical. We actively encourage these discussions and consider them essential to making the right decisions. We cannot do the work in front of us without a high degree of trust. We will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes.”

OpenAI added that it was saddened by the outcome.

“We appreciated Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek’s contributions to AI safety at OpenAI and their willingness to speak up and challenge ideas,” the company said.

“We championed their voices, supported their work, and placed enormous trust in them. These decisions were not about them raising safety concerns. We have always encouraged that and always will.”

The ex-employees’ intervention comes as OpenAI and other AI companies are at the centre of intense debate about how to ensure the rapidly evolving technology does not expose humanity to catastrophic harm.

The risk of cutting-edge AI models escaping human control has been in the spotlight since July when it emerged that autonomous agents generated by OpenAI had hacked the software start-up Hugging Face.

OpenAI and its chief rival, Anthropic, have urged the international community to work together on a coordinated slowdown in AI development.

However, that suggestion has been rebuffed by the two leading AI powers, the United States and China.

Last month, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, SpaceXAI and Nvidia endorsed a voluntary accord calling for stronger internal safeguards and the engagement of external auditors to better manage safety risks.



The accord, announced by US President Donald Trump, drew a mixed response from AI safety advocates, many of whom criticised its nonbinding nature.

OpenAI has announced a number of steps to mitigate risks in the absence of formal regulation, including scrapping the planned release of its latest-generation model, GPT-6.1 Astra.

The ChatGPT creator said it decided not to go ahead with the release after its model failed to meet company standards for acting in accordance with human wishes.

World.title: Firing squad execution to be livestreamed, Pentagon says
World.content:
The public will be able to watch the execution of a former US Army major by firing squad, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has said.

A Defense Department official told the BBC the execution of Nidal Hasan, who shot dead 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, would be livestreamed.

It is believed it would be the first public execution in the US in almost a century. The decision to livestream it is "unprecedented in the modern era" and "on uncertain legal terrain," said John Mills, a lawyer who works with inmates sentenced to death.

"People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," said Hegseth.

The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group.

The Pentagon announced earlier this week it would execute Hasan in the first military execution in more than 60 years.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, admitted fatally shooting 13 unarmed soldiers in a crowded medical building at Fort Hood.

Alonzo Lunsford, a former US Army sergeant who was shot seven times in the attack, told the BBC's Today programme that he supported the execution by firing squad, as a method "befitting" for what he did.

He does not believe everyone should be able to watch the livestream, concerned about the message it sends younger people, but says it is important that those affected by the shooting are given the opportunity.

"As far as the families of the fallen and the families of the survivors, and the survivors themselves, yes, I think we should be able to look at it uncensored."

Lunsford says he plans to attend the execution and before they pull the trigger he wants Hasan to look him in the eyes. "I want him to know he failed. I'm still here."

World.title: Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream
World.content:
But Lunsford said that as a Christian, he has forgiven Hasan because "I cannot heal if I don't forgive him".

"We're taught that with your last breath you can ask for forgiveness and I think that's what he [Hasan] should do," he added.

Telling his account of what happened that day, he said Hasan got out of his chair and jumped onto a counter, before pulling out a weapon and discharging rounds.

Lunford said he was looking for an exit via the back door, which was "two or three strides" away from him when he was first shot above his left eye and then "hit two more times in my back" as he crawled behind a desk.

"At that point I played dead," he said. When Hasan moved on, he grabbed a nearby wounded soldier and went outside, where Lunsford said Hasan came up behind them and shot him again.

One memory he said that "bothers" him from the day was of a woman who told Hasan she was pregnant.

"We heard a gunshot and the last thing that girl was saying was: 'Oh my god, my baby, my baby.'"

Lunsford said personnel don't carry weapons in medical facilities, and that Hasan "took the coward's way out" to attack them there.

"And then for him to say he is fighting for his cause? I've read the Quran, and everything that he said he was doing that was in the Quran is not supported by the Quran," he explained.

Hasan's execution was announced by the Pentagon earlier this week, in what will be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

Legal experts have told the BBC there are a number of hurdles around the livestreaming of this which could mean it is successfully challenged in court.

Some politicians have been vocal in their opposition.

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN it was "disgusting" while Republican Senator Thom Tillis said public executions were what "oppressive dictators" did.

"It should not be happening in America," he added in a post on X., external

World.title: France promises 3,000 extra teachers in first step to calm student protests
World.content:
The French government has made its first sign of giving ground to teenage protesters, with a promise of 3,000 extra supply teachers in the coming days.

Education minister Edouard Geffray made the offer in a television interview on Thursday evening, at the end of another day of sometimes violent demonstrations by high-school students.

The government says 6,877 people have been arrested, 86% of whom are under the age of 18, since protests began centred around demands for more resources in secondary education.

In what unions have billed as Act Four of the three-week movement, some 71,000 people staged protests across the country on Thursday, with 24,000 gathering at the Bastille in Paris.

Police once again intervened with tear-gas to disperse groups who attacked them with paving stones and homemade fireworks.

In Bordeaux, a lycÃ©e, or high school, was ransacked by protesters, and in Marseille a deputy-head was beaten up.

On Friday, some 140 lycÃ©es - out of 3,500 - were totally or partially closed, a big drop on previous days. But another day of action has been called for next Tuesday.

World.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC
World.content:
A former Ukrainian security services officer linked to a bomb attack in Monaco in June that targeted a multi-millionaire says he believed it was authorised by senior members of HUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC from prison in Kyiv, facilitated by his lawyer, Vitalii Zhykovych has given his own account of the attempted assassination for the first time.

Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev and his 13-year-old son were badly hurt in the blast and his partner suffered catastrophic injuries. Yermolayev later described their survival as "nothing short of a miracle".

Zhykovych describes himself as a "freelancer" for Ukraine's SBU security service and says Anastasia Berezovska, the woman caught on camera planting the bomb in Monaco, was his "agent".

A week after the bombing, Berezovska's body was discovered in the woods west of Kyiv with gunshot wounds to the head.

But Zhykovych insists he did not send her to kill, and nor did he kill her.

He was arrested and accused of her murder together with an active-duty intelligence officer from HUR called Vladyslav Reut.

Reut initially confessed to investigators, and led them to the shallow grave. But days later in court, he changed his testimony to blame Zhykovych.

World.title: Thieves steal 30,000 wine bottles worth €5m in Italy, reports say
World.content:
Thieves have stolen 30,000 bottles of wine collectively worth about â¬5m (Â£4.2m) from a prestigious Italian winery, Italian media reports.

Marchesi Antinori, one of Italy's biggest family-owned wineries, said the theft at its storage facility in Tuscany took place on Saturday as the company was preparing to ship a consignment to customers abroad.

At least seven masked men are believed to have deactivated the alarms, disabled the cameras and used company forklifts to load two large trucks of the company's prized Tignanello, Solaia and Guado al Tasso Tuscan reds.

Renzo Cotarella, the chief executive, told Corriere della Sera this was the largest theft of its kind in Italy.

"A theft of this scale and value has certainly never occurred in Italy," he said.

He added that he was hopeful the authorities would be able to trace the stolen wine.

"Two trucks full of merchandise can't just disappear into thin air. The Tuscan roads are full of cameras; perhaps with a bit of luck we'll be able to recover at least some of the bottles stolen from us."

He told the Financial Times: "These wines have a great value and I don't know how they can sell all this wine around the world without being seen."

The company believes the selection of bottles, which usually sell for between â¬150 and â¬500 each, suggests the thieves were wine connoisseurs and had inside knowledge.

The theft was only discovered on Monday morning as staff arrived on site. No arrests have been made.

Marchesi Antinori was founded in 1385 and exports to 170 countries. It had a revenue of â¬263m (Â£223m) last year.

There has been a spate of wine thefts in Italy this year, including two in the northern Piedmont region where hundreds of thousands of euros worth of bottles were reportedly taken.

World.title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City
World.content:
A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot a man in the Bronx in New York City on Thursday.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which runs the agency, confirmed an ICE officer "discharged his weapon" during "a targeted enforcement operation... to arrest a criminal illegal alien".

In a statement, it added the man was alive and at a local hospital.

New York mayor Zohran Mamdani said it was an "unconscionable and incredibly serious situation".

"Early reports indicate agents surrounded him and a five-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds. We believe the child was physically unharmed," he said.

The BBC has approached DHS for comment about Mamdani's remarks.

Late on Thursday evening, New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she had spoken to President Donald Trump about the shooting and had expressed "outrage on behalf of New Yorkers".

"I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth."

Trump has not yet commented publicly on the shooting.

The DHS said the man, who has not been named by officials, was from the Dominican Republic and had "a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny, and multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession".

He was arrested by police officers in New York in December 2023 and released "a few days later", according to the DHS statement.

It also claimed he was associated with the Trinitarios, described by the US justice department as a transnational criminal group.

World.title: Crazy Rich Asians to return as TV show with original film's stars
World.content:
Four of the stars of 2018's Crazy Rich Asians film are reprising their roles for a TV show of the same name.

The series will pick up events after the end of the hit film, with Constance Wu and Henry Golding playing their lead roles of Rachel and Nick, while Ronny Chieng is back as Eddie and Oscar winner Michelle Yeoh will have a recurring role as Nick's mother Eleanor.

"It's a 'Crazy Rich' family reunion!" said Adele Lim, who co-wrote the film, calling it the sequel we've been waiting for". It will "delve into the characters and worlds of Kevin Kwan's brilliant books" over eight episodes, she said.

The show will be made by HBO, and the news was announced days after HBO's parent company Warner Bros announced its Â£110bn (Â£82.8bn) merger with Paramount Skydance.

Adapted from Kwan's bestseller books, written between 2013 and 2017, the film topped the US box office and was nominated for two Golden Globes.

It featured an all-Asian cast and told the story of an Asian-American woman who gets a culture shock meeting her boyfriend's ultra-wealthy family in Singapore.

Lim is showrunner for the new TV series and will be one of the executive producers, as will the the film's director Jon M Chu.

World.title: Doctor accused of 1994 Rwanda genocide offences to face trial in UK
World.content:
A doctor accused of a number of offences relating to the 1994 Rwanda genocide is set to face trial in autumn next year.

Dr Vincent Brown, formerly Dr Vincent Bajinya, 65, is accused of "killing, directing or encouraging" the deaths of members of the Tutsi ethnic group in Rwanda. He is the first person in the UK to have been charged over the genocide.

Brown, of Islington, north London, is charged with one count of conduct ancillary to genocide and six offences of conduct ancillary to murder as a crime against humanity.

A judge has now set his provisional trial date to begin in October 2027. He denies wrongdoing and has not yet entered a plea.

The defendant appeared via video link from Belmarsh prison on Friday for a pre-trial hearing at the Old Bailey during which Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb set a provisional eight to 12-week trial from October 4 2027.

A plea and case management hearing has also been set for 15 January.

He has indicated he will plead not guilty to the charges against him.

An estimated 800,000 Tutsis and politically moderate Hutus were killed during the 1994 Rwanda genocide which lasted for 100 days.

Brown is a medical doctor who qualified in Rwanda in the 1980s. He later became head of the country's Department of Family Health in Kigali and lived in a suburb there with his wife and young son.

Between April 6 and 13 1994, he was allegedly a party to six murders and was later charged following a seven-year British investigation into the killings.

The court heard on Friday that a Â£100,000 bail condition, imposed earlier in October, had not yet been met.

Prosecutor Bill Emlyn Jones KC told the court the events in 1994 were "the most devastating wave of mass killing in modern history".

Jones said: "One hundred thousand were murdered in Kigali especially in the first days and weeks of the genocide."

World.title: Tinubu, Sultan expected as MUSWEN General Assembly meeting holds in November
World.content:
The President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Bola Tinubu, Southwest states governors and the Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, are among the dignitaries expected at the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South West Nigeria (MUSWEN), holding on November 15 at the University of Ibadan Central Mosque.

AbdulRahman AbdulGhaniy, the Chairman of the General Assembly 2026 Central Planning Committee, said in a statement in Ibadan that Borno State Governor Babagana Zulum is expected to deliver the annual lecture.

Leaders of Muslim organisations across the Southwest geopolitical zones attend the annual General Assembly of MUSWEN.

In addition to the annual lecture, delegates are expected to ratify the organisation’s leadership change, as the incumbent president vacates office after leading MUSWEN for the last six years.

Rasaki Oladejo became President of MUSWEN on November 22, 2020, succeeding the late Sakariyau Babalola.

In the statement, Mr AbdulGaniy also called on Muslim philanthropists to support MUSWEN in reaching its goal of raising N2 billion to support its projects on empowerment of the less privileged, construction of a state-of-the-art health facility and provision of scholarships for needy members of the Ummah.

MUSWEN is the umbrella body for all Muslims in South Western Nigeria. Its primary member organisations are the Muslim Communities or Muslim Councils of all the States in South West Nigeria.

World.title: The pharaonic policy (Al-Siyasah Al-Fir’auniyyah) of “starve your dog, and it will follow you”!, By Murtadha Gusau
World.content:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

All praise is due to Allah, the Just, the Provider, who has forbidden oppression for Himself and made it forbidden among His creation.

Dear brothers and sisters! We often hear worldly aphorisms born of human arrogance. We hear the toxic philosophy of ‘Starve your dog, and it will follow you’. Fir’aun (Pharaoh) used it. The tyrants of old used it. Today, exploitative corporate systems and corrupt leaders use economic anxiety and systematic deprivation to enforce obedience.

But Allah the Almighty tells us a different law of the universe. In a Hadith Qudsi, Allah the Most High says:

“O My servants, I have forbidden oppression for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another.”

Islam completely flips this toxic paradigm. In the light of the Qur’an and the Sunnah, we do not rule hearts by starving them; we win souls by nourishing them. And true strength and power is not breaking the wills of others to make them follow you—it is conquering your own ego to follow Allah.

Depriving those under your care—whether they are your employees, your family, or your community—does not yield loyalty. It breeds resentment and revolution. True leadership is rooted in enrichment and generosity. When the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) built his Ummah, he did not rule by withholding; he gave until he had nothing left for himself, earning an unbreakable loyalty born of love, not fear.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Respected servants of Allah! Look at the fate of those who practice this proverb. The king who said it was destroyed by the very hunger he manufactured.

Islam teaches us that loyalty cannot be bought with desperation. If you are an employer, pay your workers before their sweat dries. If you are a parent or spouse, do not withhold emotional or financial sustenance to assert control. Let us remember that the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) warned us against the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah the Almighty.

Dear servants of Allah! The Jahiliyyah period, the age of ignorance, taught a brutal philosophy of leadership: “Starve your dog, and it will follow you.” It tells us that if you want loyalty, you must keep people vulnerable. If you want obedience, you must withhold. This is the methodology of Fir’aun (Pharaoh). Fir’aun (Pharaoh) kept his people weak, terrified, and desperate so that they would look to him as a god.

But what happens when you starve a creature? You erase its dignity. You build a relationship based on desperation, not devotion. And the moment that creature finds a hand that feeds it better, it will turn around and bite the hand that starved it. Worldly control built on fear is a ticking time bomb.

Look instead, O Muslim believers, to the Master of Humanity, Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him). He did not come to starve humanity; he came to feed their souls, their minds, and their bodies.

Allah the Most High says in the noble Qur’an about the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him):

“And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.” [Qur’an, 21:107]

When the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) conquered Makkah—the very city that starved his companions, boycotted his family, and persecuted his followers—he did not starve them in return. He did not humiliate them to force their loyalty. He stood before them and said, “Go, for you are free.”

He fed their dignity, and what was the result? They didn’t just follow him; they were ready to lay down their lives for him. Hearts are opened by Ihsan, excellence and kindness, not by oppression.

If there is anything in this life you should starve, my dear brothers and sisters, it is not the people around you. It is not your spouse, your children, or your employees. Starve your lower self, the Nafs!

Your Nafs al-Ammarah, the soul that commands evil, is like a wild beast. If you feed it every desire, every luxury, every glance, and every whim, it will master you. It will lead you to destruction. But if you starve it through fasting, through discipline, through lowering your gaze, and through standing in the night prayer—it will finally submit. It will follow you in obedience to Allah.

May Allah purify our hearts, break our egos, and make us leaders of mercy, not masters of oppression. Ameen!

Dear brothers and sisters! In human relationships, this proverb “Starve your dog, and it will follow you” represents a dark psychological truth: manipulation. We see it in toxic marriages where one partner withholds affection to gain power. We see it in corporate environments where managers keep employees insecure to ensure compliance.

But Islamic psychology teaches us that a loyalty born of starvation is artificial.

Contrast the harsh Arabic proverb with one of the most emotional traditions in Islam. The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) told us of a man walking through the desert. He was parched with thirst. He found a well, climbed down, drank his fill, and climbed back out.

Upon reaching the top, he saw a dog panting heavily, licking the moist earth out of extreme thirst. The man looked at the dog and didn’t think, “Let me leverage this animal’s weakness.” Instead, his heart melted with empathy. He climbed back down into the well, filled his leather sock with water, held it in his teeth as he climbed out, and gave the dog a drink.

The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) concluded:

“Allah thanked him for his deed and forgave his sins.” [Sahih al-Bukhari]

The world tells you to exploit weakness to gain followers. Islam tells you to alleviate weakness to gain the pleasure of the King of Kings, Allah the Almighty!

When you treat people with the philosophy of “starvation,” you are acting out of your own deep insecurity. You fear that if they are strong, free, and self-sufficient, they will leave you. But true leadership—good leadership—is about empowering others so much so that they choose to stand by you out of genuine love and respect.

Don’t starve the world around you to make it bend to your will. Feed it with mercy, and watch how Allah the Almighty elevates your status in this life and the next.

The Arabic proverb “Starve your dog, and it will follow you” (جَوِّعْ كَلْبَكَ يَتْبَعْكَ) carries a raw, historical realism about power, control, and the darker side of human politics. However, when viewed through the profound lens of Islamic spirituality, psychology, and Prophetic wisdom, this proverb serves as a powerful mirror—not for how we should treat others, but for how we must discipline our own inner selves.

The historical proverb “Starve your dog, and it will follow you” represents the ultimate form of tyrannical control, psychological manipulation, and the deliberate crushing of human dignity. In Islamic history and theology, this approach is famously known as the Pharaonic Policy, Al-Siyasah al-Fir’auniyyah.

Fir’aun (Pharaoh) did not just rule through physical chains; he ruled by engineered dependency, breaking the spirit of his people until they viewed their oppressor as their sole provider.

Dear servants of Allah! Tyrants throughout history have never ruled by strength alone; they rule by weaponising artificial scarcity. When the Fir’aun (Pharaoh) of Egypt looked at the Children of Israel, he did not just see a minority to oppress—he saw a population that needed to be kept weak, hungry, and desperate.

To make people break their own backs chasing a loaf of bread, and they will never have the energy to look up and demand their freedom. Keep them terrified of losing their sustenance, and they will bow to the one holding the grain.

But the great religion of Islam came to shatter this illusion. Islam arrived to scream into the hearts of humanity: Your boss is not your provider. Your leader is not your provider. The market is not your provider. Ar-Razzaq, The Ultimate Provider, is Allah the Almighty!

When Fir’aun (Pharaoh) claimed, “I am your lord, most high,” he was attempting to centralise all dependency onto himself. He wanted the people to believe that if they disobeyed him, they would starve.

But look at how Allah the Almighty refutes this psychological warfare in the noble Qur’an. Allah the Most High says:

“And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision…” [Qur’an, 11:6]

When you realise that your life, your breath, and your wealth are written by the King of Kings, the Pharaonic policy, the Siyasah Al-Fir’auniyyah loses all its power over you. They can restrict the earth, but they cannot close the gates of heaven.

Remember, when the Muslim army faced the superpower of their time—the Persian Empire—the Persian general Rustam asked to speak to an emissary. The Muslims sent Rib’iyyu Ibn Amir, a man wearing simple, patched clothes, riding a small horse, carrying a basic spear.

Rustam sat in a courtyard filled with gold-woven carpets, silk cushions, and glittering wealth. He expected this simple Arab man from the desert to be blinded by the wealth, to crawl and beg for food and treaties—to follow the “crumbs” like a starved dog. Instead, Rib’iyyu rode his horse right onto the luxurious carpets. He drove his spear into the expensive rugs, tearing them up as he walked forward with his head held high.

Rustam asked him: “What brought you here?”

Rib’iyyu delivered words that should be carved into the heart of every sincere Muslim believer today. He said:

“Allah has sent us to deliver whomsoever He wills from the worship of creation to the worship of the Creator alone, from the narrowness of this world to its vastness, and from the tyranny of false religions to the justice of Islam.”

Rib’iyyu could not be starved, because his soul was already full. He could not be bribed, because he knew that the Persian Empire’s wealth belonged to Allah anyway.

Respected brothers and sisters! The policy of “Starve your dog, and it will follow you” has not faded into history; it has merely modernised.

Today, economic systems and corporate structures often thrive on keeping people in a state of perpetual survival anxiety. When people are drowning in debt, living paycheck to paycheck, and terrified of losing their healthcare or shelter, they become compliant. They tolerate toxic environments, sacrifice their morals, and remain silent in the face of injustice because they fear their “provider” will cut them off.

Pharaoh’s greatest victory was not building the pyramids; it was convincing the people that without him, they would perish. When Prophet Musa came with clear signs, Pharaoh’s response was to attack their livelihood and security:

● He doubled their workload.

● He threatened their survival.

● He forced them into a state of pure panic.

The psychological trap is making the victim believe they are a “dog” that needs the master to survive.

The great religion of Islam breaks this cycle through three foundational psychological shifts:

1. True Tawhid (Monotheism)

Believing that provision is fixed. No human being can give you a single penny that Allah did not decree for you, and no human can take away a single crumb that Allah wrote in your destiny.

2. The Honour of Bani Adam

Allah the Most High says:

“And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam…” [Qur’an, 17:70]

A Muslim believer is a servant to Allah, but a noble leader on this earth. You are not a creature to be starved and commanded.

3. Contentment

When you train yourself to be content with less, you become unbribable. If a tyrant cannot tempt you with luxury, and cannot scare you with poverty, they lose all leverage over you.

And if you are currently feeling trapped in a situation where someone is using your livelihood, your job, your emotions, or your security to control you—remember the parting of the Red Sea.

The Children of Israel stood with the roaring sea in front of them and Pharaoh’s marching army behind them. They panicked and cried out:

“We are surely overtaken!”

But Prophet Musa (Peace be upon him), whose heart was entirely detached from Pharaonic fear, replied with absolute certainty:

“No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.” [Qur’an, 26:62]

So the sea split. The oppressor drowned. The provision came from where they least expected it.

Never let anyone starve your soul to command your body. Turn away from the hand holding the false crumbs, look up to the Heavens, and realise that you are free.

Respected brothers and sisters! The proverb “Starve your dog, and it will follow you” جوع كلبك يعطيك or جوع كلبك يتبعك is historically attributed to Amr Ibn Hind, a powerful and tyrannical 6th-century king of Al-Hirah, the modern-day Iraq.

According to historical Arabic literature, the king used this phrase to describe how he ruled over the Arab tribes. He believed that if his subjects became wealthy, prosperous, and self-sufficient, they would rebel against his rule. Therefore, he kept them economically strained and dependent on his royal favours to ensure their absolute submission.

Ironically, the proverb is often cited alongside its historical undoing: Amr Ibn Hind was eventually assassinated by the famous poet and warrior Amr Ibn Kulthum because of the king’s extreme arrogance. This birthed a counter-proverb:

“Perhaps your dog will bite you when it grows hungry.”

Today, this proverb is never used as positive advice. Instead, it is used critically to describe machiavellian tactics, political tyranny, or toxic manipulation.

It is frequently invoked in political discourse to criticise corrupt governments or leaders who intentionally plunge their populations into economic hardship. By keeping citizens preoccupied with basic survival: bread, water, fuel, etc, the leaders ensure the public has no time or energy to demand political freedom or reforms.

It can also describe an abusive employer who keeps employees underpaid and insecure so they won’t leave, or describe a toxic relationship where one partner emotionally starves the other to maintain control.

In modern commentary, whenever this proverb is quoted, it serves as a warning to oppressors. Just as a starved animal may eventually turn on its owner out of sheer desperation, an oppressed group will eventually revolt when they have nothing left to lose.

In the Machiavellian corridors of worldly politics, the phrase “Starve your dog, and it will follow you” has long been used to justify oppression. Tyrants throughout history have known that a population preoccupied with basic survival has no energy to revolt. They control by restriction.

But when we pull this proverb out of the political mud and wash it in the ocean of Tazkiyyah, it transforms into an explosive psychological truth.

Ya Allah, do not leave us in charge of our own souls even for the blinking of an eye. Quiet our egos, feed our hearts with Your love, and make our desires subservient to Your guidance, ameen Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May the peace, blessings and salutations of Allah be upon our noble Messenger, Muhammad, and upon his family, his Companions and his true followers.

Murtadha Muhammad Gusau is the Chief Imam of Nagazi-Uvete Jumu’ah and the late Alhaji Abdur-Rahman Okene’s Mosques, Okene, Kogi State, Nigeria. He can be reached via: [email protected] or +2348038289761 or +2348024192217.

World.title: Concerns about the 2027 general elections, By Jibrin Ibrahim
World.content:
As the countdown to the 2027 elections reached 100 days this week Tuesday, Joash Amupitan, chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), called a press conference to brief the Nation on their preparedness for the rapidly approaching polls. His big story was that the commission will deploy artificial intelligence (AI) tools for result verification and to strengthen cybersecurity ahead of the 2027 elections. He announced the establishment of a dedicated AI division within its information and communication technology (ICT) department which will enable automated AI auditing tools that are integrated into the commission’s result verification process under a five-pillar AI governance framework. He added that the use of AI would be subjected to mandatory human oversight and that the commission is working with international technology leaders and partners to integrate AI-driven anomaly detection tools into its systems. He said the tools would be used to monitor database traffic and protect the commission’s systems against cyber intrusions and unauthorised alterations. Given current universal concerns over AI enabled abuses, I doubt that his words were very reassuring given the trust deficit Nigerians already have about INEC. Everything else he said was about their excellent state of preparedness for the elections.

There have been widespread concerns on Professor Amupitan’s political neutrality and the onus is on him to prove his credibility. As elections in the Fourth Republic roll by, Nigerians have become increasingly concerned about the decline of the electoral system as an institution that could guarantee the rights of citizens to freely choose those who exercise power on their behalf. Since assuming office, the new Chairman of INEC has expressed commitment and readiness to rewrite Nigeria’s electoral history by ensuring the integrity of the 2027 elections surpasses previous elections. I definitely hope and pray that he is truthful.

The legitimacy of elections is derived from the existence of a level playing ground for competition and contestation. Where competition is eliminated or restricted, elections lose their democratic ingredient. One of the most profound threats to the 2027 elections is the systematic erosion of political competition through induced defections from political parties and the incremental decimation of opposition parties. This distortion of the political landscape could disincentivise public participation in the 2027 elections, as voters will have limited political choices. Constricting the political space and the gradual descent towards a one-party state threaten Nigeria’s democratic trajectory ahead of the 2027 elections. When political pluralism is overtly or covertly removed from electoral politics, authoritarianism creeps in, and it diminishes the legitimacy of electoral outcomes. My greatest fear for the 2027 elections is the growing concern of Nigerians that their votes may not count. The fear is that three major institutions: security agencies, INEC, and the judiciary might compromise the electoral process.

The widespread insecurity and escalating tensions in the country is not new but poses directly the question whether insurgency, banditry, communal conflicts, separatist agitations, and organised criminal violence could continue to overstretch Nigeria’s security architecture and create conditions to explain away State complicity in compromising the elections. This expanded geography of insecurity undermines the likelihood of a safe and peaceful environment for elections. INEC may be constrained to organise elections in volatile and ungoverned spaces, while voters in conflict zones may be disenfranchised. Where insecurity impedes the deployment of election personnel, materials, and security assets, the credibility and inclusiveness of the electoral process are fundamentally compromised.

The increasingly prominent role of the judiciary in determining electoral outcomes is another facet of the problem. If INEC decides to go rogue, it could do a lot of damage. It would be recalled that in 2023 Justice Inyang Okoro led Supreme Court Presidential Petition Panel said that INEC is at liberty to prescribe the mode of collating results during an election and that IReV is not a collation centre and shouldn’t be a reason to invalidate the results of an election. More recently, the Supreme Court has also affirmed the right of INEC to prescribe guidelines that affect political party primaries and membership. We recall that in June 2002, INEC rejected the registration applications of over 24 political associations. It was the Supreme Court that declared its action void and ordered the registration of the associations. That judgment became a precedent that once an association had met the constitutional requirements, INEC was bound to comply with its registration in line with the decision of INEC v. Balarabe Musa (2003) 3 NWLR (Pt. 806). In 2007, INEC arbitrarily disqualified Atiku Abubakar from contesting the 2007 election because he had been indicted by a tribunal, even without conviction. It was still the same Supreme Court that restricted their powers and held that INEC had no power to disqualify a candidate from contesting the election.

Since then, almost all judgments seem to favour the administrative actions of INEC, even when they are a clog in the wheels of democracy. The fear now is that on-going attempts to block major opposition candidates. In his address at the press conference on Tuesday, the INEC Chairman confirmed receipt of the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the Supreme Court judgment on the validity of key provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 following a legal challenge by the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) affirming the constitutionality of some sections of the Electoral Act 2026. The Supreme Court judgment concerns Sections 77(5), 77(6), 77(7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which regulate political parties’ membership registers and the nomination of candidates for elective positions.

The court, in a unanimous judgment delivered on 24 September 2026, restored the four provisions after the Court of Appeal had earlier voided them. The court ruled that section 77(5) provides that only members whose names appear on a political party’s membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before a primary, congress or convention can participate in the exercise. Section 77(6) requires political parties to use the membership register submitted to INEC for their primaries, congresses and conventions, while Section 77(7) provides that a party that fails to submit its register within the stipulated period cannot field a candidate in an election. Section 84(2) provides that political parties shall nominate candidates for elective positions through direct primaries or consensus. The Supreme Court held that the provisions were consistent with the Nigerian Constitution and consequently restored the judgment of the Federal High Court, which had earlier dismissed the legal challenge to the provisions. INEC now has the tools to mess up opposition candidates if it decides to do so.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A professor of Political Science and development consultant/expert, Jibrin Ibrahim is a Senior Fellow of the Centre for Democracy and Development, and Chair of the Editorial Board of PREMIUM TIMES.

World.title: NNPC petrol discount is not fuel subsidy — Finance minister
World.content:
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said the discount on petrol to be sold at Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Retail stations is a commercial decision by the retailer and does not amount to a return of fuel subsidy.

In a statement issued on Friday, Mr Oyedele said the discount was being funded by NNPC Retail through a reduction in its retail profit margin, rather than from the Federal Government’s budget or the Federation Account.

He said the arrangement was intended to offer some relief to motorists without reversing the removal of petrol subsidy in May 2023.

“A margin discount means the retailer chooses to take a smaller margin, or no margin at all for a period, and passes the saving to the customer. The cost of the discount is borne by the retailer alone,” he said.

The clarification comes a day after the Federal Government announced a 30-day discount on petrol sold at NNPC stations, with public transport operators expected to receive priority under the arrangement.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that Mr Oyedele warned that restoring fuel subsidy could cost Nigeria more than N20 trillion annually and put additional pressure on government finances, the naira and petrol prices.

How the discount works

Mr Oyedele explained that NNPC Retail buys petrol from the Dangote Refinery and other suppliers at market prices before adding its retail margin to determine the pump price.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Under the discount arrangement, the company reduces or temporarily gives up part of that margin, allowing it to sell petrol at a lower price without the government paying the difference.

He distinguished this from the former subsidy system, under which public revenue was used to cover part of the cost of petrol.

The minister said selling crude oil owned by the Federation below market prices would be different because the resulting shortfall would ultimately be borne by public revenue.

He also argued that the discount could benefit NNPC Retail commercially if lower prices attracted more customers and increased sales volumes.

According to him, higher sales could offset the reduced margin per litre and potentially support the company’s profits and dividend payments to the Federation.

Government defends targeted relief

Mr Oyedele said the discount was part of broader measures to reduce the pressure of high fuel prices on households and businesses without restoring a blanket subsidy.

Other measures announced by the government include a proposed ceiling of N1,350 per litre on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol, expanded compressed natural gas deployment, additional support for vulnerable households and subsidised credit for small businesses and consumers.

The government is also considering an excess-profit tax on operators found to be taking undue advantage of consumers during the energy crisis. Mr Oyedele said proceeds would be directed towards measures to cushion the impact of fuel prices on vulnerable people.

The minister said the NNPC Retail discount was unlikely to create the same incentive for cross-border fuel smuggling associated with previous subsidy arrangements. He argued that retail margins account for less than five per cent of the pump price, limiting the extent to which the discount could widen the price gap between Nigeria and neighbouring countries.

He acknowledged that fuel prices remained a burden on households and businesses but maintained that targeted interventions were preferable to a return to a subsidy system that the government says it can no longer afford.

The new clarification comes amid continued public debate over the rising cost of petrol and calls for the government to do more to ease the impact on transport costs and household spending.

World.title: Comoros vs Nigeria Preview: Super Falcons begin 2028 Olympic race in Ikenne
World.content:
The Super Falcons will begin their quest for a second consecutive Olympic appearance on Friday when they face Comoros in the first leg of their second-round African qualifying tie for the Los Angeles 2028 Women’s Football Tournament.

Nigeria, Africa’s most successful women’s national team, return to Olympic qualifying after their appearance at Paris 2024 ended a 16-year absence from the competition. However, the road to Los Angeles presents another demanding challenge, with only two African nations guaranteed places at the Games.

The first leg is scheduled for 6:00 p.m. Nigerian time on Friday, 9 October, at Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, Ogun State.

Despite Comoros being the nominal home team, the match will take place in Nigeria because the island nation does not have a stadium approved by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) for international fixtures. Consequently, both legs of the tie will be played at the same venue, with the return fixture scheduled for Tuesday.

For interim head coach Augustine Eguavoen, the encounter represents his first official assignment in charge of the Super Falcons and an opportunity to begin the Olympic qualification campaign with a convincing performance.

But while Nigeria enter the tie with significantly greater international experience, Comoros arrive with confidence after an extraordinary opening round in which they scored 30 goals without conceding.

Nigeria’s Olympic qualification campaign begins in round two

The Super Falcons were among the highest-ranked teams in the qualifying competition and received a bye into the second round, allowing them to avoid the opening stage.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Comoros, meanwhile, earned their place in the second round after dismantling Sudan over two legs in June.

Nigeria’s pedigree in African women’s football is unquestionable. The Falcons have won the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations a record 10 times and remain one of the continent’s most recognisable teams.

However, continental dominance has not always translated into smooth Olympic qualification campaigns.

Nigeria returned to the women’s Olympic football tournament at Paris 2024 after missing the previous four editions. Their participation in France was a significant achievement, and they will now be determined to make the Games for a second consecutive time.

The challenge is straightforward in principle but unforgiving in practice: negotiate five knockout rounds and finish among the two African teams that qualify for Los Angeles.

That leaves little room for a poor two-legged tie, particularly against opponents who have already demonstrated their ability to score heavily.

Comoros arrive after a 30-goal qualifying statement

Comoros could hardly have made a more emphatic start to their Olympic qualifying campaign.

They opened their first-round tie against Sudan with a staggering 17-0 victory on 4 June before completing the job with a 13-0 win in the return fixture on 8 June.

The result gave them a remarkable 30-0 aggregate victory, with the team scoring 30 times and keeping clean sheets in both matches.

Among the standout performers were Houmadi and H. Ahamada, who scored four goals each across the two games. Boina Ali added three goals, while Maoulida and D. Saïd were also among the scorers.
