World.title: Olowolafe Unveils Devt Blueprint for Ekiti
World.content:
Founder of the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation and Chancellor of Ekiti State University (EKSU), Dr. Tunji Olowolafe, has unveiled an ambitious development blueprint for Ekiti State, calling for a deliberate transition from its reputation as a centre of learning to an economy driven by skills, technology, industrial production, and wealth creation.

Olowolafe, who delivered the lead paper at the Ekiti at 30 Future Summit held at the Obafemi Awolowo Civic and Convention Centre in Ado-Ekiti, said the state must now convert its formidable intellectual capital into measurable economic prosperity.

Speaking on the theme: ‘The Path to Ekiti’s Greatness: Opportunities, Choices, and Imperatives for the Next 30 Years’, Olowolafe identified reliable power, practical vocational skills and direct access to industrial supply chains and global markets as three critical requirements for the state’s economic transformation.

He proposed an immediate technical audit of Ekiti’s 177 political wards with a view to establishing renewable-energy microgrids capable of powering schools, health centres, workshops, and small businesses.

According to him, solar microgrids of between 300 and 500 kilowatts could serve many of the wards, describing such projects as bankable and within the state’s capacity to execute with support from the Rural Electrification Agency (REA).

Olowolafe also called for a significant expansion of vocational and technical education, arguing that the emerging global economy would increasingly reward practical competence in areas such as solar installation, welding, fabrication, machinery repair, food processing and other high-value trades.

While acknowledging the six government technical colleges already established by the state, he said they were inadequate to meet the demand from young people across Ekiti State’s 16 local government areas.

He advocated the modernisation of their curricula and the recruitment of master vocational instructors from countries with strong technical education systems, including Switzerland, Germany, Canada and South Africa.

Olowolafe further urged major industries to participate directly in curriculum design, training and recruitment from technical colleges, saying the status of vocational education would rise once young people could clearly see pathways from the workshop to well-paying jobs.

He said Ekiti State already possessed the fundamentals required to prosper in a rapidly changing world, citing its education culture, tertiary institutions, professional excellence and disciplined work ethic.

But he warned that advances in artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology, automation and new energy systems were changing the global economy at unprecedented speed and that states and societies unable to adapt risked being left behind.

Olowolafe praised the continuity that had characterised some major development initiatives in Ekiti State, citing the Ekiti Knowledge Zone and the Ekiti Agro-Allied International Cargo Airport.

He noted that the airport represents an example of successive administrations building on one another’s efforts, from its conception by former Governor Segun Oni, through land acquisition and site clearing under former Governor Ayodele Fayose, construction under former Governor Kayode Fayemi, and completion under Governor Biodun Oyebanji.

Turning to agriculture, the businessman and medical doctor challenged the state to move aggressively from production of raw commodities to value addition.

Using cocoa as an example, Olowolafe questioned why, despite Ekiti’s pool of universities, engineers, scientists and artisans, farmers were still drying cocoa beans in primitive conditions rather than using affordable locally produced solar-powered dryers.

He said Ekiti State produced about 4,500 tons of cocoa in 2025 and proposed a clear objective that cocoa grown in the state should increasingly be processed into chocolate and other finished products at source.

“The central question,” he said, was how Ekiti State could turn knowledge and innovation into progress capable of lifting communities out of poverty.

The same principle, he added, should apply to solid minerals, with Ekiti State developing the scientific and technical capacity to identify, process and derive greater economic value from its mineral resources rather than exporting them in raw form.

Olowolafe also announced three major commitments by the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation towards supporting the state’s development agenda.

Under the first initiative, the foundation, working with the Ekiti State Government, would install and upgrade modern Information and Communication Technology centres in the state’s six government technical colleges, modelled after the GOMTECH ICT Centre in Are-Ekiti, with solar power and high-speed Starlink internet.

The foundation would also recruit international vocational training experts on its payroll to support teachers, train students and assist in reforming the technical college curriculum, with success measured by the number of graduates who secure professional certification, employment or establish businesses.

Thirdly, Olowolafe pledged that the foundation would work with leading mining schools in Canada and South Africa in a bid to make EKSU’s Department of Geology the best in Africa within five years.

At EKSU, he said the foundation’s Project Digi-Teach was aimed at bringing all 650 lecturers to full digital teaching proficiency, while high-speed Starlink internet had been installed at 12 locations across the university campus.

He challenged the present generation to demonstrate similar courage.

“Ekiti State has mineral resources, cash crops and excellent human capital. Our first 30 years proved that the state could exist. The next 10 must prove that Ekiti State will lead,” he declared.

World.title: Anosike Plans to Industrialise Umuahia, Make It True State Capital
World.content:
The Governorship Candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Abia State, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, has unveiled plans to develop and industrialise Umuahia to make it a cosmopolitan city befitting of a state capital.

Anosike spoke when a group known as Umuahia Urban Men paid him a courtesy visit in Umuahia to declare their support for his governorship ambition.

He lamented that Umuahia, the state capital, has remained underdeveloped because successive governors who relocated governance to their home areas.

“Umuahia is not developing. Part of the reason is that every state governor moves the state capital to his area. Anywhere the governor comes from is where the state capital moves. This has made businesses in Umuahia to be dying, instead of growing,” Anosike said.

According to him, the lack of commitment to the capital city is evident in the fact that former governors do not even own homes in Umuahia.

“The former governors, none has a home in Umuahia. They don’t have any house. In Umuahia, all the former governors have no joy and pride to own a house in the state capital. It is a plan not to develop Umuahia. So, we will put an end to it,” he declared.

Anosike said if elected to become the governor, his administration would be determined to reverse the trend by developing Umuahia into a cosmopolitan city with an industrial layout

“Our determination is to develop Umuahia into a cosmopolitan city. It will not be wrong to site an industrial layout at Ohiya. It’s the government that will designate it. Companies will come in to develop it. So that businesses will boom here. Activities will pick up,” he said.

He explained that deliberate government policy to favour Umuahia will translate to more money for residents and businesses.

“If government policy changes in favour of the city, it will translate to more money in your pockets.

“If I emerge and my administration comes and gives attention to this city and injects funds, uses local contractors who are living here, they stay here and they spend their money, in three months, you will see the difference. But you see, the problem here is that those that work for the government, (particularly major contractors), don’t spend their money here. When they get their money, they wire it to their companies and families. We will use local contractors but we will not do substandard work,” he said.

The PDP flag bearer further revealed plans to set up industries as private enterprises rather than government bureaucracies.

“We plan to set up a battery factory in Umuahia but it will be run like a private enterprise, not a bureaucracy. The State government can register an investment company. It will run like a private enterprise because it is profit-oriented. Why can’t we have Abia Cement? We have limestone. I can bring Chinese and we float Abia Cement company like a limited liability company. There is a lot to be done for anyone who has genuine intention to develop the state,” he said.

Anosike said his administration will create agencies to drive development, including Operation Feed Abia (OFA) for agricultural revolution and food security, Abia Labour and Global Opportunities Agency (ALGOA) to create jobs for youths, Traders Micro-finance Bank for cooperative financing with collateral-free and interest-free loans, as well as health insurance and subsidy.

On recreation, he decried the absence of leisure facilities in Umuahia.

“There is no form of organization in Umuahia. I’ve not seen an amusement park, wonderland or a water park. What you see in big cities for birthdays, parties, ceremonies and so on. Those are one of the low-hanging fruits that we need to set up. Imagine if they have an amusement centre here with a gaming centre inside it and water parks. It’s even a way to generate money for the state,” he said.

He assured the people that Abia has enough resources to develop, noting that local governments alone have received about N350 billion in three years, with the least monthly allocation at N500 million.

Earlier, the Chairman of Umuahia Urban Men for Good Leadership, Hon. Endy Paschal, had said that the group resolved to identify with Anosike because they believed in his manifesto.

“After our deliberations, we decided to pay a courtesy visit to you because, indeed, we believe that come next election, by His grace, that you will be the governor of Abia State. So on that note, we decided to associate with you, to let you know that Urban Men are in existence in Umuahia. And we have much part to play in your government,” he said.

World.title: Cape Town makes two of the world’s top city lists
World.content:
Cape Town has been named one of the world’s best and friendliest cities in the latest Condé Nast Traveller Readers’ Choice Awards. Image: canva

Cape Town has once again earned a place among the world’s top cities, with international travellers naming the Mother City one of the best and friendliest cities on the planet.

The city ranked 15th among the world’s best cities and 10th among the friendliest, according to the latest Condé Nast Traveller Readers’ Choice Awards.

It was also the only African city to appear on either list.



The awards were based on almost 800 000 responses from readers in the United Kingdom, who rated their travel experiences around the world.

Cape Town makes two global lists

Cape Town scored 88.33 in the best cities category, placing it 15th overall.

The magazine highlighted the city’s combination of beaches, mountains, vineyards and nightlife, describing it as a place that offers visitors “the best of both worlds”.

Its position on the friendliness list was even stronger.

Cape Town scored 96.00, placing it 10th among the world’s friendliest cities.

That is a drop from third place in 2025, but the Mother City remains firmly inside the global top 10.



Condé Nast Traveller pointed to attractions including Table Mountain and Boulders Beach, while also highlighting the South African braai as an important part of the city’s social culture.

Why Cape Town keeps attracting visitors

Cape Town’s appeal stretches well beyond its famous scenery.

Visitors can spend the morning on one of the city’s beaches, head into the Winelands in the afternoon and finish the day at a rooftop bar or restaurant. The city’s cultural diversity and food scene are also major attractions.

Alderman James Vos, the City’s Mayoral Committee Member for Economic Growth, said Cape Town’s friendly reputation is closely connected to what makes the city such a popular destination.

“Yes, the beaches and mountains are beautiful beyond compare, but it’s Capetonians who are so welcoming to visitors.”

Vos said Cape Town’s cuisine was likely part of the reason for the country’s strong showing.

“Cuisine is one of the most remarkable aspects of Cape Town and South Africa,” he said, adding that the country’s food reflects its history and mix of cultures.

Tourism is big business for Cape Town

The rankings come as Cape Town heads into its peak visitor period. Tourism generated R24.5 billion in direct spending in Cape Town during 2025, while the sector supported more than 106 000 jobs.

The City has set ambitious targets for the years ahead, aiming to reach R35 billion in tourism spending and 234 041 tourism jobs by 2030.

It plans to pursue this through increased destination marketing, stronger airline partnerships and efforts to turn visitor interest into more bookings, longer stays and higher spending.

World.title: Durban-born judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
World.content:
Navi Pillay started her legal career in apartheid-era Durban, representing people the state wanted silenced.

Decades later, she has received the world’s most famous peace award.

On Friday, 9 October, the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to the South African judge.



Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, 85, was honoured “for her efforts to promote peace and international law.”

It’s the 125th Nobel Peace Prize, and it puts Pillay alongside some of South Africa’s most famous names.

WHY NAVI PILLAY WON THE NOBEL PEACE PRIZE

According to Al Jazeera, the committee said Pillay had been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

Committee chair Jørgen Watne Frydnes warned that the system of international law “is under tremendous pressure, and its institutions are under attack”.

The committee also said that the ability to resolve conflicts without force or violence depends on the international rule of law.

Pillay was chosen from 287 nominations.



The prize comes with 12 million Swedish kronor (about R20 million).

FROM APARTHEID-ERA DURBAN TO THE WORLD’S COURTS

Pillay was born on 23 September 1941 in working-class Clairwood, Durban, into a family of Indian Tamil origin. Her father was a bus driver.

In 1967, she became the first woman to start a law practice in what was then Natal province.

During apartheid, she acted as a defence lawyer for Nelson Mandela and other anti-apartheid activists.

She also helped shape South Africa’s democracy. As a member of the Women’s National Coalition, she contributed to the equality clause in the Constitution, which prohibits discrimination on grounds including race, gender, religion and sexual orientation.

She later became the first non-white woman judge of the High Court of South Africa.

A CAREER IN INTERNATIONAL JUSTICE

Pillay’s work took her far beyond South Africa.

She spent eight years on the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, which prosecuted those responsible for the 1994 genocide. For the last four, from 1999 to 2003, she served as its president.

Her work there helped establish rape as an act of genocide, a landmark in international law.

From 2003 to 2008, she served as a judge at the International Criminal Court (ICC). She then became United Nations (UN) High Commissioner for Human Rights.

She still sits on the International Court of Justice (ICJ), in the case in which Myanmar is accused of genocide.

In 2025, she headed an independent UN Commission of Inquiry which found that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza.

The commission does not speak on behalf of the UN. According to Reuters, Israel dismissed the report as “scandalous”.

‘I MAY SHARE THIS PRIZE WITH TRUMP’

Pillay reacted to the news with her trademark humour.

When she was told she’d won, she said she first thought “it must be a joke.”

As a lawyer and a judge, she added, she still wanted to verify it.

Later, speaking to a standing ovation in Nuremberg, Germany, she joked: “If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump.”

The quip was a reference to US President Donald Trump, who has made no secret of wanting to win the prize himself. The 2025 winner, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, even gave Trump her Nobel medal.

The moment was captured by Amnesty International secretary-general Agnès Callamard and shared on X.

SOUTH AFRICA’S NOBEL PEACE PRIZE WINNERS

Pillay joins a proud list of South African Nobel Peace Prize laureates.

Chief Albert Luthuli won in 1960. Archbishop Desmond Tutu followed in 1984. Nelson Mandela and FW de Klerkshared the prize in 1993.

That makes Pillay the fifth South African, and the first South African woman, to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

She will receive the award at a ceremony in Oslo on 10 December.

A bus driver’s daughter from Clairwood, who grew up under apartheid, now standing where Luthuli, Tutu and Mandela once stood.

Whatever your view of the cases she’s worked on, it’s a proud day for Durban, and for South Africa.

World.title: Saleng and Nkota could decide the MTN8 final and here’s how
World.content:
Monnapule Saleng and Mohau Nkota could make their first appearances of the season when Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns meet in the MTN8 final on Saturday.

The two South African football giants will battle for the trophy at Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban, with both sides hoping to get their hands on silverware.

Nkota, who joined Pirates on loan from Saudi Arabian club Al-Ettifaq, was spotted in training this week after recovering from an injury.



The winger could make a surprise appearance in the final, with coach Abdeslam Ouaddou potentially handing him an opportunity in the second half. His pace and attacking ability could provide the Buccaneers with an additional option as they look to overcome Sundowns.

Meanwhile, Saleng has also returned to training at Sundowns, raising hopes that he could feature against his former club.

The winger’s future at Chloorkop had been uncertain following reports of a fallout with head coach Miguel Cardoso. However, his return to training suggests that the situation may be improving.



Saleng has unfinished business with Pirates

Having previously played for Pirates and scored in an MTN8 final, Saleng could now find himself facing his former teammates in a potentially intriguing storyline.

Former Sundowns midfielder Brent Carelse, who scored the winning goal the last time the Brazilians defeated Pirates in a cup final, has welcomed Saleng’s return.

“That’s good for him personally and good for the team. I think he’s a player we need, he’s got a lot of creativity and the fans obviously like him, they obviously would like to see him playing,” Carelse told KickOff.



“So, hopefully he will get back into the squad and back into the field as quickly as possible. But we’re excited to see him come back again.”

Who will win the final?

World.title: Orlando Pirates get their ‘engine’ back just in time for the MTN8 final
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have received an almighty boost ahead of their glittering MTN8 final against Mamelodi Sundowns.

Pirates meet Sundowns in another MTN8 final

90 minutes, or perhaps more, separates Pirates from an unprecedented fifth consecutive MTN8 crown. Is Dlamini back in time for Orlando Pirates?

World.title: Pollen levels remain high in three South African cities this week
World.content:
Tree pollen remains high in parts of South Africa, raising concerns for people with seasonal allergies. Image: Unsplash

Tree pollen levels have dropped in several parts of South Africa, but Cape Town, Pretoria and Potchefstroom continue to record high concentrations.

The latest pollen report shows that tree pollen remains the main concern for people who suffer from seasonal allergies.

Cape Town also recorded moderate grass pollen levels, while weed pollen and mould concentrations remained generally low across the monitoring sites.



Cape Town: Tree pollen remains high

Cape Town continues to record high tree pollen levels, with olive trees contributing the most pollen.

Other trees releasing pollen include cypress, pine, oak, mulberry, gum, plane and yellowwood.

Grass pollen has reached moderate levels, making Cape Town the only monitored city to record moderate grass concentrations this week.



Weed pollen remains low, while mould levels are generally low despite occasional increases in Alternaria, a type of mould that can trigger allergies.

Johannesburg: Rain helps reduce pollen

Johannesburg recorded low tree, grass and weed pollen levels this week.

Rain throughout the week likely helped wash pollen out of the air, reducing the amount people could breathe in.



Trees releasing pollen included birch, false olive, mulberry, plane, pine and oak.

Mould concentrations also remained low.

Pretoria: High tree pollen expected

Pretoria continues to face high tree pollen levels, although the monitoring team could not analyse this week’s sample.



A courier delay prevented the pollen strip from arriving in time, so researchers used six-year averages to estimate conditions.

The estimates indicate high tree pollen levels, with possible contributions from jacaranda, acacia, cypress, olive, pine, oak and several other trees.

Weed pollen and mould levels are expected to remain low.



Bloemfontein and Kimberley: Pollen levels drop

Bloemfontein recorded a decline in tree pollen, with concentrations falling to low levels.

Several trees continue to flower, including acacia, cypress, gum, olive, oak and karee.

Weed pollen and mould levels also remained low.

Kimberley recorded low pollen concentrations across all categories. The monitoring station detected pollen from several trees, including birch, cypress, pine, plane and elm, but found no weed pollen.



Durban and Gqeberha: Low pollen levels

Durban recorded low tree, grass and weed pollen concentrations.

Trees releasing pollen included jacaranda, cypress, birch, gum, oak and yellowwood.

The monitoring station also detected several weed types and fern spores, although overall concentrations remained low.



Gqeberha recorded similarly low pollen levels across all categories.

Trees contributing pollen included acacia, cedar, cypress, gum, olive, pine and yellowwood.

Mould concentrations remained low in both coastal cities.



George: Low pollen levels expected

George is expected to experience low pollen concentrations across all categories.

Researchers used two-year averages to estimate conditions at this monitoring site.

Trees that may contribute pollen include Australian pine, cypress and yellowwood, while grass, weed and mould concentrations are expected to remain low.



Potchefstroom: Pine pollen dominates

Potchefstroom remains one of the areas with high tree pollen concentrations this week.

Pine trees contributed the most pollen, while birch, olive, cypress, mulberry, oak and yellowwood also released pollen.

Grass and mould levels remained low, with rainfall helping to reduce concentrations.



Weed pollen included pigweed, plantain, sedges and bulrush.

What should allergy sufferers know?

Although pollen levels have dropped in several cities, people who suffer from seasonal allergies may still experience symptoms in areas with high tree pollen concentrations.

Pollen can trigger sneezing, itchy eyes, a runny nose and nasal congestion.



Rain can temporarily reduce airborne pollen, while dry and windy conditions can carry pollen through the air.

The latest readings also show that pollen levels can vary considerably between cities, even during the same week.

World.title: Rainy days and dogs: What every pet owner should know
World.content:
Dogs that drink from puddles after rainfall may encounter harmful bacteria, parasites and chemicals. Image: Unsplash

Your dog may love splashing through puddles after a downpour, but drinking the water could put its health at risk.

With rain and thundershowers expected in parts of South Africa, pet owners should pay attention to where their dogs drink water during outdoor walks.

A puddle might look harmless, especially after fresh rainfall, but standing water can collect dirt, animal waste and other contaminants.



While clean rainwater is not necessarily dangerous, water that collects on roads, pavements and in gardens can pose health risks.

Bacteria can hide in puddles

One of the risks associated with contaminated water is leptospirosis, a bacterial disease that affects animals and humans.

Infected animals, including rodents, can spread the bacteria through their urine.

When infected urine contaminates water or soil, dogs can become infected by drinking the water or coming into contact with it through their eyes, mouth or damaged skin.

Leptospirosis can cause fever, vomiting, loss of appetite, muscle pain and weakness.

In severe cases, the infection can damage the kidneys or liver.



Parasites can cause stomach problems

Puddles and other contaminated water sources can also expose dogs to Giardia, a microscopic parasite that infects the intestines.

Infected animals shed the parasite in their faeces, allowing it to spread into water and the surrounding environment.

Dogs can become infected when they swallow contaminated water.

Giardia commonly causes diarrhoea, although some infected dogs show no symptoms.

Other dogs may experience vomiting, weight loss or a reduced appetite.

Roadside puddles can contain chemicals

Bacteria and parasites are not the only concerns.

Rainwater can wash oil, fuel, antifreeze and other chemicals from roads and parking areas into puddles.

Antifreeze containing ethylene glycol is particularly dangerous because even a small amount can cause severe poisoning in dogs.

Dogs that swallow it may develop vomiting, weakness, poor coordination or seizures. The chemical can also cause life-threatening kidney damage.

How can you keep your dog safe?

You do not have to stop taking your dog outside whenever it rains. However, a few precautions can reduce the risk of illness.

Rainwater itself does not automatically make dogs sick.

As rainy conditions continue in parts of the country, keeping fresh water available for your dog is one simple way to help prevent unnecessary health risks.

Does your dog try to drink from puddles after it rains?

World.title: ‘Pirates were very aggressive’: Rulani reveals on how Downs lost out on Mofokeng
World.content:
Pyramids FC head coach Rulani Mokwena has revealed that he wanted Mamelodi Sundowns to sign Relebohile Mofokeng while the winger was still at the School of Excellence.

After leaving the School of Excellence at 17, Mofokeng spent four years at Orlando Pirates before making a move to Royal Union Saint-Gilloise in July.

Speaking in an interview with the South African Football Journalists Association (SAFJA), Mokwena explained how he identified the talented playmaker during an Engen Knockout competition match between the School of Excellence and Orlando Pirates.



Rulani wanted Mofokeng at Sundowns

The former Sundowns coach said he immediately contacted Shawn Bishop, who was then involved in youth development, methodology and coaching at the club’s academy, to recommend that they sign the youngster.

“One thing that I have to say, and Shawn Bishop, if you get a chance to speak to him, will tell you, there was an Engen Knockout match between School of Excellence and Orlando Pirates. Immediately I got onto the phone to Shawn, who was the Head of Youth and Methodology and Coaching with the academy at Sundowns. And I said, ‘Shawn, there’s a number 10 that you have to sign at School of Excellence,'” Mokwena said.

However, Sundowns were not the only club interested in securing Mofokeng’s services, with Pirates also working aggressively to recruit the promising youngster.



“Orlando Pirates was very, very aggressive with trying to also secure him,” Mokwena added.

Although Rulani was unable to bring Mofokeng to Sundowns, he believes the winger benefited greatly from his time at Pirates, where he was given opportunities to develop and establish himself in the first team.

Reflecting on what might have happened had the player joined Sundowns instead, Mokwena acknowledged that his career could have taken a different path.



“He could have been at Sundowns, but then we wouldn’t know whether the story would be the same or not. But Orlando Pirates was very important for him because they gave him the opportunity to play,” he said.

Mofokeng spent three successful seasons with the Buccaneers senior team before he left for Belgium.

Do you believe Rulani’s story?

World.title: Cape Town gets two new direct routes to tropical island destinations
World.content:
Two new Airlink routes now connect Cape Town directly with Mauritius and Zanzibar. Image: canva / supplied

Cape Town travellers have two new reasons to look toward the Indian Ocean, with Airlink adding direct flights to both Mauritius and Zanzibar.

The airline has officially launched its new Cape Town–Mauritius and Cape Town–Zanzibar services this month.

Both routes give travellers a direct alternative to connecting through Johannesburg, making it easier to reach two of the region’s most popular island destinations.



Cape Town to Mauritius

Airlink launched its first-ever route to Mauritius on 2 October 2026, operating twice a week between Cape Town and the Indian Ocean island.

The airline is operating the route with its new Embraer E195-E2 aircraft, which can carry 124 passengers.

Flights operate on Tuesdays and Fridays.

Flight Days Route Departure Arrival 4Z 350 Tue, Fri Cape Town → Mauritius 10:05 17:15 4Z 351 Tue, Fri Mauritius → Cape Town 18:15 22:35

The daytime schedule is designed to give holidaymakers more usable time at their destination while also making the route practical for business travellers.

Mauritius attracted more than 1.4 million visitors in 2025, with South Africa among its biggest source markets.



The island is known for its beaches and resorts, but also has established business links with South Africa. More than 140 South African businesses operate across sectors including agriculture, manufacturing, consumer goods and ICT.

Cape Town to Zanzibar

The second new route now connects Cape Town directly with Zanzibar from 3 October 2026.

Airlink will operate the route once a week on Saturdays, also using the E195-E2.

Flight Day Route Departure Arrival 4Z 356 Saturday Cape Town → Zanzibar 08:15 14:30 4Z 357 Saturday Zanzibar → Cape Town 15:30 20:50

The flight takes just over six hours, with the schedule offering daytime departures and arrivals.

Until now, travellers flying between Cape Town and Zanzibar had to face a connection through Johannesburg. The new service removes that extra leg.

Zanzibar is a major leisure destination, particularly popular for its white-sand beaches, warm Indian Ocean waters and historic Stone Town.

New aircraft on both routes

Both services are being operated using Airlink’s new Embraer E195-E2, which has a 124-seat, two-class configuration.

One of the biggest differences for passengers is that there are no middle seats. The aircraft has a two-by-two Economy Class layout, meaning passengers get either a window or aisle seat.

Airlink’s Business Class cabin also uses a staggered configuration designed to provide additional personal space. Passengers can expect complimentary meals and beverages, along with power outlets, large windows and overhead storage.

World.title: 6,113 voters, six metros: Inside MarkData's election survey
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - In any survey, the method used to reach the results is key.

This survey was conducted by prominent market research company MarkData.

To maximise the response rate, personal interviews were used in township, lower-income and middle-income areas. Telephonic interviews were used in higher-income, gated communities and unsafe areas.

The survey was conducted in six metros: Cape Town, Ekurhuleni, eThekwini, Johannesburg, Nelson Mandela Bay and Tshwane.

The people polled were registered voters 18 years and older, residing in South Africa, who intended to vote in this election.

A multistage random probability sample design was used to draw the sample. A probability sample means that every person in the target population had an equal chance of being selected. Multistage refers to three stages of selection to ensure random, non-biased selection. The three stages of selection were the enumerator area, the household within the enumerator area and the respondent within a household.

The sampling frame was generated from a top-down and bottom-up approach, using the latest released StatsSA census and mid-year estimates, and the GeoTerraImage national Building Census (structure/dwelling unit type) dataset, respectively – an updated version of the SA population.

The sampling frame information included, among others, the number of households, number of people, numbers per population group, gender, age, and neighbourhood lifestyle index (NLI™©).

Regarding telephone interviews, a database of more than 14 million contact numbers from the credit bureau is linked to the sampling frame already referred to was used as sampling basis. Higher-income respondents were randomly selected from the linked telephone database.

The realised sample and margin of error by metro were:

Realised sample Margin of error at a 95% confidence level Cape Town 1004 ±3.09 Ekurhuleni 1019 ±3.07 eThekwini 1039 ±3.04 Johannesburg 1011 ±3.08 Nelson Mandela Bay 994 ±3.11 Tshwane 1046 ±3.03 Total 6113

The sample design was disproportionate to ensure that smaller groups and areas were sufficiently represented.

To correct these disproportions, the results were weighted back to the correct population proportions (as per StatsSA Midyear estimates), IEC data on registration, and data on registration vs intention to vote as collected during the survey.

Interviews were conducted at respondents’ homes or telephonically in their language of choice by supervised experienced interviewers from 10 August to 14 September 2026.

At least 20 percent back checks were conducted in the field and at the office to ensure correct completion of the questionnaires.

World.title: Man City face Anfield cauldron after guilty Premier League verdicts
World.content:
LONDON - Manchester City are set for a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday in their first outing since being found guilty of over 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City have appealed and proclaim their innocence, but the Premier League leaders' place in the division is now at threat following findings they used "sham" sponsorship deals to inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).

Manchester United and Tottenham are both badly in need of a win when they meet at Old Trafford, while Arsenal aim to bounce back at home to Leeds following a rare defeat.

AFP Sports looks at the pick of the action as the English top-flight returns after a three-week international break.

City's transformation into the dominant force in English football since an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover 18 years ago has cost Liverpool more than most.

The charges labelled against City cover the period between 2009 and 2018, but the foundations they built in that time ensured they remained the Premier League's top dogs during the bulk of Pep Guardiola's subsequent time in charge.

Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool twice missed out on the title to Guardiola's side despite amassing over 90 points.

Those battles to be crowned champions of England over the past decade have turned this fixture into the Premier League's marquee match-up and the eyes of the football world will be on Anfield again come Sunday.

City have won every game since Enzo Maresca replaced Guardiola, but their title challenge is likely to be ruined by a sanction unless they can overturn the verdict of an independent commission.

Liverpool will seek to capitalise on City's uncertainty and kickstart their own campaign.

Andoni Iraola remains unbeaten as Liverpool manager but draws against Newcastle, Nottingham Forest and Fulham have left the Reds six points off top spot.

"I think it's a big game and I think everyone is expecting to play, to watch, to be part of that game," said Iraola.

"We know we will have to be at our best and also I know that the people will be looking to help the team."

World.title: AI rebrand unlikely to win over sceptical public, experts warn
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Donald Trump's campaign to rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence" is unlikely to win over a wary public and could make matters worse, experts say, even as the US president threatens to treat holdouts as enemies.

On Thursday, he warned that anyone refusing to adopt the term would be considered an "ENEMY" by the White House, without saying what that would mean.

He had floated the name change in September before the UN General Assembly, saying it sounded much better.

"The use of the word artificial makes intelligence fake. It makes it sound fake, and it is not fake. It’s actually amazing," he said.

He later signed an executive order mandating the term in government communications.

According to Jean-Pierre Dube, a marketing professor at the University of Chicago, there is a genuine concern at the White House that the backlash against AI and data centres could "stifle one of the key drivers of economic growth right now" and "cede technological dominance to China."

However, "the idea that a rebrand that mischaracterises the technology will turn around some of the public sentiment seems like wishful thinking," he told AFP.

- 'Poor choice' -

But expert opinion matters little to Trump, who wrote in his book "The Art of the Deal": “I don’t trust fancy marketing surveys. I do my own surveys and draw my own conclusions.”

He even polled users on Truth Social, where "super intelligence" beat out the other option, "superior intelligence."

Americans see Trump as overly enthusiastic about artificial intelligence, which many already use but whose consequences for safety and jobs they fear, while also worrying about the rapid construction of massive data centres.

In a recent Quinnipiac University poll, only 25 percent of voters said they were satisfied with how the 80-year-old Republican is approaching AI, against 58 percent who were dissatisfied.

"If we believe that 'artificial' already encourages fear, 'super' seems like something far more worrisome," said Dube, calling it "a poor choice of new brand."

For Ronald Kline, a historian at Cornell University, "the phrase 'super intelligence' means more than simulating human intelligence; it means going beyond human intelligence," he told AFP.

The term "artificial intelligence" was born in 1956 at an austere summer workshop at Dartmouth College.

Deliberately abstract, it was chosen to bring under one banner the research of scientists from varied backgrounds -- mathematicians, psychologists and engineers driven by the same ambition: teaching computers, at the time enormous calculating machines, to "think" like humans.

Seen by some as a catch-all, the term never won unanimous support from the scientific community, which nonetheless came to accept it -- as did Herbert Simon, winner of the 1978 Nobel Prize in Economics, who wrote as early as 1969: "'artificial intelligence' seems to be here to stay, and it may prove easier to cleanse the phrase than to dispense with it."

For Kline, the name truly took off when it became the acronym AI, associated with the stratospheric growth of companies such as OpenAI.

The ChatGPT maker is not forced to change its name by Trump’s executive order, which applies only to the federal government.

But some of the sector’s top executives have chosen to follow the president, who closely tracks whether his various unilateral name changes are adopted.

The Associated Press news agency drew his wrath for refusing to adopt the name "Gulf of America" in place of "Gulf of Mexico."

The term "super intelligence" has appeared in communications from Meta, Mark Zuckerberg’s group.

Elon Musk, a Trump ally, enthusiastically supports the name change and uses "super intelligence" in his posts on X.

A Washington industry lobbyist interviewed by AFP predicted a pragmatic approach from companies.

"I think you’ll see it used when it has to be used, i.e. when you’re communicating with the administration," he said. "Insisting on 'AI' versus 'super intelligence' isn't a fight you need to pick."

World.title: Seals and sea lions get hearing tested at Australia zoo
World.content:
SYDNEY - Scientists in Australia trained sea lions and seals to respond to a hearing test for research into how the marine mammals are affected by human-made noise.

Keepers at Sydney's Taronga Zoo trained two sea lions and two fur seals to listen to sounds and press a paddle when they heard a tone.

They were rewarded with fish for the right answers.

"Before we can understand whether a noise is affecting an animal, we need to know whether it can hear that noise in the first place," Curtin University professor and lead researcher Christine Erbe said on Thursday.

"These hearing tests give us that baseline and allow us to start asking how noises from ships, boats, aircraft and coastal construction might affect seals and sea lions."

The peer-reviewed study found the pinnipeds were most sensitive to sounds around 3.2 kilohertz.

World.title: EU trade chief seeks 'tangible outcomes' in China talks
World.content:
BEIJING - The European Union's top commerce official said that it was crucial to achieve "tangible outcomes" in talks set to wrap up in China on Friday.

The negotiations follow months of rising tensions between the 27-nation EU and the Asian powerhouse that risk escalating into a full-blown trade war.

"Building on three intensive months of engagement, we're working hard to rebalance EU-China trade," Maros Sefcovic said late Thursday after meeting Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in Beijing.

"It's crucial that the first phase of our talks under the Trade and Investment Consultations delivers tangible outcomes," Sefcovic said on X, posting a photo together with Wang.

Sefcovic had said earlier Thursday that the EU's trade deficit with China, running at around one billion euros ($1.1 billion) every day, was "unsustainable".

Cheaper products coming from China have strangled European industry, resulting in tens of thousands of job losses across the continent.

Many in Europe accuse China of unfair trade practices, including supporting firms with huge subsidies, price-dumping and currency manipulation.

But Europe can ill afford to anger China.

Beijing could throttle supplies of vital items such as rare earth minerals or throw up barriers to European exports to China.

The stakes are also high for President Xi Jinping, however, with China heavily reliant on exports to compensate for its weak domestic economy.

The EU parliament's trade committee chief, Bernd Lange, said ahead of Sefcovic's trip that this "economic crisis in China" gives the bloc "bargaining power".

World.title: Vehicle torched at Constitutional Hill as protests erupt in Joburg CBD
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A vehicle has been torched at the Constitutional Hill Human Rights Precinct as fresh protests erupted in Johannesburg on Friday.

Authorities said multiple protests had been reported in the Johannesburg CBD, with protesters expected to converge on the Constitutional Court.

Motorists and members of the public have been urged to avoid the affected area and exercise extreme caution.

READ | Home Affairs withdraws directive on asylum applications

The protests follow a Constitutional Court judgment delivered on 7 July, which declared certain provisions of the Refugees Act unconstitutional and invalid. The court ruled that asylum seekers could not be denied access to the asylum system solely because of procedural failures.

The judgment was followed by violent protests in Durban and Soweto, during which more than 20 vehicles were torched.

On Friday, the Department of Home Affairs withdrew a directive issued on 28 September concerning the intake of asylum applications.

World.title: Court rules Andile Lungisa’s removal from ANC candidate list 'unlawful'
World.content:
GQEBERHA - The Johannesburg High Court has ordered the ANC to reinstate Andile Lungisa on its proportional representation (PR) candidates list for the Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality.

The court ruled on Friday that Lungisa’s removal from the list was unlawful, invalid and unconstitutional.

The ANC NEC member approached the court after his name was removed from the party’s candidate list, denying him the opportunity to contest the 4 November local government elections.

In court papers, Lungisa said he had been nominated by ANC branches in Nelson Mandela Bay, placed at the top of the list and confirmed as the highest-ranked candidate at the provincial list conference.

He was subsequently shortlisted and publicly announced by ANC president Cyril Ramaphosa as the party’s mayoral candidate for the municipality.

However, Lungisa said his name was removed before the list was submitted to the Electoral Commission of South Africa.

World.title: Mamelodi community demands justice for murdered 14-year-old twins
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Mamelodi West community is demanding justice following the gruesome killing of 14-year-old twin brothers Bonolo and Bohlale Makena.

The boys were found with multiple stab wounds at their home on Friday.

With no arrests made, community members gathered for a candlelight vigil and march to mourn the teenagers and call for those responsible to be brought to justice.

Their mother reportedly returned home from work on Friday afternoon to find her sons dead.

Family members suspect the killer may have been known to the boys, as there were reportedly no signs of forced entry at the property.

Community members are also calling for greater action to address violence against women and children.

Police say they are following up on leads and have urged anyone with information that could assist the investigation to come forward.

World.title: 'Mental' stability delays bail ruling for Mbithe, children in Mutiso murder case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Mbithe and her two children questioned Ndetei’s mental stability and capacity to swear an affidavit relied upon in opposing the accused persons’ release on bail. [File, Standard]

Rose Mbithe and her two children will spend more time in custody after the High Court postponed its bail ruling to first determine a fresh application seeking to question Dr Victoria Mutiso’s husband, Professor David Ndetei, over his mental capacity to swear an affidavit opposing their release on bail.

Milimani High Court Judge Alexander Muteti on Friday deferred the bail ruling, which had been scheduled for October 19, 2026, pending the determination of the fresh application seeking to reopen the bail application hearing and summon Mutiso's husband, Professor David Ndetei, for cross-examination.

Mbithe and her two children, through Lawyer Joel Mbaluka, questioned Ndetei’s mental stability and capacity to swear an affidavit relied upon in opposing the accused persons’ release on bail, arguing that the court needed to establish whether the evidence was reliable.

In his ruling, Justice Muteti said the defence had made the fresh application after the parties had concluded their arguments on bail, meaning the court would first have to determine whether to reopen the bail hearing proceedings.

“The advocates for the first, second and third accused, supported by counsel for the sixth accused, have made an application for summoning of Professor David Ndetei to appear for cross-examination. This application has been made after arguments are closed in respect of the bail application,” the judge said.

He added that the court would deliver its ruling on the fresh application on October 19, 2026, with the decision on bail to await the determination of that application.

Lawyer Mutinda, representing the defence, told the court that the application was intended to help establish the truth and ensure the accused persons’ right to a fair hearing was protected.

“The affidavit by prof dated October 5, 2026 opposing bail is from someone with a confirmed mental infirmity,” Lawyer Mutinda submitted.

The defence further claimed it had received information that Ndetei had been hospitalised in a high-dependency unit (HDU) around the time the affidavit was allegedly made.

The lawyers urged Justice Muteti to summon Ndetei for questioning, arguing that his mental capacity and the circumstances surrounding the preparation of the affidavit required clarification before the court could determine the bail application.

They also sought to have Mbithe, her son Chris Mulwa and daughter Angela Mulwa escorted to IPOA offices to facilitate investigations into their complaints, including alleged assaults at their residence and various police stations in Kilimani and Kileleshwa.

However, the prosecution, through State Counsel Jalson Makori, opposed the application to summon Ndetei, arguing that the defence had previously been allowed to seek cross-examination but had failed to do so.

Makori told the court that the window for making the request had closed and argued that the pre-bail reports ordered by the court could address some of the issues raised by the defence.

He also opposed requests for orders involving the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA), arguing that the authority was not a party to the proceedings and that the court should not direct how it conducts investigations.

In his directions, Justice Muteti said the court would first determine the fresh application before proceeding with the bail ruling.

“The ruling on the bail application shall await the determination and delivery of the said ruling in respect of the two issues,” the judge directed.

The court scheduled the ruling on the fresh application for October 19, 2026, at 10am, postponing the bail decision until the issues are resolved.

The judge also directed that the first, second, third and sixth accused persons be escorted to the prison clinic for treatment.

If the medical officers are unable to handle their medical conditions, the officer in charge should consider referring them to another government health facility.

Aggrieved by the court’s decision to postpone the bail ruling further, Mbithe attempted to address the judge directly, but Justice Alexander Muteti declined her request and cautioned her to speak through her lawyer.

“Mbithe, there is a reason why the framers of our law decided all murder suspects must be represented. Please note that the reason why we have counsel acting for suspect or accused persons in murder cases is not just a cosmetic arrangement; there are real good reasons. Please speak through your counsel,” the judge said.

However, earlier in the proceedings, Lawyer Mbaluka, representing Mbithe and her children, urged the court to release them on bail, arguing that they were willing to comply with any conditions imposed.

He told the court that Mbithe had a fixed abode in Karen and argued that her children, Angela and Chris Mulwa, were advocates who understood the consequences of absconding from court.

The lawyer also told the court that Angela was a single mother of two children aged three and six, who had been left without anyone to escort them to school during her detention.

The seven accused persons are charged with the murder of Dr Mutiso

They are Mbithe Mulwa, also known as Rose Mbithe Ndetei; her children Chris Mulwa and Angela Mulwa; Police Constable Elijah Kibelion Kimoi; Maritim Kimutai, alias Kim; Police Constable Collins Bett Kiplangat; and Pius Muiru Mbugua, alias Headboy.

They have denied the murder charge and are currently held at Langata Women's Prison and the Industrial Remand Prison.

World.title: Revealed: 84 Kenyans killed, 52 missing in Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi. [File,Standard]

The government has records of 354 Kenyans linked to the Russia-Ukraine war, including 84 classified as killed or missing in action and five being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine.

Prime Cabinet Secretary and Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi gave the updated figures in a response to Parliament on the recruitment of Kenyans into the Russian military and the detention of Kenyans in Ukraine on Thursday, October 8.

The records show that 77 Kenyans remain on the front lines, 38 are in camps, 52 have an unknown or unclassified location and 34 are hospitalised.

Another 62 Kenyans have been repatriated, while one is in detention and another has completed a military contract.

The government said Russia has stopped the enlistment of additional Kenyans after Kenya secured the country’s placement on Russia’s ‘Stop List’ during Mudavadi’s visit to Moscow in March.

“The Embassy of Kenya in Moscow has since confirmed that no additional Kenyan nationals have been enlisted in the Special Military Operation following the implementation of the Stop List,” Mudavadi said.

Russian authorities have told Kenya that requests to terminate military contracts will be considered on a case-by-case basis by individual military unit commanders.

Mudavadi said Kenya continues to engage Russian authorities and affected families over the burial, cremation or repatriation of remains after Russia said its Defence Ministry could not meet the cost of repatriating the remains of deceased Kenyans.

Five Kenyans held in Ukraine

Five Kenyan nationals are currently being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine, according to information sent to Kenya by the Ukrainian Embassy in Vienna on September 3.

The government identified them as Evans Kibet, detained since May 2025; Willi Muniu Macharia, detained since November 2025; Haron Kibet Pachenge, detained since March 2026; Joseph, detained since April 2026; and Francis Ndarua Ndungu.

Kenya’s Honorary Consul in Ukraine visited the Zakhid 1 prisoner-of-war camp and reported that the detainees were being held in humane conditions, had access to medical services and were being treated under rules governing prisoners of war.

The government also said Ukraine was holding the remains of four other Kenyans.

They are Simon Gitau, Clinton Nyapara Mogesa, Dennis Bagaka Obwori and Eric Mwangi Nyambura.

Kenya is seeking the release and repatriation of the affected Kenyans through diplomatic channels, including engagement with Ukraine and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

The government wants Kenyans held as prisoners of war to be considered as possible victims of international human trafficking.

Mudavadi said many of the affected Kenyans reported that recruiters lured them with promises of employment before they ended up in military service.

The government says the circumstances surrounding their recruitment could fit the definition of trafficking under Article 3(a) of the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, also known as the Palermo Protocol.

It wants the issue considered during negotiations over their repatriation so the Kenyans can access assistance available to trafficking victims.

President William Ruto has also raised the matter directly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a telephone conversation, according to the government.

Kenya has further received approval from Kyiv for its ambassador to Ukraine, with the government saying this will improve its ability to respond to cases involving Kenyans in the country.

The State Department for Diaspora Affairs said families should report cases to the government as soon as communication with relatives in Russia is disrupted.

Once a family reports a case, the department collects identification details, travel information and next-of-kin contacts before referring the case to the Kenyan Embassy in Moscow for verification.

The government has also facilitated the return of 62 Kenyans who had been involved in Russia’s military operations.

It has provided affected families with updates from diplomatic missions, information on compensation processes, psychosocial support and guidance on the repatriation or burial of remains.

The government said it is also expanding measures to prevent deceptive recruitment by providing pre-departure information, urging Kenyans to verify recruitment agencies and employment offers and strengthening emergency assistance through Kenyan diplomatic missions.

The scale of the recruitment first emerged publicly in February when Parliament was told that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been recruited to fight for Russia.

The National Intelligence Service report presented to lawmakers said recruiters targeted former security personnel and civilians with promises of lucrative employment, salaries and bonuses.

The figures at the time included 89 Kenyans on the frontline, 39 hospitalised, 28 missing in action, 35 in camps or bases, 30 repatriated, one detained and one who had completed a contract.

The government then stepped up diplomatic efforts. In March, Kenya announced an agreement with Russia to stop further enlistment of Kenyans into its military operations and to facilitate consular support and voluntary disengagement for Kenyans already serving.

The issue remains unresolved for many families. More than 30 families affected by the recruitment were reported this week to be seeking a meeting with President Ruto before Kenya's delegation travels to Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit, demanding answers on missing relatives, repatriation of survivors and the return of remains.

World.title: Wajir patient isolated over suspected viral haemorrhagic fever
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home. [File, Standard]

A 20-year-old man in Habaswein, Wajir County, has been isolated after presenting with symptoms consistent with a suspected viral haemorrhagic fever, following recent travel from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

The patient, a resident of Habaswein in Wajir South Sub-County, is currently admitted at Albadar Nursing Home, where he is being treated after developing fever, headache and cough. He was also found to have severe anaemia, with a haemoglobin level of 4g/dL.

According to a disease surveillance report filed at Habaswein Police Station, the patient told health officials that he had recently travelled to the DRC, where he worked as a “tan boy” on a cargo truck or trailer.

He reportedly developed fever and headache while still in the DRC on September 2, 2026, before traveling by trailer to Uganda, where he stayed for about five days and sought medical attention.

The report states that he was treated with antibiotics in Uganda before travelling by trailer to Malaba. From Malaba, he travelled by motorcycle to a relative's residence, where he stayed for approximately five days.

He later travelled by trailer to Nairobi and proceeded by bus to Isiolo, where he stayed for about 10 days before travelling to Habaswein by Probox vehicle. He arrived in the town around September 20.

Upon arrival, the patient sought treatment at Hilac Medical Clinic, where he was managed for pneumonia and septicaemia for about three days.

However, his condition did not improve and he was subsequently transferred to Albadar Nursing Home, where he remains admitted.

The report adds that the patient is receiving intravenous Augmentin and paracetamol and has been transfused with two units of whole blood.

“Despite the above interventions, the patient remains clinically unwell and sick-looking,” the report states.

Authorities have since placed the patient in isolation as investigations continue to establish the cause of his illness.

“Sample collection has been completed, and the specimen will be shipped to National Public Health Laboratories tonight,” the report states.

World.title: Complainant letters cannot be used to initiate judge's removal, court rules
World.content:
Chief Justice Martha Koome. [File]

A letter addressed to the Chief Justice seeking administrative intervention cannot form the basis for removing a judge, the Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) has ruled.

Delivering a unanimous judgment in a case filed by Environment and Land Court Judge Anthony Ombwayo, a three-judge ELRC bench comprising Justices Jemimah Keli, Onesmus Makau, and Dr. Jacob Gikeri ruled that a letter written to the Chief Justice cannot simply be forwarded to the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) and treated as a petition for removal.

World.title: How KNEC plans to stop cheating in 2026 exams
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere. [File]

The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) will use smart padlocks to secure all examination storage containers as more than 3.6 million candidates sit the 2026 national examinations and assessments.

KNEC Chief Executive Officer Dr David Njengere said the council would monitor the containers from its headquarters to prevent anyone from accessing examination papers before the scheduled times.

“Last year KNEC piloted the use of smart padlocks in 250 containers. This year all containers will be secured using the smart padlocks which will be monitored from the KNEC headquarters,” said Dr Njengere.

Under the system, officials will open containers at designated times. Officials will access Kenya Primary School Education Assessment (KPSEA) and Kenya Junior School Education Assessment (KJSEA) papers at 6 a.m., while centre managers will collect Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) papers at 7 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.

However, Dr Njengere identified mobile phones as the biggest challenge in preventing examination malpractice.

“Mobile phones remain our biggest challenge in administration of KCSE examination,” observed Dr Njengere.

He warned that the council would not allow candidates or examination officials to have mobile phones at examination centres during examination sessions.

“Any contravention of this rule will constitute a malpractice as per the KNEC Act and the Rules and Regulations,” noted Dr Njengere.

The council will deploy 342,005 contracted professionals to administer and manage the examinations and assessments. They include centre managers, supervisors, invigilators, security officers and drivers.

For KCSE, KNEC will deploy 10,765 centre managers, 12,274 supervisors, 57,432 invigilators and 21,388 security officers. Each examination centre will have at least two police officers.

Centre managers will collect KCSE papers twice a day, and KNEC will place morning and afternoon papers in marked cartons to reduce mix-ups and unauthorised access.

KNEC has personalised question papers with candidates’ details, and examiners will receive anonymised scripts with those details removed.

The 2026 examination and assessment season will involve 3,634,846 candidates, a 6.13 per cent increase from the 3,424,836 registered in 2025.

KCSE rehearsals will take place on Friday, October 16. Examinations for papers with low candidature will run from Monday, October 19 to Friday, October 30, while papers with large candidature will run from Monday, November 2 to Friday, November 20.

KPSEA and KJSEA assessments will run from Monday, October 26 to Friday, October 30.

KNEC Chairperson Prof. Julius Nyabundi said the council was preparing for possible disruption from El Nino rains.

“As we start off the 2026 field administration season, one of the risks we contend with are the attempts to cheat in assessments and examination,” said Prof. Nyabundi.

He urged candidates, parents and examination officials to protect the integrity of the examinations, warning that malpractice could undermine public confidence in the education system.

“Cheating in examinations undermines public confidence in the credibility, fairness and quality of the entire education system,” noted Prof. Nyabundi.

KNEC will operate a 24-hour call centre with toll-free numbers for candidates, officials and members of the public to report incidents and seek assistance during the examination period.

The 2026 cycle will continue the implementation of Competency-Based Education assessments, including School-Based Assessments in primary, junior and senior school.

Grade 10 learners are undertaking their first School-Based Assessment, which will contribute 15 marks towards the Kenya Certificate of Basic Education.

World.title: Mbadi hits out at Sifuna, says opposition lacks economic agenda
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi after opening new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by the M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency. [James Omoro, Standard]

The National Treasury CS John Mbadi has hit out at Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, saying that criticising President William Ruto should not be an agenda for a presidential candidate.

Speaking when he opened new classrooms and administration blocks constructed by M-Pesa Foundation at Ligongo Primary School in Suba South Constituency, Mbadi said lack of economic agenda makes the opposition unsuitable to lead the country.

“I have heard of opposition leaders who want the presidency, but they do not have an agenda for the economic transformation of this country,” he said.

The CS claimed that none of the opposition leaders is suitable for the presidency.

“These opposition leaders cannot make any economic change in this country. They should not be elected,” he said.

He told Nyanza residents to shun the new wave of opposition led by Sifuna.

Mbadi claimed that opposition leaders lack political direction.

He said Sifuna had taken too long to unveil a political party that he will use to run for the presidency.

“Do not join the opposition bandwagon. We are just a few months away from the General Election, but Sifuna still doesn’t know a political party he will use to run for the presidency. They are still leaving in confusion,” Mbadi said.

He said Sifuna has not demonstrated how to improve this country’s economy.

“Former President Uhuru Kenyatta left the economy of this country in tatters. We have tried to improve it but we are not yet where we want it to be,” Mbadi said.

He urged Nyanza residents to support Ruto.

The CS said Ruto’s government had improved mega infrastructural projects across the country as part of economic transformation.

He cited the 74 km Mbita- Sindo- Sori road, Lake Victoria ring road and other infrastructure projects as some of the reasons residents should support Ruto.

“I urge you to support Ruto so that we can continue acquiring more development projects in this region,” Mbadi said.

World.title: Kericho Annex Prison under scrutiny over death of remand prisoner
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Brenda Chemutai, 19, who allegedly committed suicide inside the Kericho Annex Prison where she was awaiting trial for an offence of being in possession of bhang that was seized in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer. [Courtesy]

Questions are mounting over security and accountability at Kericho Annex Prison following the death of a 19-year-old remand prisoner in a suspected case of suicide.

Her family is demanding answers about how she obtained a bedsheet and why they were not notified until nearly 10 hours after the incident.

Brenda Chemutai was reportedly found hanging from a double-decker bed at around 9 am when her fellow cellmates were having breakfast on Friday.

The cell had eight inmates, who had gone for breakfast, according to a police report.

However, her relatives state they were not informed until about 7 pm, after her body had already been taken from the prison and transferred to the Kericho County Hospital Mortuary.

The delay has raised serious concerns for the family, which calls for authorities to clarify what happened between the time Chemutai was discovered and when her next of kin were contacted.

Kericho East Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) officer, Kennedy Apindi, said police have launched investigations following reports from prison officials that the incident was a suicide.

He mentioned that preliminary information indicated Chemutai allegedly used a bedsheet.

The family, however, insists that investigators determine when she was found, who discovered her, when the incident was reported to police, who authorised her body’s removal, and why her relatives were not notified immediately.

“We had spoken with Brenda. She was expected to be released around December, and by January we would all have been together at home,” said her sister, Phyllis Cherotich.

Cherotich added that the family had seen no signs indicating Chemutai intended to take her own life.

"Her death has shocked us deeply. She never mentioned any plans of this nature. We want to understand how this was possible given the level of security at the facility," she said.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged use of a bedsheet have also raised questions for the family.

Her uncle, Michael Rono, questioned how such an item came into Chemutai's possession while she was in a remand facility.

"I am deeply surprised. When one enters the prison, one is carefully searched. Where did the bedsheet come from? We ask the government to ensure justice is done," Rono said.

Chemutai had been in remand since 2024, with her relatives saying she was arrested while still a minor and had spent nearly two years awaiting the conclusion of her case.

She was being tried for the offence of possession of bhang in a vehicle allegedly belonging to a senior police officer.

Her death has consequently brought renewed scrutiny to not only what happened inside the prison but also the circumstances that led to her prolonged detention.

Youth activists from the Voice of Youth Organisation, led by Kelvin Kipchichir, have joined the family in demanding investigations into both the death and the case that resulted in Chemutai's detention.

Kipchichir claimed Chemutai was arrested alongside other suspects in a vehicle allegedly linked to an Officer Commanding Station serving in Kakamega.

According to the activists, police recovered 32 rolls of bhang from the vehicle, while some of the suspects allegedly fled, leaving Chemutai behind.

The claims have not been independently established.

Kipchichir questioned why Chemutai remained in custody for such a prolonged period and called for scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the vehicle and its alleged connection to the police officer.

“We are concerned that an OCS in the National Police Service could allow a vehicle to be used by an individual with a known criminal record,” he said.

He called on the Ministry of Interior to establish who owned or controlled the vehicle and under what circumstances it was allegedly being used.

The activists said the vehicle was still at Kericho Police Station.

For the family, the tragedy has been compounded by personal loss. Chemutai's father died while she was in remand, while she leaves behind a young child.

Relatives said detectives had informed them that the person alleged to own the bhang had since been arrested and was being held in Kisumu.

But the immediate question for Chemutai's family is what happened during her final hours.

They want a clear account of the period between the reported discovery of her body at about 9 am and the notification of the family nearly 10 hours later.

They also want investigators to establish how the bedsheet allegedly used in the incident came into her possession and whether prison officers followed all required procedures after she was found.

The activists are calling for the inquiry to extend beyond the death of Chemutai to her arrest, the length of her detention and the handling of the case against her.

The family has demanded a transparent and independent investigation, saying it wants answers on how a teenager who entered the justice system while still a minor ended up dead in remand custody.

The family says it wants those questions answered before proceeding with burial arrangements.

World.title: Pregnant woman found dead by roadside in Kirinyaga with head, hip injuries
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The National Police Service (NPS) has launched investigations after the body of a pregnant woman was found by the roadside in the Itangi area of Mwea East Sub-County, Kirinyaga County.

The woman, identified as Catherine Njeru, was found early Friday morning along the Piai-Itangi Murram Road with visible injuries to her head and hip.

In a statement, NPS said the incident is being investigated as a suspected murder.

"The NPS condoles with the family, relatives, and friends of the deceased and commits to expeditious and conclusive investigations to ensure that any person or persons responsible for this barbaric crime are brought to justice," read the statement.

Police have urged residents of Itangi to remain calm and refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation has been asked to report to the nearest police station or a law enforcement officer.

The matter is being investigated by Kirinyaga County Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) officers, local Sub-County police and Central Regional Police Command, led by the Regional Criminal Investigations Officer.

According to NPS, the Inspector General of the National Police Service has also been briefed on the incident and directed the Director of Criminal Investigations to expedite the probe and establish the facts surrounding the woman's death.

World.title: Egypt’s Hurghada allocates LE 23 million to first fully-equipped stray dog shelter
World.content:
In a major step toward balancing public safety with animal welfare, the Red Sea Housing Directorate has officially allocated a LE 23 million contract to launch Hurghada’s first fully integrated shelter for free-roaming street dogs.

Moving beyond temporary fixes, the coastal resort town is rolling out a comprehensive, humane strategy designed to manage its stray population with long-term care, structured medical intervention, and proper safety standards.

A modern approach to animal welfare

The ambitious project forms part of a broader technical and logistical framework supporting Red Sea Governorate authorities. Rather than relying on outdated containment methods, the initiative integrates standardized architectural blueprints built around high safety and hygiene guidelines, ensuring that the animals receive proper care in a secure environment.

Key components of the initiative include:

Mass vaccination campaigns: Systematically administering rabies vaccines across the local stray population to protect both communities and animals.

Specialized fleet transport: Equipping the regional directorate with purpose-built transport vehicles adhering to strict technical specifications, guaranteeing safe, stress-free relocation for street dogs.

Structured medical facilities: Establishing dedicated shelter zones for veterinary checkups, sterilization programs, and ongoing recovery.

By combining engineering precision with veterinary science, Hurghada aims to pioneer a sustainable blueprint for animal management along the Red Sea coast—offering a safer, cleaner environment for residents and tourists while giving local stray animals the care and sanctuary they deserve.

World.title: Houthi Airport attacks leave 3 dead and dozens wounded, including two Egyptians
World.content:
The Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) revealed on Wednesday that attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport resulted in several injuries among citizens and foreign residents, ranging from minor to severe, as a result of the Houthi aggression on King Khalid International Airport.

In an official statement, the authority explained that “on Tuesday and Wednesday, Abha and King Khalid International Airports were subjected to two attacks targeting their facilities. Emergency teams and competent authorities immediately responded to both attacks upon occurrence, in accordance with approved procedures and plans.”

The statement continued: “The overt attack on Abha International Airport resulted in two fatalities among female residents of Moroccan and Algerian nationalities, as well as 28 injuries among citizens and two foreign residents of Bangladeshi and Philippine nationalities, with injuries ranging from minor to severe.”

According to the statement: “The attack on King Khalid International Airport resulted in one fatality of a resident of Sudanese nationality, along with eight injuries, including five citizens, two residents of Egyptian nationality, and one resident of Pakistani nationality, with injuries ranging from minor to severe.”

The authority noted that “all injured individuals were immediately transferred to the hospital to receive the necessary medical care, and both attacks resulted in some material damage.”

The authority clarified that it is working in continuous integration and coordination with relevant security agencies to assess damages and take all necessary measures to ensure the safety of passengers and workers, while maintaining the security and safety of the civil aviation system in the Kingdom.

World.title: Israel forces out British diplomats in Jerusalem over West Bank sanctions
World.content:
Israel announced that the majority of British diplomats will depart from the British Consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, in response to UK sanctions imposed on settlements in the occupied West Bank.

According to the BBC, Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar stated that Israel implemented the measures it had announced and committed to on September 8 in response to British sanctions. Sa’ar said: “The British Consulate in Jerusalem shuts down its operations today. Accordingly, the plaque of the British Consulate in Jerusalem has been removed.”

However, the British flag could still be seen outside the building, and several staff members were seen entering on Thursday morning.

Limited diplomatic staff inside the building

Sa’ar noted that talks with the British government led to an agreement on specific principles, including that “the Consul General and 20 diplomats (including the Consul General) are ending their duties and will leave Israel.”

At the same time, the Israeli Foreign Minister acknowledged that the building “is owned by the British Government,” clarifying that Israel permitted a “skeleton staff of only seven diplomats with a very limited scope of operations” to work inside.

He added that as a result of this agreement with the United Kingdom, “no steps will be taken against Israel.”
