World.title: Forgotten trail camera yields nine months of wildlife images
World.content:
A farmer in South Estonia who forgot about a trail camera he had set up found a wealth of nature photo on it once he retrieved it.

Tarvo Siilaberg, a Põlva County farmer, left the trail cam in a forest earlier this year and it soon passed from his mind. But once he remembered and located it, he found the fully working camera had been "visited" by moose, deer, cranes and other wildlife — including a bear.

The camera's battery and systems were still running, and its memory had not filled up either.

"Part of it was simple absent-mindedness. We have quite a few camera traps for animals and one ended up in a spot I couldn't remember for a long time," said Siilaberg, owner of Raja Farm.

Cranes, a vocal summer visitor to Estonia. caught on the trailcam. Source: ERR

When he went looking for the camera in the forest, he found it hard to spot because of its nature as a trail cam — well camouflaged.

Some of the visitors captured on the footage were more surprising than others.

"We already knew that a moose trail passes through our land, which is why we put the camera at the edge of the bog forest," Siilaberg explained.

"The camera was up at the edge of the forest, where the ditch bank meets the meadow — we happened to place it right at an animal crossroads," he said. "Deer appear in front of the trail camera about as often as you'd see a pigeon in the city."

The brown bear was one of the last images to be captured by the trail cam before Tarvo Siilaberg picked it up. Source: ERR

One of the last images the camera captured before it was retrieved was also one of the most impressive: a bear.

"That was also the first photo I saw when I took the camera down from the tree. Then I knew there was something very good here," said Siilaberg, whose farm is in Kanassaare village in Põlva municipality.

"The picture of the cranes is my favorite," he said. "I hope to forget my camera in the forest again soon — then good things will start happening, if a person keeps their hands away. The result is definitely worth it."

Of the animals he had hoped to see, Siilaberg said he had wanted footage of a lynx, but there wasn't any.

World.title: NATO chief Mark Rutte to visit Estonia next week
World.content:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is due to visit Estonia next week, meeting the country's leaders and visiting Ämari Air Base and Tallinn University of Technology.

Rutte is scheduled meet with newly inaugurated President Ülle Madise on Wednesday, along with Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform), Defense Minister Martin Herem (Reform) and Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200).

Rutte will also hold a joint press conference with Prime Minister Michal, NATO's press service said Friday.

The NATO Secretary General last visited Estonia in October 2024, shortly after taking office in that role. The 2024 trip was his first visit to a NATO eastern flank country, and over the two days he met with Estonian leaders, visited Tapa military base and Tallinn University, and also visited the memorial to the victims of communism in Tallinn.

Ülle Madise takes office as president on Monday.

World.title: Possible cyberattack halts Estonian Artists' Association fundraiser auction
World.content:
A fundraiser auction for the Estonian Artists' Association (EKL) was suspended Thursday evening amid concerns over a possible cyberattack. The auction is set to resume Friday.

Auction house Eesti Kunsti Oksjonid (EKO) said its technical team was working to resolve technical issues before the auction resumes at 6 p.m. Friday, picking up where it left off the day before.

"According to livestream support provider Zone, the issue may have been caused by a cyberattack," EKO said in a press release Thursday night.

The disruption occurred after the first work, Jüri Arrak's 1985 graphic work "Tiiger," sold for €23,500, up from a starting price of €1,600. Organizers had anticipated strong demand and worked with their technical partner to prepare for it.

Initial assessments, however, indicated the failure was not caused by excessive traffic.

"It's important to us that every bidder has an equal opportunity to participate, so we're postponing the auction until Friday," auctioneer Reigo Kuivjõgi said, apologizing to those who had been watching online and hoped to bid.

Server provider: No signs of cyberattack

Zone.eu marketing chief Triin Lükk later told ERR that Zone had not said a cyberattack was or might have been to blame for the disruption.

She explained that the company provides server services to EKO but does not develop or maintain the auction application itself.

"Based on the information available to us, we have found no signs of malicious activity within the scope of our server service," Lükk said. "Thus, we have no grounds for linking the disruption to a cyberattack."

The cause of the glitch is still being investigated, she noted, adding that Zone's server services are operating as intended.

"We can rule out a cyberattack based on what we've seen," Lükk said. "We've found no signs of one."

The EKL is holding a special fundraiser auction in Tallinn from October 8–10, with proceeds from the sale of 162 works going toward recouping nearly €700,000 the artists' union lost to fraud this spring.

World.title: Estonia to recoup €25 million from Nordica's former aircraft lessor
World.content:
The liquidation of state-owned aircraft lessor Transpordi Varahaldus will put €25 million into Estonia's budget next year following the shutdown of bankrupt airline Nordica.

The government is expected to authorize Infrastructure Minister Kuldar Leis (Reform) to wind up Transpordi Varahaldus in the coming weeks, following its July decision to liquidate the company, which leased aircraft to bankrupt airline Nordica.

The company's seven aircraft and spare parts have been sold, it has no outstanding debts and its bank accounts hold €25 million. Leis said the money will go to the State Treasury, but its eventual use will remain up to the Ministry of Finance.

"It's yet unclear how that money will be used, as that decision rests with the Finance Ministry, which manages the state's cash flow," he explained. "The money won't come with a label attached."

Transpordi Varahaldus also has claims of €35.7 million against Nordica and €27.5 million against its subsidiary Regional Jet, both of which are bankrupt.

Leis said the state will retain these claims and continue seeking repayment until both bankruptcy proceedings are concluded. The claims will be transferred to the state as part of the liquidation, with either the Finance Ministry or the Climate Ministry responsible for managing them.

Final Nordica aircraft takes off from Tallinn Airport. March 31, 2026. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"We have no intention of giving up these claims," he said. "The state will continue pursuing repayment itself."

According to the minister, the liquidation process is expected to take nine to 12 months, involving routine legal procedures.

Last flight

Nordica ceased operations in March when the last of its seven 88-seat Bombardier CRJ900NG jets departed Tallinn Airport. The aircraft, owned by state-run Transpordi Varahaldus, had been sold to U.S.-based Regional One last June.

The planes had been leased to Nordica subsidiary Regional Jet. Both companies filed for bankruptcy in November 2024, with Nordica declared bankrupt in January 2025 and Regional Jet, which operated under the Xfly brand, following a month later.

Nordica launched in 2015, ahead of the bankruptcy of Estonia's former flag carrier, Estonian Air. It flew under its own name from Tallinn until 2019, then shifted to subcontracting services. Transpordi Varahaldus also began operations in 2015.

World.title: ICC Iraq joins Saudi corporate social responsibility forum ahead of Baghdad event
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Chamber of Commerce in Iraq (ICC Iraq) is planning to hold a forum on corporate social responsibility and business sustainability in Baghdad on November 1 after its participation in a major international conference in Saudi Arabia.

An ICC Iraq team attended the Global CSR Forum 2026, which took place in Riyadh on October 5-6 and was organized by Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development.

The event drew over 3,000 attendees and 100 presenters from across the globe, with over 40 sessions addressing corporate social responsibility, sustainable business practices, and international collaboration.

ICC Iraq said that its participation was intended to develop ties with foreign organizations and share experience ahead of the Iraqi Forum for Social Responsibility and Business Sustainability, which is set for November 1 in Baghdad.

The next workshop is planned to provide a venue for conversations about how Iraqi firms may integrate social responsibility and sustainability into their operations.

The program comes as Iraq strives to enhance its private sector and attract foreign investment, with a focus on corporate governance, environmental norms, and firms’ role in economic growth.

ICC Iraq’s presence at the Riyadh event demonstrates attempts to link Iraqi firms with international organizations and offer worldwide expertise in responsible business practices to the local market.

World.title: Asian stocks mixed amid AI concerns, oil dips after surge
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks headed into the weekend on a mixed note on Friday with tech weighed by renewed concerns about the AI investment boom, while support came from a drop in oil prices after Donald Trump ruled out a pre-election strike on Iran.

The outlook for artificial intelligence has provided a fresh boost to the tech sector in recent weeks, with some optimism for the upcoming earnings season. Chip titan Nvidia this week hit a record high and closed in on the $6 trillion market capitalisation.

That was dealt a blow by a Financial Times report saying OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, expected to make $50 billion in annualised revenue this year, far less than the $70 billion flagged previously.

“For most of this boom, the market has been happy to follow the money going in. Bigger data centres, more GPUs, more memory, more power, more debt, more capex,” wrote Stephen Innes at SPI Asset Management.

“Every fresh spending commitment became another brick in the bullish wall because the assumption underneath it was simple enough: if the industry is prepared to spend this much, the demand will eventually justify it.

“Then OpenAI handed the market a number that made traders look at the other side of the ledger.”

Wall Street’s Nasdaq ended more than one percent lower, with Nvidia down nearly three percent, while Microsoft, AMD and Amazon among others sharply lower.

However, Chris Weston at Pepperstone added that “the discrepancy may reflect differences in revenue measurement rather than an outright deterioration in OpenAI’s underlying business”.

Still, he said, “in a market where valuations are increasingly dependent on ambitious revenue and cash flow projections, the headlines have been enough to trigger a meaningful one-day repositioning”.

In Asia, Tokyo sank with tech investing titan SoftBank losing more than four percent, while Kioxia and Advantest were also well down.

Shanghai and Singapore were also down, though Hong Kong, Sydney, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta were all up.

Seoul and Taipei — both heavily weighted with tech firms — were closed for holidays.

Traders took a little heart from a dip in oil prices after US President Donald Trump ruled out hitting Iran before the midterm elections, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran.

His remarks came after reports said the White House had asked the Pentagon to draw up plans for a possible attack ahead of the November 3 vote, hoping a show of strength might help struggling Republicans’ chances.

Both main contracts were down around 0.7 percent Friday, though that is after they fell as much as four percent on concerns about increased Iranian strikes in the Strait of Hormuz.

That comes on top of Yemen’s Houthis taking aim at Riyadh airport with missiles and warning staff at oil facilities in Saudi Arabia to leave to avoid being targeted as hostilities escalate.

Comments from Fed officials cemented expectations for another interest rate hike before the end of the year, though this month appears unlikely.

Governor Christopher Waller said more tightening was likely necessary to bring prices under control, while St. Louis Fed boss Alberto Musalem eyed increases over the next six to nine months.

Still, National Australia Bank’s Ken Crompton said: “Whilst this is a touch hawkish relative to his (Waller’s) recent record, he’s still in close accord with (Vice Chair Philip) Jefferson and (New York Fed chief John) Williams last week, who collectively (in addition to the inflation data) helped cool market pricing of an October hike from 15 basis points to less than five basis points.”

World.title: James shines in pre-season debut for re-tooled 76ers
World.content:
New York – NBA superstar LeBron James delivered a solid first half in his first pre-season game for Philadelphia on Thursday, but the new-look 76ers fell 114-108 to the Nets in Brooklyn.

James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, announced in July that he had signed a two-year, $8 million deal with the 76ers, ending weeks of speculation over where the four-time NBA champion would land as a free agent after eight seasons and one title with the Los Angeles Lakers.

The 41-year-old superstar, entering a record-extending 24th NBA season, won two titles with Miami, another with Cleveland and a fourth with the Lakers and is aiming to help the Sixers win their first title since Julius Erving led the club to the crown 43 years ago.

Thursday’s game marked his first chance to line up alongside new teammates Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown — a new arrival from the Boston Celtics.

James scored 10 points, connecting on his lone shot from the floor and making all eight of his free-throw attempts. He added four rebounds, five assists and a steal in 18:04 minutes in the first half.

Brown led all scorers with 18 points. Julius Randle had 14 for the Nets, who out-scored the Sixers 37-23 in the third quarter to take control.

But all eyes were on James, starting with his first signature pre-game chalk-toss in a 76ers uniform.

James smoothly directed the Sixers offense in his time on the floor, making all five of his assists in the first quarter and combining effectively with Maxey.

“I think there was some really good things happening, you know, right off the bat,” 76ers coach Nick Nurse said after seeing his starters together for the first time.

“A bunch of back cuts and good passing et cetera … there were segments where obviously we turned the ball over a lot … just the little clunky segments, too. But, again, it’s pre-season, first time they’re together.

“I think you look at it as what’s good and what are the learning experiences, things that we can improve.”

The 76ers have two more pre-season games, both against Boston, before opening the NBA regular season against the defending champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on October 20.

James’s arrival has already found the 76ers battling outside “noise.”

James took to Instagram to refute a report from a play-by-play announcer during the team’s first pre-season game on Monday that James had admonished Embiid for being late to a practice.

“He ain’t been late, so stop the lie,” James posted.

James had acknowledged at the team’s media day last month that such outside hubbub around the 76ers would be “doubled, tripled and quadrupled now that I’m here.”

World.title: Tech scammer Elizabeth Holmes focus of documentary by absurdist Nathan Fielder
World.content:
Los Angeles – The private life of disgraced Silicon Valley startup founder Elizabeth Holmes will soon be aired to the public in a startling new documentary filmed in the 34 days before she went to prison.

The buzzy film from Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, out in US theaters October 16, captures the reclusive former executive’s world in the month before her incarceration for fraud at her now-defunct health technology company Theranos, whose lofty promises it couldn’t deliver.

Theranos falsely touted technology capable of performing medical tests using only a few drops of blood.

The project took Silicon Valley by storm in the early 2010s, as young entrepreneur Holmes drew investors — including Henry Kissinger, Carlos Slim and Rupert Murdoch — to her project.

But her fall proved just as rapid.

The sensational trial of Holmes ended in her 2022 sentencing to more than 11 years in prison for fraud and conspiracy.

The scandal fueled a media circus and was chronicled in a book, multiple podcasts, and the biographical mini-series “The Dropout” that starred Amanda Seyfried.

Holmes herself shied from the public eye, making the surprise release of the documentary “You Can See Everything” all the more astonishing when it debuted to high praise at the Telluride Film Festival in September.

– ‘Really sad and hard’ –

The film follows her life at home with partner Billy Evans and their two children, a hybrid of documentary and reality television portrayal that drew laughter, gasps and applause at a Los Angeles screening this week.

The Canadian comedian, writer and producer Fielder is famous for harnessing the power of awkwardness, cringe and deadpan wit to great, if unsettling, comedic effect.

He and Oppenheim said it was Holmes who initiated conversations with independent entertainment company A24 about documenting her daily life.

After a few meetings with the filmmakers, they said she invited them into her California home.

And things got strange.

Tuesday’s screening was attended by celebrities including Zach Cregger, Hannah Einbinder, Meg Stalter, Aziz Ansari and Hasan Piker, and during a discussion afterward the directors described their experience as “really sad and hard at times.”

“I still am not sure to this day, like, what I experienced, and it’s one of the reasons I’m excited for it to like come out and more people see it, because it was just a small group for so long,” Fielder said.

“Maybe it being out there, like everyone could help me understand what I went through a little bit.”

– ‘Uncomfortable’ –

Oppenheim said neither Holmes nor Evans voiced familiarity with his work when they opened their doors.

Fielder — the comic behind hit series like “The Rehearsal” and “Nathan For You,” shows that blur the line between reality and fiction — said there was “never a great explanation” as to why he should helm the project, “or why you would want to spend your last month of freedom in a decade with this guy.”

“I like to see myself as like a nice person overall, but still, I wouldn’t choose me.”

Fielder is a constant presence in the documentary, a decision made on the fly, the filmmakers said.

Close-up shots of him face-to-face with Holmes have ricocheted across social media and already become the stuff of meme gold.

Oppenheim said as the process rolled out it began to feel like “the only way, maybe, to actually make this is also to have someone kind of confront, you know, their delusions on certain aspects.”

In early images released by A24 Holmes is shown maintaining intense, unnerving eye contact with Fielder, scenes that made even him “uncomfortable,” he said.

“But I also felt like I was — these moments were so odd, and I was the one, like, ruining them or, like, bailing on them,” Fielder continued.

“At a certain point, I was like, ‘I’m not going to stop.’ If she’s looking at me, I’m just going to keep looking at her.”

The directors said living under the same roof as the documentary subjects created tensions and even saw Evans, who hasn’t seen the film, try to exert control over production.

But the filmmakers were never thrown out.

Like her partner, Holmes also hasn’t seen the finished product, Fielder and Oppenheim said. She remains in prison.

World.title: Trump’s ‘super intelligence’ rebrand to sell AI faces uphill battle
World.content:
Washington – Donald Trump’s campaign to rename artificial intelligence as “super intelligence” is unlikely to win over a wary public and could make matters worse, experts say, even as the US president threatens to treat holdouts as enemies.

On Thursday, he warned that anyone refusing to adopt the term would be considered an “ENEMY” by the White House, without saying what that would mean.

He had floated the name change in September before the UN General Assembly, saying it sounded much better.

“The use of the word artificial makes intelligence fake. It makes it sound fake, and it is not fake. It’s actually amazing,” he said.

He later signed an executive order mandating the term in government communications.

According to Jean-Pierre Dube, a marketing professor at the University of Chicago, there is a genuine concern at the White House that the backlash against AI and data centers could “stifle one of the key drivers of economic growth right now” and “cede technological dominance to China.”

However, “the idea that a re-brand that mis-characterizes the technology will turn around some of the public sentiment seems like wishful thinking,” he told AFP.

– ‘Poor choice’ –

But expert opinion matters little to Trump, who wrote in his book “The Art of the Deal”: “I don’t trust fancy marketing surveys. I do my own surveys and draw my own conclusions.”

He even polled users on Truth Social, where “super intelligence” beat out the other option, “superior intelligence.”

Americans see Trump as overly enthusiastic about artificial intelligence, which many already use but whose consequences for safety and jobs they fear, while also worrying about the rapid construction of massive data centers.

In a recent Quinnipiac University poll, only 25 percent of voters said they were satisfied with how the 80-year-old Republican is approaching AI, against 58 percent who were dissatisfied.

“If we believe that ‘artificial’ already encourages fear, ‘super’ seems like something far more worrisome,” said Dube, calling it “a poor choice of new brand.”

For Ronald Kline, a historian at Cornell University, “the phrase ‘super intelligence’ means more than simulating human intelligence, it means going beyond human intelligence,” he told AFP.

The term “artificial intelligence” was born in 1956 at an austere summer workshop at Dartmouth College.

Deliberately abstract, it was chosen to bring under one banner the research of scientists from varied backgrounds — mathematicians, psychologists and engineers driven by the same ambition: teaching computers, at the time enormous calculating machines, to “think” like humans.

Seen by some as a catch-all, the term never won unanimous support from the scientific community, which nonetheless came to accept it — as did Herbert Simon, winner of the 1978 Nobel Prize in Economics, who wrote as early as 1969: “‘artificial intelligence’ seems to be here to stay, and it may prove easier to cleanse the phrase than to dispense with it.”

For Kline, the name truly took off when it became the acronym AI, associated with the stratospheric growth of companies such as OpenAI.

The ChatGPT maker is not forced to change its name by Trump’s executive order, which applies only to the federal government.

But some of the sector’s top executives have chosen to follow the president, who closely tracks whether his various unilateral name changes are adopted.

The Associated Press news agency drew his wrath for refusing to adopt the name “Gulf of America” in place of “Gulf of Mexico.”

The term “super intelligence” has appeared in communications from Meta, Mark Zuckerberg’s group.

Elon Musk, a Trump ally, enthusiastically supports the name change and uses “super intelligence” in his posts on X.

A Washington industry lobbyist interviewed by AFP predicted a pragmatic approach from companies.

“I think you’ll see it used when it has to be used, i.e. when you’re communicating with the administration,” he said. “Insisting on ‘AI’ versus ‘super intelligence’ isn’t a fight you need to pick.”

World.title: Man City face Anfield cauldron after guilty Premier League verdicts
World.content:
Manchester – Manchester City are set for a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday in their first outing since being found guilty of over 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City have appealed and proclaim their innocence, but the Premier League leaders’ place in the division is now at threat following findings they used “sham” sponsorship deals to inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).

Manchester United and Tottenham are both badly in need of a win when they meet at Old Trafford, while Arsenal aim to bounce back at home to Leeds following a rare defeat.

AFP sports looks at the pick of the action as the English top-flight returns after a three-week international break.

City face the music

City’s transformation into the dominant force in English football since an Abu Dhabi-backed takeover 18 years ago has cost Liverpool more than most.

The charges labelled against City cover the period between 2009 and 2018, but the foundations they built in that time ensured they remained the Premier League’s top dogs during the bulk of Pep Guardiola’s subsequent time in charge.

Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool twice missed out on the title to Guardiola’s side despite amassing over 90 points.

Those battles to be crowned champions of England over the past decade have turned this fixture into the Premier League’s marquee match-up and the eyes of the football world will be on Anfield again come Sunday.

City have won every game since Enzo Maresca replaced Guardiola, but their title challenge is likely to be ruined by a sanction unless they can overturn the verdict of an independent commission.

Liverpool will seek to capitalise on City’s uncertainty and kickstart their own campaign.

Andoni Iraola remains unbeaten as Liverpool manager but draws against Newcastle, Nottingham Forest and Fulham have left the Reds six points off top spot.

“I think it’s a big game and I think everyone is expecting to play, to watch, to be part of that game,” said Iraola.

“We know we will have to be at our best and also I know that the people will be looking to help the team.”

Pressure on Carrick

City’s scandal took the attention away from a difficult start to the season on the other side of Manchester.

United have taken just five points from what appeared an inviting opening five fixtures and now face a difficult run.

Just months after being handed the job as

manager on a permanent basis, Michael Carrick is the latest United boss facing scrutiny over his ability to turn around the fortunes of the ailing English giants.

After Saturday’s visit of Spurs, the Red Devils travel to Atletico Madrid, Leeds and Como in a nine-day period and also face Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa before next month’s international break.

Tottenham spent over £300 million on new players during the transfer window, but still had to endure the past three weeks rooted to the foot of the table after taking just two points from their opening five games.

Arsenal just getting started

Defending champions Arsenal are aiming to strike back when Leeds visit the Emirates in Saturday’s early kick-off.

A perfect start to the campaign for the Gunners ended in dramatic fashion with a 3-0 defeat at Brighton in their last outing.

But developments in the City case have reinforced Mikel Arteta’s men as bookies’ favourites to retain the title.

Arsenal manager Arteta extended his contract till 2030 this week and is determined that a first league title in 22 years is only the beginning of a golden age for the north London club.

“This is only the beginning of what we can achieve together,” said the Spaniard.

World.title: CNN, MS Now, Politico urge judge to extend White House access
World.content:
Washington – CNN, MS NOW and Politico urged a federal judge on Thursday to extend White House access to the three media outlets which President Donald Trump is seeking to ban.

District Judge Timothy Kelly prolonged until Tuesday the temporary White House access he granted to the news organizations last month and said he expected to issue a ruling by then.

Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House on September 18 for distributing what he called “fake news” and “fiction and lies.”

The three outlets filed a joint lawsuit asking for a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the ban on the grounds that it violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which upholds the right to a free press.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico appeared in a downtown Washington court on Thursday to ask that the judge transform his TRO into a preliminary injunction prohibiting Trump from barring them from the White House while the case proceeds.

Theodore Boutrous, a lawyer for the media outlets, said Trump issued the ban “because of what he perceives as negative, false, bad, not positive enough reporting.”

The Republican president, Boutrous said, apparently “got up on the wrong side of the bed and declared a ban on these news organizations.”

“He doesn’t like scrutiny of his policies. He doesn’t like the reporting. He wants more good press,” he said. “If your press pass is at risk because President Trump decides something you said is false, that’s a very, very dangerous, chilling doctrine.”

Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik, urging the judge to uphold the ban, accused CNN, MS NOW and Politico of violating “journalistic standards” and endangering national security by revealing classified information.

A skeptical Kelly asked Velchik whether it was a “a violation of minimum journalistic standards to portray the administration in a negative light?”

In his ruling last month temporarily restoring the White House credentials of CNN, MS NOW and Politico, the judge, who was appointed by Trump during his first term, said the ban “likely violated their constitutional due process rights.”

Trump has long attacked media that have aired critical coverage of him, repeatedly blasting the press as the “enemy of the people.”

Following the judge’s order, CNN, MS NOW and Politico were granted access to the White House grounds and the briefing room but have been kept out of the Oval Office and Air Force One.

In a rare move, the top five US broadcasters — ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox and NBC — halted pool coverage of the White House — where a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day — in solidarity with CNN.

World.title: OpenAI says Iran, Russia influence ops busted
World.content:
Washington – OpenAI on Thursday said it shut down two influence operations — from Russia and Iran — that used ChatGPT to push fake journalist personas and run a “think-tank” to covertly peddle anti-Ukraine propaganda.

OpenAI’s report is the latest illustration of how state actors can easily exploit widely available AI tools to peddle sophisticated propaganda against adversaries on a mass scale.

The American AI giant said it banned a cluster of ChatGPT accounts that originated in Russia and Iran and were used to support “false front” entities for geopolitical and conflict-related messaging.

The Iranian operation involved seven “journalist” profiles, each purporting to be from Western countries including the United States, that were used to plant long-form articles in media outlets around the world.

“We identified almost 100 articles published or syndicated under the operation’s bylines across roughly a dozen online outlets around the world,” OpenAI said.

“These were small to medium outlets, generally focused on international affairs, geopolitics, and events in the Middle East.”

The earliest article identified by OpenAI was published in July 2025, and the latest in October 2026, with the frequency of reports increasing after the US-Iran war broke out earlier this year.

The operation also generated social media comments on topics related to the US-Iran war, it added.

One of the personas named Ervin B. Hoskins, whose bio claimed to be “an American freelance writer,” had social media accounts across tech platforms including Elon Musk’s X and Meta-owned Instagram.

X’s transparency information showed the account was connected via a “West Asia android app” and Instagram’s transparency information showed the account was based in Iran, according to screenshots provided by OpenAI.

Both accounts appeared to be suspended.

The Russian operation co-opted “unwitting people” in Latin America to run a “think-tank” — called the Social Research Center (SRC) — used for covert activities aimed at undermining Ukraine’s reputation in the region and to influence local politics, the company said.

“The available evidence indicates that the SRC’s employees in Latin America were not aware that they were working for a Russian group,” OpenAI said.

“The SRC appears to have produced a majority of original content via its co-opted staff. This stands out as the most complex attempt to run a front identity that we’ve disrupted over the past two and a half years.”

According to a statement shared by the ministry of railways, trains departing their originating stations after 2 pm on October 9 and scheduled to arrive at New Delhi or Hazrat Nizamuddin between 4 am and 2 pm on October 10 will be cancelled. World.title: Mary Kom’s ex-husband alleges character assassination, files defamation complaint

Olympic medallist Mary Komâs former husband, Karong Onkholer

Olympic medallist Mary Komâs former husband, Karong Onkholer, has filed a defamation complaint against the boxer before Delhiâs Saket Court, alleging that remarks she made during a televised interview damaged his reputation.The complaint was filed on October 6 and is pending before Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivam Gupta for pre-summoning evidence. The court is scheduled to hear the matter on November 19.According to the complaint, Onkholer and Kom married on March 12, 2005, and lived together in Faridabad. Their marriage was dissolved through customary practice on December 20, 2023, the complainant stated.Onkholer has alleged that Kom made defamatory remarks about him during a television interview aired on January 11, 2026, after the dissolution of their marriage. He claims the programme was broadcast to a nationwide audience running into millions.The complaint alleges that an ordinary viewer would interpret the statements, taken individually and collectively, as portraying Onkholer as âdishonest, unfaithful, unemployed, financially parasiticâ and dependent on alcohol.It further alleges that the remarks suggested he had misappropriated money from Komâs bank accounts and abandoned his responsibilities towards their children.The complainant has disputed the alleged portrayal of his professional life, stating that he sacrificed his own career and professional pursuits to support Komâs boxing career before and during their marriage. The complaint says this account contradicts the alleged assertion that he had no career and had never been gainfully employed.Describing Kom as an internationally renowned boxing champion with a substantial public following, the complaint argues that the broadcast carried the potential to harm his standing as a spouse and parent.Onkholer has approached the court through advocates Akash Krishna and Pragati Sharma. The complaint invokes Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with defamation.The allegations are part of a pending complaint and have not been established in court. The next hearing on November 19 is expected to determine the subsequent course of the proceedings as the court considers the matter at the pre-summoning evidence stage.

World.title: 'Women police personnel molested': Centre's charge puts Rahul Gandhi-led protest in focus
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Friday defended the security measures and restrictions imposed in Delhi ahead of the Cockroach Janta Partyâs planned protest on October 10, telling the Supreme Court that the steps were necessary to ensure the safety of residents.

However, the court expressed concern over the disruption to public transport, cautioning authorities against going overboard in the name of security.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, argued that law enforcement agencies had to take preventive measures in view of the planned demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Referring to recent protests in the national capital, Centre alleged that "women police personnel had been molested, attacked and injured," over the last few days.

The submission brought Congress leader Rahul Gandhi into the spotlight once again, after the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party accused the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha of behaving âinappropriatelyâ with a woman police officer during a protest a day earlier.

BJP leader Kesavan had criticised Rahul over the alleged incident, asking, âHow can any decent individual, let alone a member of parliament or a leader of the opposition, behave in such an inappropriate manner with a woman, and that too, a female police personnel?â

However, the top court questioned the extent of the restrictions imposed in the capital, particularly the proposed closure of Metro stations and disruption to railway services ahead of Saturdayâs protest.





âExercise caution, there's nothing wrong with that. Police are responsible for maintaining law and order,â the court observed on the security arrangements for the October 10 demonstration.

Taking up the issue of Metro station closures, the court cautioned that security measures should not bring daily life to a standstill.

World.title: 'Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai': Delhi Police issues 'open letter' to protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has issued an open letter to citizens, emphasising that protecting their safety is its responsibility and that police personnel, despite wearing uniforms, are human beings with families and loved ones.

"Dear citizen, Aapki awaaz aapka haq hai, aur aapki surakhsha hamara farz. Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai, jiska aapna Parivar hai, apne log hai. Farq sirf uniform ka hai, insaaniyat ka nahi," the letter read.

(Your voice is your right, and your safety is our duty. Behind the uniform is also a human being, who has a family and loved ones. The only difference is the uniform, not humanity).

The open letter comes amid heightened tensions over protests in the national capital after the Delhi Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Partyâs (CJP) proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10.

The police cited the late submission of its application, non-compliance with rules during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order, and traffic management.

Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the New Delhi district police received an application from CJP co-convenor Saurabh Das on October 7, seeking permission to hold a protest demanding accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.





âOn October 7, 2026, an application from Saurabh Das, Co-Convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party, was received in the New Delhi District. As per the application, an intimation was given regarding a protest to be held at Jantar Mantar on October 10 concerning the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). Upon processing this intimation, it was found that the notice was received at very short notice. Under current guidelines, an application to organise an event at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the scheduled date,â Prasad said.

Meanwhile, Delhi Police on Monday issued an advisory for journalists covering protests, asking them to carry valid identity cards issued by their respective organisations or PIB/DIP accreditation cards and keep them visibly displayed to facilitate identification by law enforcement personnel.

Three Saudi nationals were killed and several others injured in two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a Saudia Airlines aircraft on Thursday, Saudi Arabiaâs general authority of civil aviation said on Friday.The first attack targeted airport facilities, while the second struck the aircraft, the authority said. It did not identify those responsible, although Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen claimed to have targeted the airport, as cited by AP.Saudia Airlines has confirmed that a pilot was killed and an aircraft was damaged in the attack.Operations at King Khalid International Airport have since resumed, with air traffic returning to normal, according to the civil aviation authority.The attacks come amid a heightened security situation in Saudi Arabia following separate strikes on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport on October 6 and 7. Those attacks left three people dead and 36 injured, according to the authority. Two people were killed and 28 injured at Abha airport, while one person was killed and eight injured at King Khalid International Airport.Saudi Civil Defence personnel responded to Thursdayâs incident after a missile was launched by the Houthi militia, the Saudi Civil Defence said.Following the attacks on civilian facilities, Saudi-led coalition forces said they had destroyed 82 military targets belonging to the Houthi militia in Yemen.Amid the security situation, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh on Thursday advised Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain vigilant, stay indoors when necessary and follow instructions issued by local authorities through official channels.âIn view of the current situation, all Indian nationals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia are advised to remain alert and vigilant, stay indoors as necessary, and follow the instructions issued by local authorities through official channels. Indian nationals are strongly advised to refrain from circulating or reposting any videos or news related to the ongoing events," the embassy said in an advisory.The mission said the Embassy of India in Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah, including their outsourced services through VFS, continued to operate normally and would issue further updates as required."The Embassy of India, Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah and its outsourced services through VFS, are continuing to function normally and will issue updates and advisories as and when necessary. World.title: Fabrication units in Tiruchi complain of difficulties in sourcing raw materials
World.content:
At a time when public sector major, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, has been giving out a large volume of orders to its vendors in Tiruchi, the sub-contractors are complaining of difficulties in sourcing raw material, especially steel plates, and fluctuations in the price of raw material.

Fabrication units, which form the backbone of the MSME sector in Tiruchi, say they are facing short supply of raw materials, particularly steel plates of heavy-thickness and other critical materials.

“Sourcing raw material now is very challenging. Functional units are operating over and above their capacities. But some of the private steel manufacturers are seeking 100% payment advance, though SAIL accepts an advance and full payment on delivery,” said P. Senthil Kumar, chairman, BRAMAS Industrial Service Association, which consolidates requirements of raw materials such as plates and structurals and procures them for member units from steel mills.

The contractual delivery period for the vendors is typically in the range of four to five months. But steel plants frequently supply the material only after about four months. For the sub contractors, any delay in delivery of orders leads to punitive liquidated damages and have to bear substantial losses due to circumstances beyond their control, he said.

Expressing concern over the situation, the Tamil Nadu Boilers and Boiler Components Manufacturers Association has called for the intervention of the Union Minister for Heavy Industries. “MSME vendors are facing serious difficulties, particularly with regard to the availability and pricing of raw materials. During the last three months, prices of raw materials have increased sharply. These issues are affecting the smooth functioning and financial stability of MSME units in and around Tiruchi,” said Rajappa Rajkumar, Treasurer, of the association, in an appeal to the Minister.

Significantly, the problem has arisen at a time when the MSMEs have secured good volume of orders from BHEL, which has a healthy order book. “BHEL, Tiruchi, has placed orders aggregating to about 90,000 tonnes, and a large number of MSME vendors are finding it extremely difficult to get the required materials within the stipulated time,” Mr. Rajkumar said.

“Fabrication units in Tiruchi are already facing a geographical disadvantage. Being located in the south, we have to source the raw material from central India and transport the fabricated components to other parts of the country again. Tenders floated by BHEL are pan-India tenders with the same price and almost all project-site locations are in the northern part of India and the contract scope includes transportation to the site,” said Mr. Senthil Kumar, pressing for treating transportation as a separate extra rate schedule, payable on actuals, so that evaluation was location-neutral.

“We could not be competitive due to this and other issues. From what was once a thriving industry with over 400 units, we have already been reduced to just about 60-70 active units. Even these will vanish if the raw material is not available on time,” he said.

Mr. Rajkumar said the problem in getting raw materials could affect the delivery schedules of not only the MSME vendors but ultimately that of BHEL to its customers. MSME units are already operating under severe financial constraints and Mr. Rajkumar contended and urged the Minister to take up the matter with steel manufacturers, including SAIL, and ensure adequate and timely availability of the raw material to the MSME units in Tiruchi.

World.title: West Bengal bypolls: BJP retains Nandigram with record margin, wins Muslim-dominated Rejinagar
World.content:
The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Friday (October 9, 2026) won both Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly seats in West Bengal by a huge margin in the byelection that was held on October 6. In Nandigram Assembly seat located in Purba Medinipur district, BJP candidate Hasi Rani Rath won by a record margin of over 1.22 lakh votes. The margin of victory for BJP candidate Shankharavh Sarkar at Rejinagar in Murshidabad district was over 75,000 votes.

While it has been a tradition of the party in power in West Bengal to win bypolls, the significance of this victory is that a majority of Muslim electorate voted for the BJP both in Rejinagar and Nandigram. About 70% of the electorate in Rejinagar come from the minority community while 27% voters in Nandigram are Muslims.

Also Read : Bypoll results LIVE

With the results, the number of seats of the BJP in the State Assembly have increased to 209. There are a total of 294 seats in the House.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who had urged Muslims to vote for the BJP in the bypolls, thanked minority voters of both Nandigram and Rejinagar. He said the BJP received support of 80% Muslims in Nandigram and that over 60% Muslim electorate voted for BJP in Rejinagar.

Muslims backing govt.: CM

“The Muslims have voted for us because they want to stand with the government. Muslims were told that they will be put in detention centres and they will not be allowed to practice their religion, all of this have turned out to be false in the past five months. This is the reason why they (Muslims) have voted for us,” Mr. Adhikari told media persons at the State Secretariat.

The Chief Minister expressed hope that Bengali Muslims will support the BJP in the future and the party which registered 46% votes in the recent Assembly polls will get support of 60% of the electorate.

Mr. Adhikari said that even in the previous regimes led by the Congress, Left Front and Trinamool Congress, Bengali-speaking Muslims have supported the party in power. He also expressed hope that Muslims will continue to support the BJP in future, including upcoming civic polls in the State.

Congress candidate Milan Pradhan emerged as the runner-up in Nandigram securing 41,674 votes. In Rejinagar, Aam Janata Unnayan Party candidate Golam Nabi Azad secured second position by tallying 54,098 votes. The byelections to Nandigram and Rejinagar were held amidst allegations of the Opposition not being allowed to campaign. The Congress nominee from Nandigram was arrested by the police and could campaign for only four days after the Calcutta High Court granted him conditional bail. Opposition candidates in Rejinagar also alleged that they were not allowed to campaign freely.

The bypolls in Nandigram were necessitated after getting elected from Bhabanipur and Nandigram, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari decided to retain Bhabanipur and resigned from Nandigram. AJUP leader Humayun Kabir was elected from Naoda and Rejinagar and he decided to resign from Rejinagar resulting in the bypoll.
